#### T-1A.5-M04-01 · Context-priced offers (API-M04-03) and public price in search/listing projections; private prices never indexed or shared-cached
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.5 / M04
- **Depends on:** T-1A.5-M05-02, T-1A.4-M21-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 06 §4.1 API-M04-03, §1.11; 05 BR-M02-13; 16 TS-API-07, TS-PERM-05, TS-SVC-09; BP §8.4, §16.5; T02, T22
- **Description:** Implement context-priced offers API-M04-03 per 06-api §4.1 and add public prices to the search and listing projections. API-M04-03 returns only approved, published offers of a published product, priced by PricingEngine for the caller's server-derived context (guest/consumer → public list; dealer and contract prices only for a verified member of an approved business account, completed in T-1A.8-M08-06), with tax basis (D-016), tiers only for dealers, condition, explicit warranty provider and policy versions, and an empty list (not an error) when no offer exists for the context; responses are `private, no-store` whenever the context is not public (BR-M02-13, BR-M05-08, BR-M05-15, BR-M05-16; T02, T22) and client-sent segment/price fields are ignored (T10). Availability fields are added by the A04 projection (T-1A.6-M06-03) and delivery estimates by T-1A.9-M12-01; reference price and savings only per D-166. In search, the public price (public list and its tax basis) is indexed for API-M21-01 results, price sorts and price filters and as the public hint of API-M21-02; dealer prices and tier hints are computed per request for verified dealers and never written into shared projections (BR-M21-06; 06-api §1.11). Not part of this task: dealer price-list view API-M05-04 (T-1A.8-M08-06), quotes (T-1A.9-M05-01), storefront rendering (T-1A.9-M09-05, T-1A.9-M09-06), cache invalidation mechanism (T-1A.9-M09-04, D-105).
- **Files/components:** `backend/catalog/` offers query (CatalogQueryService with PricingEngine) and `backend/search/` projection/indexer changes (finer structure per D-001/D-032); API and cache-header tests.
- **Database impact:** None new; reads E-offer, E-sku and DB-G3 pricing entities; search projection gains the public price fields (storage per D-032).
- **API impact:** Implements API-M04-03; extends API-M21-01 (public price, price sort/filter, dealer tier hints resolved privately) and API-M21-02 (public price hint).
- **Frontend impact:** None (consumed by P-S02, P-S03, P-S04, P-S06 in 1A.9).
- **Backend impact:** CatalogQueryService offers, PricingEngine, SearchIndexer, SearchService, SuggestionService; BR-M02-13, BR-M05-08, BR-M05-15, BR-M05-16, BR-M21-06.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-API-07 — context-dependent responses carry `private, no-store` and public ones are cacheable; TS-PERM-05 — case 05.1 (guest with forged parameters gets only public prices from offers, search and suggestions) and case 05.2 API part (after dealer sign-out the same client receives no private price); TS-API-10 — every field of 06-api §1.4 ignored on API-M04-03; TS-SVC-09 — no private price appears in any shared projection; TS-API-01 for API-M04-03; T02 and T22 at API level.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A guest or consumer calling API-M04-03 receives only public prices with the D-016 tax basis; forged segment, `dealer_approved` or price fields change nothing (TS-API-10, TS-PERM-05.1 pass).
   2. A verified dealer context (test fixture until T-1A.8-M08-06) receives dealer or contract prices and tiers, and that response is `private, no-store` (TS-API-07 passes).
   3. Only approved offers of published products are returned; a product without an offer for the context returns `offers: []`.
   4. Search results and suggestions show the public price only; dealer prices and tier hints are computed per request and never stored in the shared projection (TS-SVC-09 private-price case passes).
   5. Price sorting and price filtering in API-M21-01 use the caller's context price without exposing private prices to other callers.
   6. After a dealer signs out, the next request from the same client returns public prices only (T22 API part).
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.5-M05-03 · Price-list administration: lists, change requests shown as diff with approval, tier editor data, read-only simulation (API-M05-10…16)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.5 / M05
- **Depends on:** T-1A.5-M05-02, T-1A.2-M17-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 05 BR-M05-17; 10 §4; 11 §9.3; 06 API-M05-10…16; 16 TS-ERP-16, TS-API-04; BP §8.4, §18.1
- **Description:** Implement price-list administration in PriceListService, PriceChangeService and PriceSimulator (05 §5.5; 10 §4; 11 §9.3): list and detail of price lists with validity, fallback, assigned accounts, version history and expiry/successor state (API-M05-10, API-M05-11); creation of a draft list with basis, validity, mandatory fallback and reason (API-M05-12; the location type answers FEATURE_DISABLED unless D-044 is approved — T-1A.5-M05-06); change requests for lines, tiers, header changes or "duplicate as draft" with reason and `expected_version` that create a draft/pending E-price_rule_version and an approval request and return 202 while the live list stays unchanged (API-M05-13; BR-M05-17); the pending change as a diff with header diff, line changes with increase/decrease/floor-breach filters and impact (API-M05-14); tier-editor data per SKU × list with cost and floor figures only for roles allowed under D-197 (API-M05-15); and the read-only simulation through the live engine with its step trace, authority and margin checks and no side effects (API-M05-16). Approval decisions come through API-M17-03; activation on approval switches the active version atomically at its effective date (TX-10) and locked quotes keep their price (BP §8.1 step 7). The price-list editor cannot approve the same change (SoD-4; BR-M02-06); a dealer tier/list change follows staff request → manager within delegated policy → owner (BP §18.1, §12.6). Not part of this task: the P-E07 screens (T-1A.5-M05-08), promotions (T-1A.5-M05-04), margin floors and override requests (T-1A.5-M05-05), cost signals (T-1A.7-M05-01), assigning a list to a business account (API-M08-36, T-1A.8-M08-07).
- **Files/components:** `backend/pricing/` — PriceListService, PriceChangeService, PriceSimulator, API tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-price_list, E-price_rule_version (draft/pending/active transitions), E-price_list_item, E-quantity_tier, E-approval_request, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M05-10, API-M05-11, API-M05-12, API-M05-13, API-M05-14, API-M05-15, API-M05-16; consumes API-M17-03 (decision) through the approval core.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E07 in T-1A.5-M05-08).
- **Backend impact:** PriceListService, PriceChangeService, PriceSimulator; BR-M05-09, BR-M05-14, BR-M05-17, BR-M02-06; TX-10 activation; approval routing by ApprovalService with thresholds from D-024.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-16 — change request shown as a diff, live list unchanged until approval, activation on approval at the effective date; TS-API-04 — stale `expected_version` on API-M05-13 returns 409; TS-PERM-08.1 — the requester of a price change cannot approve it; TS-UNIT-01 — simulation result equals the engine result for the same inputs; TS-API-01 for the seven endpoints; TS-SVC-03 — activation and change requests audited with reason.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A change request returns 202 with an approval reference, and the live list keeps pricing until the approved version becomes active on its effective date.
   2. Approval activates the new version atomically and supersedes the previous one; a quote locked before activation keeps its price.
   3. The requester of a change cannot approve it (403 SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED) and a stale `expected_version` returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT.
   4. The diff endpoint shows header and line changes with the increase, decrease and floor-breach filters; cost and margin figures appear only for roles allowed under D-197.
   5. Creating a list without a fallback is refused; a location list is refused with FEATURE_DISABLED unless D-044 approved it.
   6. The simulator returns the same price and step trace as the engine and creates no quote, reservation or record.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.5-M05-04 · Promotions, stacking policy and coupon codes with P-E07 #promotions (CONDITIONAL; E-promotion, E-promotion_code)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.5 / M05
- **Depends on:** T-1A.5-M05-02, T-1A.3-M24-01
- **Decisions:** D-043, D-004
- **References:** 08 §4.28; 04b §10.5; 06 API-M05-17…19, API-M05-24; 03 §2.4.5, §2.21.18; 16 TS-ECOM-14, TS-UNIT-01; BP §8.1 step 4; PR1 §8
- **Description:** CONDITIONAL — built only if D-043 approves promotions/coupons (BP §8.1 step 4; PR1 §8 "subject to confirmed scope"; 12 §1.3); when disabled the promotion APIs answer FEATURE_DISABLED, the engine skips step 4 and P-E07 `#promotions` and the storefront coupon field are hidden (TS-ECOM-14). This task migrates E-promotion and E-promotion_code (DB-G3 conditional entities; `redeemed_order_id` is added with DB-G7) and implements PromotionService: promotions list with the active stacking policy, coupon validation failures of the last 24 hours and budget/usage controls (API-M05-17), promotion drafts that need approval before going live (API-M05-18), single-use code batches (API-M05-19), and pause/resume/end of live or scheduled promotions with reason (API-M05-24). The engine's step 4 applies only eligible promotions under the explicit stacking policy of the active `pricing_policy` version (D-017), never the largest discount by default, with the explanation returned per line (BR-M05-05, BR-M05-07; BP §8.4 "promotion plus dealer discount"); allocations per order line are kept for refunds (BR-M05-13); invalid, expired, ineligible or exhausted codes return COUPON_INVALID and code guessing is rate-limited (D-084). Promotion types, eligibility and whether promotions combine with dealer prices are decided in D-043; bank/UPI payment offers are MOCKUP-ONLY (D-062) and bundle promotions depend on D-072 — neither is built here. The P-E07 `#promotions` tab (04b §10.5, incl. the new-promotion form not drawn in the mockup) is built here as a custom screen if D-004 so decides.
- **Files/components:** `backend/pricing/` — E-promotion and E-promotion_code migrations, PromotionService, stacking evaluation tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002); `frontend/workspace/screens/` P-E07 `#promotions` tab if D-004 = custom (finer structure per D-101); feature flag via the configuration service.
- **Database impact:** Creates E-promotion and E-promotion_code (DB-G3, CONDITIONAL D-043); promotion versions recorded in E-price_rule_version (rule_type promotion); approval requests for drafts.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M05-17, API-M05-18, API-M05-19, API-M05-24; extends the engine used by API-M05-01 (coupon_codes, from T-1A.9-M05-01) and API-M05-16.
- **Frontend impact:** P-E07 `#promotions` (toolbar, table, stacking-policy panel, validation failures, budget controls, new-promotion form, code generation) if D-004 = custom.
- **Backend impact:** PromotionService, PricingEngine step 4; BR-M05-05, BR-M05-07, BR-M05-13; approval via ApprovalService; rate limits per D-084.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-14 — disabled: FEATURE_DISABLED and hidden UI; enabled: cases below; TS-UNIT-01 stacking cases — only eligible promotions, exclusive conflicts resolved by priority not by size, consumer promotions not applied to dealer lists if D-043 so decides, allocation per line; TS-ERP-16 promotions part — draft needs approval, pause/resume/end audited; TS-FE-03 for the tab; TS-DB-02 — code uniqueness, single-use code redeemed once.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. With D-043 not approving promotions, every promotion endpoint answers FEATURE_DISABLED, the migration is not applied and no promotion UI is shown.
   2. With promotions enabled, a promotion goes live only after approval, and pause, resume and end require a reason and are audited.
   3. The engine applies only eligible promotions under the active stacking policy and explains each applied discount per line; when two exclusive promotions conflict, the higher-priority rule wins, not the larger discount.
   4. Single-use codes are unique and redeem once per confirmed order; invalid, expired, ineligible or exhausted codes return COUPON_INVALID.
   5. Promotion allocations are stored per line so that refunds can reuse them (BR-M05-13 test with a partial refund fixture).
   6. Payment-offer and bundle promotion types are not offered unless D-062 or D-072 approve them.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.5-M05-05 · Margin floors, discount authority and override requests (API-M05-20, API-M05-21)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.5 / M05
- **Depends on:** T-1A.5-M05-02, T-1A.2-M17-01
- **Decisions:** D-135, D-197
- **References:** 05 §5.5; 07 §7, §9; 06 API-M05-20, API-M05-21; 16 TS-ERP-16, TS-PERM-09, TS-PERM-10; BP §8.4, §18.1
- **Description:** Implement margin floors, discount authority and override requests in MarginAuthorityService (05 §5.5; 07 §7, §9; BP §8.4, §18.1): the controls view with margin floors by scope, the authority matrix by role from E-discount_authority and open override requests (API-M05-20), margin-floor change requests versioned as E-price_rule_version (rule_type margin_floor) and approved by the owner (API-M05-21), and the engine step-6 check that returns `margin_check` and `authority_check` and, when a price falls below the applicable floor or a discount exceeds the caller's authority, creates a `margin_override` or `discount_override` approval request with the mandatory reason instead of executing (202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED; BR-M05-10, BR-M05-20; A07). Decisions are made through API-M17-03 by an approver other than the requester (SoD-1). Floor rates and authority limits are client-supplied under D-024 and loaded as thresholds in T-1A.14-M17-07 — until then records stay draft and tests use fixture thresholds (07 §9; 16 P8); the cost used for margin follows the valuation method of D-135, and which roles see cost and margin columns follows D-197 (columns omitted, not blanked). Not part of this task: the P-E07 `#controls` screen (T-1A.5-M05-08), threshold administration (T-1A.14-M17-07), assisted-order discount entry (T-1A.13-M10-01), the margin-leakage flag A36 (T-1B.4-M05-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/pricing/` — MarginAuthorityService, floor-change requests, tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-margin_floor versions via E-price_rule_version, reads E-discount_authority; creates E-approval_request (margin_override, discount_override); E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M05-20 and API-M05-21; consumes API-M17-03 through the approval core.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E07 `#controls` in T-1A.5-M05-08).
- **Backend impact:** MarginAuthorityService, PricingEngine step 6; BR-M05-10, BR-M05-20, BR-M02-06; automation A07; cost basis per D-135; visibility per D-197.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-16 — below-floor price routes to an override with reason; TS-PERM-09 — case 09.1 within vs above fixture thresholds, case 09.2 request-only roles; TS-PERM-10 — case 10.3 cost/margin columns absent for roles not allowed under D-197; TS-PERM-08.1 — requester cannot approve own override; TS-API-01 for API-M05-20 and API-M05-21.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A calculation below the applicable margin floor returns an approval-required result with an override request carrying the reason; nothing is priced below the floor without an approved override.
   2. A discount within the caller's authority (fixture thresholds) executes; above it, an approval request is created (TS-PERM-09.1 passes).
   3. Margin-floor changes are created as versions requiring owner approval and take effect only after approval.
   4. Placeholder thresholds are never active: until D-024 values are loaded, floor and authority records stay draft.
   5. Cost and margin fields are returned only to roles allowed under D-197, using the D-135 cost basis.
   6. The requester of an override cannot decide it.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.6-M06-01 · DB-G4 schema (E-stock_position, E-stock_movement, E-serial_unit, E-serial_event, E-inspection, E-transfer, E-transfer_line, E-stock_count, E-stock_count_line, E-stock_adjustment, E-supplier_availability, E-reorder_rule; E-lot by T-1A.6-M06-09)

- **Description:** Create the DB-G4 (Inventory & serials) migrations of 03 §4 on the selected core, recording native-versus-extension mapping per D-001 (e.g. stock ledger, bin and serial candidates named in 03 §2.5): E-stock_position (unique key SKU × location × bin × disposition × stock owner × lot, quantity ≥ 0, `last_movement_id`/`as_of` as version marker), E-stock_movement (append-only; the movement types and disposition rules of 03 §5.3; source document, actor, reason and approval references), E-serial_unit (unique internal serial number, separately stored and indexed manufacturer serial, lifecycle status, refurbished-unit fields of BR-M06-22, replacement links), E-serial_event (append-only), E-inspection, E-transfer and E-transfer_line (from ≠ to; shipped/received quantities), E-stock_count and E-stock_count_line, E-stock_adjustment (non-zero signed delta, reason, approval and posted-movement references), E-supplier_availability (created now, used from 1B.2) and E-reorder_rule (unique SKU × location), with the dispositions of 03 §2.5 (receiving_inspection, sellable, quarantine, damaged, repair, in_transit; further states only per D-139). The stock-owner dimension follows D-128 (company-owned at launch unless consignment is decided). Not part of this task: E-lot (T-1A.6-M06-09, D-126), E-reservation (DB-G7, T-1A.9-M10-01), seeds S-13/S-14 (T-1A.6-M06-10), services (T-1A.6-M06-02 onwards).

#### T-1A.6-M06-02 · Stock ledger, positions and ATP: append-only movements per BP §9.2 event table, dispositions, position maintenance, ATP formula, ledger/position reconciliation (API-M06-03, API-M06-04, API-M06-11)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M06
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 05 §5.6 BR-M06-*; 10 §5; 03 §5.2, §5.3; 06 API-M06-03, API-M06-04, API-M06-11; 16 TS-ERP-02, TS-UNIT-05, TS-DB-03, TS-DB-04, TS-DB-07; BP §9.1, §9.2, §17.6
- **Description:** Implement StockLedger and AtpCalculator as the single stock authority (BP §9.1, §9.2, §17.6; 05 §5.6; 10 §5): every stock-affecting operation posts append-only E-stock_movement rows with the movement types and disposition effects of 03 §5.3 (the BP §9.2 event table), each carrying source document, actor, reason and approval where required, and updates E-stock_position in the same transaction; positions are never written directly and discrepancies are corrected only by reversal or approved adjustment (BR-M06-03, BR-M06-04); frozen bins reject movements (BR-M03-03). ATP per SKU × location × stock owner (× lot if D-126) is `max(0, sellable_on_hand − active_reserved − safety_buffer)`, where sellable already excludes quarantine, damaged, repair and in-transit and is never reduced twice, open POs and supplier availability never count, the safety buffer is read from the D-027 configuration, and active reservations count once reservations exist (T-1A.9-M06-01) (BR-M06-02). It implements the staff stock views API-M06-03 (enterprise stock by SKU with sellable, reserved, buffer, ATP, quarantine, in-transit and reorder point, filters, location scope; the `web_projection` column is filled by T-1A.6-M06-03) and API-M06-04 (per-location/bin breakdown), and the ledger read API-M06-11; results are intersected with the caller's location scope and cross-branch read follows D-029 (BR-M02-04). A nightly ledger-vs-position reconciliation job proves Σ movements = positions and raises a `stock_mismatch` exception through the exception core on drift (I-04). If the stock authority is unavailable, confirmations stop rather than guess (BR-M06-17). Not part of this task: the availability projection (T-1A.6-M06-03), serial, inspection, transfer and count services (T-1A.6-M06-04…T-1A.6-M06-08), reservations (T-1A.9-M06-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` — StockLedger, AtpCalculator, reconciliation job, API handlers, unit/property tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-stock_movement and E-stock_position; reads E-configuration_version (`safety_buffer.policy`) and E-location_bin state; creates E-exception_case (`stock_mismatch`). No schema change.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M06-03, API-M06-04, API-M06-11.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E08 `#stock` and `#movements` in T-1A.6-M06-11; P-E06 ATP column).
- **Backend impact:** StockLedger, AtpCalculator; BR-M06-01, BR-M06-02, BR-M06-03, BR-M06-04, BR-M06-17, BR-M03-03; nightly reconciliation job on the job runtime; exceptions via ExceptionService (T-1A.2-M17-02).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-02 — every BP §9.2 stock-event row produces the documented movement and effect, no quantity overwrite, history reconciles; TS-UNIT-05 ATP part — formula cases incl. zero floor, excluded dispositions never subtracted twice, buffer from configuration fixture; TS-DB-03 — invariants I-02 and I-04 over randomised operation sequences; TS-DB-04 — ledger append-only; TS-DB-07 — Σ movements = positions, zero drift after a load run; TS-PERM-11 — location scope on stock lists (case 11.1); TS-API-01 for API-M06-03, API-M06-04, API-M06-11.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Each BP §9.2 event of 03 §5.3 posts exactly the documented movement and position change; no code path updates a position without a movement (TS-ERP-02 passes).
   2. ATP equals `max(0, sellable − reserved − buffer)` for every test case; quarantine, damaged, repair and in-transit quantities never reduce ATP a second time; POs and supplier availability never add to it (TS-UNIT-05 ATP cases pass).
   3. A movement into or out of a frozen bin is rejected.
   4. The reconciliation job reports zero drift on generated histories and raises one `stock_mismatch` exception when drift is injected (TS-DB-07 passes).
   5. Stock and ledger lists return only locations in the caller's scope (cross-branch read per D-029) and show reserved and in-transit quantities separately.
   6. Movements cannot be updated or deleted; corrections appear as reversal or adjustment movements with reason.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.6-M06-03 · Availability projector A04: committed stock events refresh listing/PDP/search availability, lag metric, periodic reconciliation
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M06
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-02, T-1A.4-M21-01, T-1A.1-M17-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 05 §4 A04, §5.6; 02 §16; 16 TS-SVC-09, TS-PERF-03, TS-PROOF-08; BP §16.5, §20.1; A18
- **Description:** Implement AvailabilityProjector (A04) and the shared authorised stock view (A18) (05 §4, §5.6; 02 §16; BP §16.5, §20.1): committed stock movements write outbox events that recompute ATP for the affected SKU × location × owner and refresh the availability projection consumed by the offers API (availability message, source and `as_of` in API-M04-03), search results and the in-stock filter (API-M21-01 `stock_message`), the P-E06 ATP column and the `web_projection{value, as_of}` column of API-M06-03; the projection carries version/timestamp so stale data is detectable (BR-M06-18, BR-M21-03), "Only N left" wording is produced only from real ATP (BR-M04-18), and checkout always revalidates with the authority. A timestamped movement-to-display lag metric is emitted for monitoring (BP §20.3; target proposed in D-034), and a periodic reconciliation compares projection and authority, repairs drift and, after the retry cap, raises one actionable incident (A38 via the exception core). The shared stock view distinguishes reserved and in-transit quantities for branch users within the D-029 visibility rule (A18). This task is the projection part of proof scenario 8 (recover a failed stock-update job and reconcile the channel view). Not part of this task: supplier/partner availability and freshness (T-1B.2-M06-01), the cache invalidation mechanism of the storefront (T-1A.9-M09-04, D-105), reservation effects (T-1A.9-M06-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` — AvailabilityProjector, projection reconciliation job; `backend/search/` projection consumer (finer structure per D-001/D-032); lag metric in `backend/platform/observability/`.
- **Database impact:** Uses E-outbox_operation and E-job_attempt; projection storage per D-032/D-105 (search/offer projection fields); E-exception_case for persistent failures. No new entity.
- **API impact:** Extends API-M04-03 (availability), API-M21-01 (stock message, in-stock filter) and API-M06-03 (`web_projection`).
- **Frontend impact:** None directly (values shown on P-S02/P-S03 in 1A.9 and on P-E06/P-E08).
- **Backend impact:** AvailabilityProjector; automations A04 and A18; BR-M06-01, BR-M06-18, BR-M21-03; outbox worker and scanner (T-1A.1-M17-01); exception creation per A38 (T-1A.2-M17-02).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SVC-09 — an approved/committed change refreshes projections with version/timestamp and a stale projection is detectable; TS-PERF-03 baseline — timestamped movement-to-display propagation measured; TS-PROOF-08 projection part — kill the worker after a movement commit, the scanner and reconciliation restore the channel view with no duplicate effect; TS-SVC-02 — outbox recovery cases for the projection job; TS-PERM-11 — shared view respects the D-029 rule.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A committed movement changes the projected availability of the affected SKU/location with a newer version/timestamp; stale projections are detectable by `as_of` (TS-SVC-09 passes).
   2. The movement-to-display lag is measured and recorded as the TS-PERF-03 baseline against the D-034 proposal.
   3. After a forced worker crash, the scanner/reconciliation restores the projection without duplicate processing and records exactly one incident if the retry cap is exceeded (TS-PROOF-08 projection part passes).
   4. "Only N left" and "In stock" texts are derived solely from real ATP; supplier availability is never included.
   5. Branch users see company-wide availability read-only with reserved and in-transit shown separately, within the D-029 rule.
   6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.6-M06-04 · Serial units and lifecycle: internal vs manufacturer serial, duplicate check, scan/type lookup, unit actions, serial events (API-M06-05…08)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M06
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-02
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 05 §5.6; 10 §5; 03 §2.5.4, §2.5.5; 06 API-M06-05…08; 16 TS-ERP-03; BP §9.4
- **Description:** Implement SerialUnitService (BP §9.4, §7.2, §7.5; 05 §5.6; 10 §5): serialised units with an internal tracking serial separate from the manufacturer serial (BR-M06-09), the refurbished-unit record fields of BR-M06-22 (purchase source, grade, latest inspection, warranty policy version, erasure evidence, accessories, defects, replaced components, keyboard layout, OS licence status, lifecycle status), append-only serial events for every lifecycle step, and a duplicate-manufacturer-serial check that holds the new unit out of sellable stock and raises a `duplicate_serial` exception instead of a hard constraint (BP §9.4; T15 basis). APIs: unit list and quarantine view with disposition, location, source and days-in-state filters (API-M06-05); scan/type lookup by internal ID, manufacturer serial or order number with a duplicate warning (API-M06-06; order-number matches once orders exist); unit record with masked manufacturer serial, inspection history and lifecycle (API-M06-07); unit actions with mandatory reason (API-M06-08): re-grade (requires a new inspection, T-1A.6-M06-05), send to repair (disposition change movement), open discrepancy case, and return to supplier, which creates the supplier-RMA draft only once the supplier-RMA service exists (T-1A.12-M13-06). Repair replacement keeps both units' histories and recall queries find affected units and orders (BR-M06-21). A unit can never be on two active fulfilments or ship twice (BR-M06-08) — enforced here by lifecycle guards and completed with reservations/fulfilment in 1A.9/1A.11. Manufacturer serials are masked by default; reveal is T-1A.8-M02-01. Not part of this task: inspections (T-1A.6-M06-05), serial capture at receipt (T-1A.7-M07-05), P-E08 `#serials` (T-1A.6-M06-11).
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` — SerialUnitService, duplicate check, lifecycle guards, API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-serial_unit, E-serial_event, E-stock_movement (disposition changes), E-exception_case (`duplicate_serial`, discrepancy), E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M06-05, API-M06-06, API-M06-07, API-M06-08.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E08 `#serials` in T-1A.6-M06-11; P-E04 quarantine queue in T-1A.12-M13-08).
- **Backend impact:** SerialUnitService; BR-M06-08, BR-M06-09, BR-M06-21, BR-M06-22; exceptions via ExceptionService.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-03 — duplicate serial check, manufacturer vs internal identifier, lifecycle events, replacement history, recall query (batch recall per D-126); TS-DB-04 — serial events append-only; TS-PERM-10.1 — manufacturer serial masked for staff reading a unit; TS-PERM-02.6 — unit of another location answers 404; TS-API-01 for the four endpoints.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Internal serial numbers are unique; a manufacturer serial already present on another unit holds the new unit out of sellable stock and raises one `duplicate_serial` exception (TS-ERP-03 duplicate case passes).
   2. Lookup finds a unit by internal ID or manufacturer serial and returns the duplicate warning when applicable.
   3. The unit record shows a masked manufacturer serial and a complete lifecycle with reference and actor for each event.
   4. Unit actions require a reason; re-grade leaves the unit non-sellable until a new inspection is recorded; send-to-repair posts a disposition-change movement.
   5. A repair replacement keeps both histories linked and a recall query returns the affected units and their orders.
   6. Staff outside the unit's location scope receive 404.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.6-M06-05 · Inspections and condition grading for units (receipt QC, return inspection), public unit inspection report and staff inspection document (API-M06-09, API-M06-02, API-M06-31; E-inspection)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M06
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-04, T-1A.4-M04-02
- **Decisions:** D-023
- **References:** 08 §4.6; 10 §5; 03 §2.5.6; 06 API-M06-09, API-M06-02; 16 TS-ECOM-02; BP §6.6, §9.3; T01
- **Description:** Implement InspectionService and the unit inspection documents (BP §6.6, §7.2, §9.2, §9.3; 08 §4.6; 10 §5): record an inspection/QC result (API-M06-09, idempotent) for serialised units or a batch of a non-serialised receipt line, in the contexts inbound QC, customer return and re-grade, against an active checklist version (`inspection_checklist.<category>`, content per D-023) with per-check results, grade outcome, defects, accessories, battery and OS-licence details, actual-unit photos (stored as media owned by the serial unit with rights recorded) and outcome pass/fail; the assigned inspector records it (scope assigned). Stock effects follow 03 §5.3: inbound QC pass → `qc_accept` to sellable, fail → `qc_reject` to quarantine (BR-M07-04); re-grade → `regrade` movement to the SKU of the new grade; a customer-return inspection only records a recommended disposition because resale is a separate decision (BP §10.5, T-1A.12-M13-03). It provides the public unit inspection report for listed or sold units (API-M06-02: internal unit reference, masked manufacturer serial, grade, checklist results, defects, replaced components, accessories, battery, OS licence, actual photos, inspection date, inspector role, erasure evidence, warranty; JSON or PDF per D-111; public history wording per D-165) and the staff inspection document with the full checklist (API-M06-31, rendering per D-111). No "like new" or unmeasured claims are generated (BP §6.6). The link from an inspection to a goods-receipt line is added with DB-G5 (T-1A.7-M07-01) and used by receiving (T-1A.7-M07-05). Not part of this task: erasure evidence (T-1A.6-M06-06), return inspections' disposition decisions (T-1A.12-M13-03), P-S03/P-S04 rendering (T-1A.9-M09-06).
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` — InspectionService, public report and staff document builders, tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002); document rendering per D-111.
- **Database impact:** Writes E-inspection, E-serial_unit (`latest_inspection_id`, grade), E-serial_event, E-stock_movement, E-media_asset (unit photos), E-attachment, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M06-09, API-M06-02, API-M06-31.
- **Frontend impact:** None directly (P-E09 `#receive` QC, P-E04 inspection tab, P-E08 re-grade and "Full checklist", P-S03 `#inspection` consume these later).
- **Backend impact:** InspectionService; BR-M06-22, BR-M07-04, BR-M04-13; checklist versions from PolicyService; media via MediaImportService.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-02 — unit photos and inspection report, grade rubric described, masked serial, defects and box contents, no implied manufacturer warranty; TS-API-03 — API-M06-09 replay returns the stored result; TS-ERP-02 — QC pass/fail movements; TS-API-01 for API-M06-09, API-M06-02, API-M06-31; T01 unit-report part.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. An inspection can be recorded only against an active checklist version and by the assigned inspector; a replayed request creates no second inspection or movement (TS-API-03 passes).
   2. Inbound QC pass moves the unit to sellable; fail moves it to quarantine; re-grade moves it to the SKU of the new grade; a return inspection changes no disposition.
   3. The public report is available only for units listed or sold publicly, shows the masked manufacturer serial, actual photos and the inspection details, and returns 404 otherwise.
   4. The staff document shows the full checklist results for authorised staff in the unit's location scope.
   5. Photos attached to a unit are recorded with rights and appear only after the unit is published.
   6. T01 unit-report part is demonstrated on staging with a graded refurbished unit.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.6-M06-07 · Transfers: request, ship to in-transit, receive incl. partial and late units, discrepancy/loss with approval (API-M06-12…17)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M06
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-02, T-1A.6-M06-04, T-1A.2-M17-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 05 §5.6; 10 §5, §12; 06 API-M06-12…17; 16 TS-ERP-05; BP §9.5; T16
- **Description:** Implement TransferService for stock transfers (BP §9.5, §9.2; 05 §5.6; 10 §5, §12): list with status and route filters (API-M06-12); create a transfer request as draft or submitted with reason (catalogue D-139), needed-by date and lines whose quantities must not exceed ATP at the source at submission, with approval by value per D-024 returning 202 when required (API-M06-13); detail with per-line shipped, received and in-transit quantities, discrepancies and the enterprise balance check (API-M06-14); transitions submit, ship and cancel (API-M06-15, idempotent, `expected_version`), where shipping posts `transfer_ship` movements from source sellable to destination in-transit atomically with serial scans for serialised SKUs (TX-6); receipt at the destination including late units (API-M06-16, idempotent), posting `transfer_receive` movements from in-transit to sellable for received quantities only (TX-6); and discrepancy handling (API-M06-17): investigate (E-exception_case `transfer_discrepancy`) or record a loss, which creates a stock adjustment request subject to thresholds (D-024). Transfers never create or destroy enterprise stock and in-transit quantities are not available at the destination until received; partial receipts keep in-transit and the discrepancy visible (BR-M06-10; T16). Branch visibility, request and promise rules follow D-029. Not part of this task: customer-order transfer shortcuts on P-E02 and P-E03 (their tasks), P-E08 `#transfers` screen (T-1A.6-M06-11).
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` — TransferService, API handlers, service and property tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-transfer, E-transfer_line, E-stock_movement, E-serial_event, E-exception_case, E-stock_adjustment (loss), E-approval_request, E-idempotency_record, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M06-12, API-M06-13, API-M06-14, API-M06-15, API-M06-16, API-M06-17; consumes API-M17-03 for approvals.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E08 `#transfers` and `m-transfer` in T-1A.6-M06-11).
- **Backend impact:** TransferService, StockLedger, AdjustmentService (loss path); BR-M06-10, BR-M06-11, BR-M06-13; TX-6; approval routing via ApprovalService with D-024 thresholds.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-05 — ship/receive, in-transit not available at the destination, partial receipt keeps the discrepancy visible, enterprise total unchanged; TS-API-03 — replays of API-M06-15 and API-M06-16 return the stored result; TS-API-04 — stale `expected_version` on transitions; TS-SVC-01 — TX-6 atomicity under fault injection; TS-PERM-02.6 — transfer of another location answers 404; T16.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Shipping posts source-to-transit movements atomically; the destination's ATP is unchanged until units are received (TS-ERP-05 passes).
   2. A partial receipt leaves the remaining quantity in transit and a visible discrepancy with an owner; receiving a late unit clears it (T16 passes).
   3. The enterprise total per SKU is identical before and after any transfer sequence (property test).
   4. Submission above available ATP returns 409 STOCK_UNAVAILABLE; value above the D-024 threshold returns 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED and nothing ships until approval.
   5. Recording a loss creates an adjustment request that changes stock only after approval.
   6. Replayed ship/receive requests produce no second movement; a fault inside TX-6 leaves no partial effect.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.6-M06-08 · Counts and adjustments: blind count, bin freeze while counting, recount, variance review A24, adjustment requests with threshold routing (API-M06-18…23, API-M06-32)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M06
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-02, T-1A.2-M17-01
- **Decisions:** D-069
- **References:** 05 §5.6 BR-M06-13; 06 §4.8, API-M06-18…23; 16 TS-ERP-06, TS-PERM-09; BP §9.6, §18.1; A24
- **Description:** Implement CountService (A24) and AdjustmentService (BP §9.6, §18.1; 05 §5.6 BR-M06-12, BR-M06-13; 06-api §4.8): list counts (API-M06-18); start a cycle, full count or recount with location, scope and control mode freeze or reconcile as decided in D-069, a second counter for recounts (API-M06-19); the count sheet with expected quantities hidden from counters when the D-069 policy requires a blind count (API-M06-20); per-bin start that freezes the bin for movements until the count is submitted, `409 BIN_BUSY` otherwise (API-M06-32, idempotent); submission of counted quantities and serials seen, recording time, operator, expected and observed and producing variances with value impact and required approval — without changing stock (API-M06-21, idempotent); the adjustment/variance review queue with value visible only to permitted roles (API-M06-22); and adjustment requests with mandatory reason, server-computed value (valuation per D-135) and threshold routing by quantity and value (D-024) — staff request, managers approve within threshold, large unexplained losses to owner/finance — returning 202 with the approval request (API-M06-23). On approval (API-M17-03 or bulk API-M17-04, each item keeping its own history) the adjustment movement posts with reason and approver (TX-7); would-be negative balances with active reservations are refused or raised as exceptions (I-02). Counts never overwrite quantities; the counter cannot approve the own variance (SoD-10) and requesters never approve their own adjustments. Tolerance auto-accept shown in the mockup applies only if D-024/D-069 decide it; until thresholds are decided, tests use fixtures (16 P8). Not part of this task: threshold administration (T-1A.14-M17-07), P-E08 `#counts` (T-1A.6-M06-11), short-pick recounts from P-E03 (T-1A.11-M12-03).
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` — CountService, AdjustmentService, API handlers, tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-stock_count, E-stock_count_line, E-stock_adjustment, E-location_bin (frozen state), E-stock_movement (on approval), E-approval_request, E-idempotency_record, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M06-18, API-M06-19, API-M06-20, API-M06-21, API-M06-22, API-M06-23, API-M06-32; consumes API-M17-03 and API-M17-04.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E08 `#counts` in T-1A.6-M06-11).
- **Backend impact:** CountService, AdjustmentService, StockLedger; automation A24; BR-M06-04, BR-M06-12, BR-M06-13, BR-M02-06; TX-7; approvals via ApprovalService.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-06 — blind count, bin freeze, variance review, no stock change until approval, threshold routing; TS-PERM-09 — case 09.1 within vs above fixture thresholds; TS-PERM-08.1 — requester or counter cannot approve own adjustment/variance; TS-API-03 — replays of API-M06-21, API-M06-23 and API-M06-32; TS-SVC-01 — TX-7 atomicity; TS-API-01 for the seven endpoints.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Submitting a count creates variances and changes no stock position (TS-ERP-06 passes).
   2. A frozen bin rejects movements until its count is submitted; starting an already frozen bin returns 409 BIN_BUSY.
   3. Expected quantities are hidden from counters when the D-069 policy requires blind counts.
   4. An adjustment request without a reason returns 422; within the fixture threshold it is approvable by the manager, above it the request routes to the higher approver (TS-PERM-09.1 passes).
   5. Approval posts exactly one adjustment movement with reason and approver in one transaction; the counter or requester cannot approve (403).
   6. Bulk approval keeps a separate decision record per item.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

   4. A recall query returns every unit/lot movement and related order for a given lot number.

#### T-1A.6-M03-01 · Bin label documents (API-M03-07) and scanning input conventions for SKU, serial and bin labels
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M03
- **Depends on:** T-1A.2-M03-01
- **Decisions:** D-110, D-111
- **References:** 06 API-M03-07; 01 §21; 10 §2.3; BP §9.5, §10.4
- **Description:** Implement bin label documents and the scanning input conventions (BP §9.5, §10.4; 01 §21; 10 §2.3). LocationService renders the bin label document for selected bins of a location (API-M03-07; QR/barcode content, label format and printer type per D-110 and D-111), and P-E15 `#locations` gains the "Print labels" action for users with `org.bins.read` in the location (R-warehouse_staff, R-branch_manager, R-ops_admin, R-owner). The scanning conventions define, per D-110, the code formats for SKU (display SKU and barcodes), serial (internal serial label; manufacturer serial as printed by the maker) and bin labels, the input device mode (e.g. keyboard-wedge scanner vs camera, as decided), and one shared scan-code resolver that turns a scanned value into a SKU, serial unit or bin within the caller's location scope, where unknown or ambiguous codes are logged and change nothing (04b §2.16). The resolver and conventions are used by receiving (T-1A.7-M07-05), counts (T-1A.6-M06-08), transfers (T-1A.6-M06-07), serial lookup (T-1A.6-M06-04) and picking (T-1A.11-M12-03). Not part of this task: device/station integration (T-1A.11-M12-10, D-147), shipping labels and invoices (T-1A.11-M19-01, T-1A.11-M12-04).
- **Files/components:** `backend/organisation/` — bin label document; `backend/inventory/` — scan-code resolver and scanning-conventions document (finer structure per D-001/D-002); "Print labels" action in the P-E15 folder of `frontend/workspace/screens/` if D-004 = custom; scan-box input handling in `frontend/workspace/patterns/`.
- **Database impact:** None (reads E-location_bin, E-sku, E-serial_unit).
- **API impact:** Implements API-M03-07.
- **Frontend impact:** P-E15 `#locations` "Print labels"; scan-box behaviour shared by P-E08, P-E09 and P-E03.
- **Backend impact:** LocationService label rendering (document generation per D-111); scan-code resolver in the inventory module; BR-M03-03 (bins as stock locations).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ADM-06 labels part — label document for selected bins, scope enforced; scan-resolver unit tests — valid SKU, serial and bin codes resolve, unknown/ambiguous codes are logged and change nothing, codes outside the caller's location scope do not resolve; TS-API-01 for API-M03-07.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. "Print labels" produces a label document for the selected bins in the format decided under D-110/D-111; a user without `org.bins.read` for that location receives 404.
   2. The scanning conventions document lists the code formats for SKU, serial and bin labels and the input device mode decided in D-110.
   3. The resolver maps each valid scanned value to exactly one SKU, serial unit or bin; an unknown or ambiguous value is logged and causes no state change.
   4. Receiving, counting and transfer services use the same resolver (single implementation, verified by tests).
   5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.6-M04-01 · Bundles with component stock (CONDITIONAL; E-bundle_component; API-M04-06)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M04
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-02, T-1A.4-M04-04
- **Decisions:** D-072
- **References:** 08 §4.7; 03 §2.3.16; 06 API-M04-06; 16 TS-ECOM-14
- **Description:** CONDITIONAL — built only if D-072 approves bundles at launch (BP §7.5; PR1 §8 "subject to confirmed scope"; 12 §1.3); when not approved, API-M04-06 answers FEATURE_DISABLED, `is_bundle` cannot be set and the "Frequently bought together" bundle block is hidden (TS-ECOM-14). If approved, this task migrates E-bundle_component (DB-G2 conditional; bundle SKU with component SKUs and quantities; components are not bundles unless D-072 allows nesting) and implements BundleService: a bundle has no independent stock, its ATP is the minimum over components of component ATP ÷ component quantity, and bundle stock is never editable (BR-M04-17); the public API-M04-06 returns bundles containing a product with context price from the engine and component availability. Reserving or dispatching a bundle must reserve and move each component in the same transaction — this is implemented with the reservation service (T-1A.9-M06-01) and dispatch (T-1A.11-M12-05) and is flagged there when D-072 is approved. Not part of this task: P-S03 rendering (T-1A.9-M09-06), bundle promotions (D-043/D-072 in T-1A.5-M05-04).
- **Files/components:** `backend/catalog/` — E-bundle_component migration and BundleService; ATP composition in `backend/inventory/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002); feature flag via the configuration service.
- **Database impact:** Creates E-bundle_component (DB-G2, CONDITIONAL D-072); activates `is_bundle` on E-sku.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M04-06.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-S03 block in T-1A.9-M09-06 when enabled).
- **Backend impact:** BundleService, AtpCalculator composition; BR-M04-17.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-14 — disabled: FEATURE_DISABLED and hidden; enabled: bundle ATP = min over components, no direct bundle stock movement accepted, component quantities validated, context price from the engine; TS-DB-02 uniqueness case; TS-API-01 for API-M04-06.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Without D-072 approval, API-M04-06 answers FEATURE_DISABLED and the migration is not applied.
   2. With approval, bundle ATP equals the minimum over its components of component ATP divided by component quantity.
   3. No stock movement can be posted against a bundle SKU itself.
   4. The bundle price in API-M04-06 comes from the pricing engine for the caller's context.
   5. The requirement that reservation and dispatch act on every component is recorded against T-1A.9-M06-01 and T-1A.11-M12-05.
   6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.6-M23-01 · Branch POS / legacy stock-event adapter through a supported interface (API-M23-01; CONDITIONAL on existing-system decision)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.6 / M23
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-02, T-1A.2-M23-01
- **Decisions:** D-009, D-030
- **References:** 05 §5.23; 10 §12; 06 API-M23-01; 16 TS-INT-07, TS-ERR-02; BP §9.5, §21.3, §29.4; T05
- **Description:** CONDITIONAL — built only if D-009 keeps a legacy branch POS/ERP as a selling channel and D-030 decides how branch sales reach the stock authority (BP §9.1, §9.5, §16.4, §21.3, §29.4; 05 §5.23; 10 §12); otherwise branch sales use the counter path of assisted orders (T-1A.13-M10-01) and API-M23-01 stays disabled (FEATURE_DISABLED). If built, LegacyErpPosAdapter implements API-M23-01 for an R-integration credential scoped to legacy events only (issued through API-M02-36): event types branch sale, branch return and adjustment with external reference, location code, lines (SKU, quantity, serial) and occurrence time; the same stock-authority rules as online sales apply — ATP check (409 STOCK_UNAVAILABLE with available quantity), serial validity, returns into quarantine — and a duplicate external reference is a no-op (E-integration_event deduplication; idempotent). No uncontrolled dual-write between two ledgers (BR-M23-02, BR-M25-03); during an outage the D-030 process applies (segregated allocation or supervised manual entry; BR-M06-19, BR-M06-17). The adapter completes the integration contract checklist of BR-M23-01 (authentication, mapping, source of truth, identifiers, schema/version, retries, timeouts, rate limits, idempotency, reconciliation, support owner) and a reconciliation job compares legacy totals with the ledger. The movement type and source document used for a legacy branch sale are not specified in 03 §5.3 and must be confirmed (flagged); linking to an order record, if D-009 requires it, is completed when orders exist (T-1A.9-M10-03), and T05 end to end passes at T-1A.13-M16-05.
- **Files/components:** `backend/integrations/` — LegacyErpPosAdapter, contract checklist, reconciliation job, sandbox/contract tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002); integration setting per environment (seed S-18 part).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-integration_event, E-stock_movement, E-serial_event, E-exception_case; E-integration_setting record for the legacy adapter.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M23-01.
- **Frontend impact:** None (machine interface; status shown on P-E15 `#integrations` by T-1A.16-M24-01).
- **Backend impact:** LegacyErpPosAdapter → StockLedger/AtpCalculator; BR-M23-01, BR-M23-02, BR-M23-04, BR-M06-01, BR-M06-17, BR-M06-19; reconciliation job; R-integration credential (BR-M02-12, BR-M02-19).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-INT-07 — stock events through the supported interface, idempotent, shared authority with online sales (T05 part), outage allocation per D-030; TS-ERR-02 — stock authority unavailable and branch outage: no confirmation without authority; TS-AUTH-09 — the legacy credential cannot call any other endpoint; TS-API-03 — duplicate external reference returns the stored result; TS-INT-10 — contract checklist complete.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Without D-009/D-030 selecting this path, API-M23-01 answers FEATURE_DISABLED and no credential is issued.
   2. A branch sale for the last available unit is rejected with 409 STOCK_UNAVAILABLE when the unit is already reserved or sold online (T05 stock part).
   3. Replaying an event with the same external reference produces no second movement.
   4. The legacy credential is refused on every endpoint other than API-M23-01.
   5. During a simulated stock-authority outage no branch sale is confirmed except through the D-030 process, and the case is visible as an exception.
   6. The integration contract checklist is complete and the reconciliation job reports matching totals on test data.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.6-M25-01 · Opening stock and serial import scripts with control totals by location, owner, condition and serial
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **Description:** Write the opening stock and serial import scripts (BP §21.2 Stock and Serials, §5.1 1A exit gate "reconciled opening stock"; 03 §7.4; 05 §5.25). Opening balances by location, bin, stock owner, condition (SKU/grade) and serial are loaded only as `opening_balance` movements through StockLedger — never by direct position insert — within an E-import_job (job type opening_stock/migration) with row-level results and `row_hash` idempotency; serialised units are created with E-serial_unit, a `received` serial event and an inspection record where evidence exists, with the duplicate manufacturer-serial check (duplicates held and reported); unit cost values follow the valuation method decided in D-135; the historical scope and legacy read-only boundary follow D-038; lot numbers only if D-126 approved lot tracking (seed S-25, T-1A.6-M06-09). The scripts produce control totals of quantity and value by location, owner, condition and serial count for physical verification and reconciliation, recorded in an E-migration_rehearsal (`sample_trial`) for the stock dataset; rehearsal of the full load and final execution happen in 1A.17 (T-1A.17-M25-03, T-1A.17-M25-06). Not part of this task: catalog migration (T-1A.4-M25-01), open purchase orders (T-1A.7-M25-01), physical count execution at cutover.
- **Files/components:** `backend/migration/` — stock and serial mapping document, load scripts, control-total report (finer structure per D-001/D-002); rehearsal evidence referenced from `tests/migration/`.
- **Database impact:** Loads (staging) E-stock_movement (`opening_balance`), E-stock_position via the ledger, E-serial_unit, E-serial_event, E-inspection; E-import_job/E-import_row; one E-migration_rehearsal record; E-exception_case for duplicate serials.
- **API impact:** None (scripts run as audited batch jobs).
- **Frontend impact:** None.
- **Backend impact:** Scripts call StockLedger and SerialUnitService; BR-M25-01 (stock and serial datasets), BR-M25-03, BR-M25-06, BR-M25-07; BR-M06-04, BR-M06-09.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-MIG-03 stock part — control totals of quantity and value by location, owner, condition and serial reconcile with the source sample; TS-DB-07 — Σ movements = positions after the load; rerun idempotency (no duplicate movements or units); duplicate manufacturer serials reported, not loaded as sellable.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Opening stock is loaded only as `opening_balance` movements; no position row is inserted directly.
   2. Control totals of quantity, value (D-135), location, owner, condition and serial count reconcile with the source sample and are stored in the rehearsal record (TS-MIG-03 stock part passes).
   3. After the load, Σ movements equals positions for every key (TS-DB-07 passes).
   4. Rerunning the same extract creates no duplicate movements or serial units.
   5. Duplicate manufacturer serials are held out of sellable stock and listed as exceptions.
   6. The mapping document and procedure are reviewed by operations and finance for use in 1A.17.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

## Stage 1A.7 — Purchasing & receiving

#### T-1A.7-M07-01 · DB-G5 schema (E-purchase_order, E-purchase_order_line, E-goods_receipt, E-goods_receipt_line, E-supplier_bill, E-supplier_bill_line, E-replenishment_suggestion, E-cost_signal; E-landed_cost_charge by T-1A.7-M07-06)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.7 / M07
- **Depends on:** T-1A.6-M06-01, T-1A.5-M05-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 03 §4 DB-G5, §2.6; 16 TS-DB-01
- **Description:** Create the DB-G5 (Purchasing & receiving) migrations of 03 §4 on the selected core, recording native-versus-extension mapping per D-001 (purchase order, receipt and supplier-invoice candidates named in 03 §2.6): E-purchase_order (unique PO number; states draft → awaiting_approval → approved → sent → partially_received → received → closed/cancelled; approval request by value; totals in fixed money), E-purchase_order_line (ordered, received and cancelled quantities; unit cost; substitution link; cost-variance reason), E-goods_receipt (unique GRN number; approved PO; location; supplier reference; states in_progress/posted/cancelled; idempotency reference), E-goods_receipt_line (unique per receipt and PO line; received/accepted/rejected quantities; variance type none/over/short/substitution/wrong_serial; scanned serials), E-supplier_bill (unique supplier + supplier invoice number within the fiscal-year rule of D-055; match and review states; attachment), E-supplier_bill_line (PO/GRN line references, quantities, prices, tax, variances), E-replenishment_suggestion (inputs snapshot, suggested/accepted quantity, decision fields) and E-cost_signal (source, previous/new cost, state, resulting draft price version). It also adds the deferred nullable references declared in DB-G4: `serial_unit.goods_receipt_line_id`, `inspection.goods_receipt_line_id` and `lot.first_goods_receipt_line_id` (the latter only if E-lot exists under D-126). Not part of this task: E-landed_cost_charge (T-1A.7-M07-06, D-056), E-advance_shipping_notice (T-1B.1-M14-10, D-131), services (T-1A.7-M07-02 onwards), open-PO migration (T-1A.7-M25-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/purchasing/` migrations and entity definitions (E-cost_signal definition in `backend/pricing/`) with migration tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** DB-G5 created: E-purchase_order, E-purchase_order_line, E-goods_receipt, E-goods_receipt_line, E-supplier_bill, E-supplier_bill_line, E-replenishment_suggestion, E-cost_signal; nullable `goods_receipt_line_id` added to E-serial_unit and E-inspection (and to E-lot if present). No seed sets.
- **API impact:** None.
- **Frontend impact:** None.
- **Backend impact:** Entity definitions only.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-DB-01 — DB-G5 applies after DB-G2, DB-G3 and DB-G4 on an empty database and on the previous release; TS-DB-02 — constraint cases (duplicate PO/GRN number, duplicate GRN line per PO line, zero ordered quantity, duplicate supplier invoice key, bill line without PO or GRN reference); TS-DB-08 — money columns not floating point.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. DB-G5 migrations apply after DB-G4 on an empty database and on the previous release; reversible migrations roll back (TS-DB-01 passes).
   2. Each listed constraint is enforced with a passing TS-DB-02 case, including the supplier + invoice-number uniqueness within the D-055 fiscal-year rule.
   3. E-serial_unit and E-inspection carry the new nullable goods-receipt-line reference; existing rows are unaffected.
   4. E-landed_cost_charge and E-advance_shipping_notice are not created.
   5. The native/extension mapping of each DB-G5 entity is recorded per D-001.
   6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.7-M07-03 · Reorder rules and replenishment suggestions A17 (API-M06-30, API-M07-01, API-M07-02; nightly job; drafts only)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.7 / M07
- **Depends on:** T-1A.7-M07-01, T-1A.1-M17-01
- **Decisions:** D-070
- **References:** 05 §4 A17, §5.7; 10 §6; 06 API-M06-30, API-M07-01, API-M07-02; 16 TS-ERP-09; BP §9.3, §5.3
- **Description:** Implement reorder rules and replenishment suggestions (A17; BP §9.3, §5.3; 05 §5.7; 10 §6). ReorderRuleService maintains per SKU × location the reorder point, lead time, optional preferred supplier, owner (buyer role per D-222) and active flag (API-M06-30 with `expected_version`; archived SKUs excluded; parameter values and basis — quoted or measured lead time — per D-070). ReplenishmentService runs as a nightly job on the job runtime: it compares ATP plus open PO quantities against the reorder point, excludes discontinued items and creates E-replenishment_suggestion rows with an inputs snapshot (ATP, reorder point, on order, average daily demand, lead time) and a reason; the suggestions list supports supplier and stock-out filters (API-M07-01), and the buyer creates draft POs grouped per supplier with edited quantities or dismisses with reason and optional snooze (API-M07-02). The rule only drafts — nothing is sent to suppliers and every draft needs the PO approval of T-1A.7-M07-04 (BR-M07-02; "autonomous purchasing" excluded, BP §5.3). The job is specified with the BP §12.3 template (trigger, inputs, preconditions, action, idempotency, failure behaviour, human boundary, audit, KPI, disable) and is activated per D-078 through the rule registry of T-1A.14-M17-01/T-1A.14-M17-02; failures raise one incident via A38. Forecast-based quantities (A30) are LATER. Not part of this task: P-E09 `#suggestions` (T-1A.7-M07-08), the P-E08 reorder-point column (T-1A.6-M06-11).
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` — ReorderRuleService; `backend/purchasing/` — ReplenishmentService job, API handlers, tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-reorder_rule, E-replenishment_suggestion, E-purchase_order/E-purchase_order_line (drafts only), E-job_attempt, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M06-30, API-M07-01, API-M07-02.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E09 `#suggestions` in T-1A.7-M07-08).
- **Backend impact:** ReorderRuleService, ReplenishmentService; automation A17; BR-M07-02, BR-M07-13; nightly job with idempotency per run; exceptions per A38.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-09 — suggestion only, never a sent PO; discontinued items excluded; draft POs grouped per supplier; dismiss requires a reason; TS-SVC-02 — job crash and rerun create no duplicate suggestions; TS-API-01 and TS-API-04 for the three endpoints; reorder parameter values are test fixtures until D-070 is decided (16 P8).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. The nightly job creates suggestions only for active rules whose ATP plus open POs falls below the reorder point, with the inputs snapshot and reason stored.
   2. Archived/discontinued SKUs never receive suggestions.
   3. "Create draft POs" produces one draft PO per supplier and sends nothing to any supplier (TS-ERP-09 passes).
   4. Dismissing a suggestion requires a reason; snoozed suggestions reappear only after the snooze date.
   5. Rerunning the job for the same period creates no duplicate suggestions.
   6. Reorder-rule changes are audited and refused with a stale `expected_version`.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.7-M07-04 · Purchase orders: draft, edit, purchasable-SKU lookup, submit for approval by value, send to supplier, remind, cancel remaining, PO document (API-M07-03…08, API-M07-21)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **Depends on:** T-1A.7-M07-02, T-1A.2-M17-01
- **Decisions:** D-176, D-175, D-111

- **Description:** Implement PurchaseOrderService (BP §9.2, §9.3, §18.1; 05 §5.7; 10 §6): PO list with search, supplier and status filters (API-M07-03); create a draft PO (API-M07-04, idempotent: active supplier, deliver-to location with receiving capability, expected date, payment and freight terms, supplier quotation reference, note, lines with mapped SKU, quantity and unit cost ≥ 0, and returned checks — supplier active/GSTIN verified, price vs last PO with a reason required above the D-024 threshold, open-PO overlap, delivery date vs lead time); PO detail with lines, approval and linked receipts/bills (API-M07-05); edit a draft with `expected_version` (API-M07-06); transitions (API-M07-07, idempotent): submit for approval by PO value with thresholds from D-024 (202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED, or approved within the caller's own authority only if D-175 allows self-approval below a limit; creator never approves above it — BR-M02-06, BR-M07-10), send to supplier only when approved — automatically or by explicit action and through the channel decided in D-176 (outbox to email via M20; portal view in 1B) — remind supplier, cancel remaining unreceived quantity with reason, update expected date or keep a backorder (BP §9.3), and close; the PO document (API-M07-08, approved/sent only, rendering per D-111); and the purchasable-SKU lookup with supplier code and last cost shown only with `cost.view` (API-M07-21; D-197). Issuing a PO never changes on-hand stock (BR-M07-01). The buyer responsibility maps to roles per D-222; approvals decide through API-M17-03 (TX-10). The purchase-budget check shown in the mockup is MOCKUP-ONLY (D-177) and not built. Not part of this task: P-E09 screens (T-1A.7-M07-08), receipts (T-1A.7-M07-05), supplier confirmation/ASN (T-1B.1-M14-10).
- **Files/components:** `backend/purchasing/` — PurchaseOrderService, PO document rendering hook, API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-purchase_order, E-purchase_order_line, E-approval_request (purchase_order), E-outbox_operation, E-idempotency_record, E-audit_event; reads E-supplier_code_mapping.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M07-03, API-M07-04, API-M07-05, API-M07-06, API-M07-07, API-M07-08, API-M07-21; consumes API-M17-03.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E09 `#orders`, `d-po`, `#new-po` in T-1A.7-M07-08).
- **Backend impact:** PurchaseOrderService; BR-M07-01, BR-M07-03, BR-M07-09, BR-M07-10, BR-M02-06; TX-10 for approval; outbox for supplier transmission (M20 email adapter from 1A.2).

- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A draft PO is created with its checks returned; submitting it twice with the same idempotency key returns the same PO and approval request.
   2. Submission above the caller's authority returns 202 with an approval request; a PO cannot be sent until approved, and the send behaviour/channel follows D-176.
   3. The PO creator cannot approve the PO (403); self-approval below a limit happens only if D-175 allows it.
   4. Cancel-remaining affects only unreceived quantities and requires a reason; update-expected-date/keep-backorder records the new date.
   5. Issuing, approving or sending a PO creates no stock movement.
   6. The PO document is available only for approved or sent POs; last cost in the SKU lookup is visible only with `cost.view` per D-197.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

- **Description:** Implement ReceiptService for goods receipt with serial scanning and QC (A03; BP §9.2, §9.3, §9.4, §17.4; 06-api §4.6; 05 §5.7 BR-M07-11): list receipts (API-M07-20); start (or directly post) a receipt against an approved/sent, not closed PO for a location the receiver is assigned to, with supplier reference (API-M07-09, idempotent); GRN detail with lines, scan log, variances and QC per unit (API-M07-10); scans (API-M07-12) resolved through the scan-code resolver of T-1A.6-M03-01 and classified as matched, duplicate_serial, not_on_po or over_qty — duplicate serials (enterprise-wide) and codes not on the PO open an E-exception_case with the scan evidence and never create stock (BR-M07-05; T15), and matched serialised units get an internal serial with the manufacturer serial captured where required; draft updates of quantities, variance handling (short/backorder/cancel remaining, over-receipt held for buyer approval, substitution held for buyer approval — BP §9.3) and QC outcomes recorded as inspections through API-M06-09 (API-M07-11, `expected_version`); and posting (API-M07-13, idempotent, `422 UNRESOLVED_LINES` while handling is missing) as one stock transaction (TX-5): receipt into receiving_inspection, QC pass → sellable (`qc_accept`), QC fail → quarantine (`qc_reject`) with the supplier resolution (RTV/replacement/credit note) recorded — the E-supplier_rma draft is created once the supplier-RMA service exists (T-1A.12-M13-06) — held lines → exception without stock, PO received quantities and status updated, outbox events for the availability refresh (A04) and bill matching, audit (BR-M07-03, BR-M07-04, BR-M07-12). Only assigned warehouse staff, managers and owner/ops record receipts; vendors never (BR-M07-11); the "PO creator should not receive" rule warns or blocks per D-196. Scanner devices follow D-110. Not part of this task: landed cost (T-1A.7-M07-06), P-E09 `#receive` (T-1A.7-M07-09), ASN pre-fill (T-1B.1-M14-10).
- **Files/components:** `backend/purchasing/` — ReceiptService, scan classification, posting transaction, API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-goods_receipt, E-goods_receipt_line, E-serial_unit, E-serial_event, E-inspection, E-stock_movement, E-purchase_order_line quantities, E-exception_case, E-approval_request (substitution/over-receipt), E-outbox_operation, E-idempotency_record, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M07-09, API-M07-10, API-M07-11, API-M07-12, API-M07-13, API-M07-20; consumes API-M06-09 for QC records.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E09 `#receive` in T-1A.7-M07-09).
- **Backend impact:** ReceiptService with StockLedger, SerialUnitService and InspectionService; automation A03; BR-M07-03, BR-M07-04, BR-M07-05, BR-M07-11, BR-M07-12; TX-5.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-04 — partial receipt, wrong serial → discrepancy and nothing published (T15), over/short, substitution approval, quarantine on fail, posting idempotent; TS-SVC-01 — TX-5 fault injection leaves no partial effect; TS-API-03 — replays of API-M07-09 and API-M07-13 return the stored result; TS-API-01 for the six endpoints; TS-PERM-02.6 — GRN of another location answers 404; T15.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Posting a receipt of three serialised units with one QC fail and one wrong serial yields two sellable units (or per outcomes), one quarantined unit and one exception with no stock for the wrong serial (T15 passes).
   2. A duplicate or not-on-PO scan opens an exception with the scan evidence and never creates a unit or movement.
   3. Over-receipt and substitution lines stay held until buyer approval; posting with unresolved handling returns 422 UNRESOLVED_LINES.
   4. Replaying the posting request produces no second movement; a fault inside TX-5 leaves nothing posted.

- **Backend impact:** ReceiptService landed-cost allocation; BR-M07-08, BR-M05-14; cost signals raised for changed unit costs.
- **Testing requirements:** Disabled: landed-cost input answers FEATURE_DISABLED and the UI is hidden (12 §1.3); enabled: allocations by value, quantity and weight sum exactly to the charge; unit cost updated; no price-list change occurs; cost fields absent for roles not allowed under D-197 (TS-PERM-10.3 case).

   1. Without D-056 approval, landed-cost input is refused with FEATURE_DISABLED and no landed-cost UI appears.
   2. With approval, each allocation basis distributes the charge so that allocations sum exactly to the charge amount.
   3. Posting landed cost changes unit cost only; no price list or live price changes (verified by comparing price versions before and after).
   4. Landed-cost values are visible only to roles allowed under D-197.
   5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.7-M07-07 · Supplier bills, three-way match and duplicate detection A25 (API-M07-14…17)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.7 / M07
- **Depends on:** T-1A.7-M07-04, T-1A.7-M07-05
- **Decisions:** D-178
- **References:** 05 §5.7 BR-M07-07; 06 API-M07-14…17; 16 TS-ERP-09; BP §9.3; A25
- **Description:** Implement BillMatchingService for supplier bills, three-way match and duplicate detection (A25; BP §9.3; 05 §5.7): record a supplier bill by manual entry (API-M07-15, idempotent: supplier, supplier invoice number and date, lines referencing PO/GRN lines, totals, mandatory bill attachment through API-M22-01) with the duplicate check on supplier + normalised invoice number within the fiscal-year rule — an exact duplicate creates the bill on hold with `409 DUPLICATE_SUSPECTED` and an exception, near matches are flagged for staff review (look-back window, number normalisation and near-match criteria per D-178; BR-M07-07); list bills with match status (API-M07-14); the three-way match detail comparing PO quantity/price, received quantity and billed quantity/price and tax per line with the tolerance result (tolerance values per D-024) and duplicate candidates (API-M07-16); and actions with mandatory reason (API-M07-17): send to buyer, request credit note, approve with variance (202 by threshold), mark not a duplicate (approval per separation of duties) and reject as duplicate. A late GRN recalculates the match; matched or approved bills become payable and are exported once to the accounting authority by T-1A.15-M19-01 (A26; D-011); payment execution stays in accounting. OCR extraction (A31) is LATER. Not part of this task: P-E09 `#bills` (T-1A.7-M07-09), cost signals from bills (T-1A.7-M05-01), accounting export (T-1A.15-M19-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/purchasing/` — BillMatchingService, duplicate detector, match recalculation, API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-supplier_bill, E-supplier_bill_line, E-exception_case (duplicate/variance), E-approval_request, E-attachment, E-idempotency_record, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M07-14, API-M07-15, API-M07-16, API-M07-17; consumes API-M22-01 and API-M17-03.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E09 `#bills` in T-1A.7-M07-09).
- **Backend impact:** BillMatchingService; automation A25; BR-M07-06, BR-M07-07, BR-M07-09; bill recording + duplicate check in one transaction; match recalculation on late GRN.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-09 — duplicate supplier invoice detection (exact key blocked, near match flagged), three-way match variances routed to finance/buyer, approve with variance per threshold, late GRN recalculates; TS-API-03 — replay of API-M07-15 creates no second bill; TS-API-01 for the four endpoints; tolerance and duplicate-window values are fixtures until D-024/D-178 (16 P8).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Recording a bill whose supplier and normalised invoice number match an existing bill creates it on hold with 409 DUPLICATE_SUSPECTED and an exception; a near match is flagged for review.
   2. The match detail shows per-line PO, GRN and bill quantities and prices, tax comparison and the tolerance result.
   3. A bill within tolerance becomes matched; outside tolerance it is held until an authorised approve-with-variance (202 when above threshold) or credit note.
   4. "Not a duplicate" and "approve with variance" require a reason and cannot be decided by the person who recorded the bill where separation applies.
   5. A GRN posted after the bill recalculates the match automatically.
   6. Replaying the record request with the same key returns the stored bill.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.7-M05-01 · Cost signals from supplier bills/receipts that never change live prices automatically (API-M05-22, API-M05-23; E-cost_signal)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.7 / M05
- **Depends on:** T-1A.7-M07-07, T-1A.5-M05-03
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 05 §5.5; 00 §7.2 E-cost_signal; 06 API-M05-22, API-M05-23; 04b §10; BP §8.4
- **Description:** Implement CostSignalService so that supplier cost changes never change live prices automatically (BP §8.4 "Supplier changes cost"; BR-M05-14; 00 §7.2 E-cost_signal): detect cost changes from posted receipts and PO lines (unit cost vs previous cost), supplier bill lines (billed price vs PO/last cost) and, if D-056 is approved, landed-cost allocations — later sources (supplier availability and import files) are added in 1B.2 — and create E-cost_signal records with previous and new cost, margin at the current price (cost basis per D-135), a suggested action and state open. The signals list (API-M05-22) shows product, source, cost change, margin at current public/dealer price and suggestion; actions (API-M05-23) either create a draft price-list change through PriceChangeService — a draft E-price_rule_version that follows the normal change-request approval and is never auto-activated — or dismiss with a mandatory reason. The "Supplier cost changes detected" section of P-E07 `#approvals` (04b §10.8) is built here as custom UI if D-004 so decides. Cost and margin values are visible only to roles allowed under D-197. Not part of this task: price-list approval and activation (T-1A.5-M05-03), the margin-leakage flag A36 (T-1B.4-M05-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/pricing/` — CostSignalService, detection hooks called from `backend/purchasing/`, API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002); P-E07 `#approvals` cost-signal section in `frontend/workspace/screens/` if D-004 = custom.
- **Database impact:** Writes E-cost_signal and draft E-price_rule_version rows; E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M05-22, API-M05-23.
- **Frontend impact:** P-E07 `#approvals` "Supplier cost changes detected" table with "Draft change" and "Dismiss".
- **Backend impact:** CostSignalService with PriceChangeService; BR-M05-14; detection on receipt posting and bill recording events.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-16 — a supplier cost change creates a signal and never changes a live price; drafting creates a pending change that still needs approval; dismissal needs a reason; TS-PERM-10.3 — cost/margin fields absent for roles not allowed under D-197; TS-API-01 for API-M05-22 and API-M05-23.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A posted receipt or recorded bill with a changed unit cost creates exactly one open cost signal per SKU and source.
   2. No live price list version changes as a result of any signal (verified by version comparison).
   3. "Draft change" creates a draft price-list change that follows the normal approval; "Dismiss" without a reason returns 422.
   4. Cost and margin columns appear only for roles allowed under D-197.
   5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

Conditional DB-G6 entities are migrated by their feature tasks only after their decision: E-customer_tag (T-1A.8-M08-09, D-145), E-customer_merge (T-1A.12-M08-01, D-133), E-wishlist_item (T-1A.9-M09-09, D-042), E-alert_subscription (T-1A.13-M20-05, D-141).
