#### T-1A.8-M08-02 · Consumer registration, own profile, contact change with dual codes, addresses (API-M08-01…08)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.8 / M08
- **Depends on:** T-1A.8-M08-01, T-1A.2-M02-05
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 07 §3.2; 08 §4.22; 06 API-M08-01…08; 16 TS-ECOM-09, TS-AUTH-06, TS-UNIT-07
- **Description:** Implement RegistrationService, CustomerProfileService and AddressService (07 §3.2; 08 §4.22; 05 §5.8): consumer registration (API-M08-01) that requires the verification token from a `register` one-time code (API-M02-02, API-M02-03), creates E-customer and E-user_account with an optional password per D-040, records service and marketing consents per channel and purpose separately (marketing never pre-ticked; BR-M08-06) and the accepted terms and privacy-notice versions (E-terms_acceptance), answers existing-account cases without enumeration (generic `409 ALREADY_REGISTERED` — the mockup conflict is resolved non-enumerating under D-040) and issues a session; own profile read and update of name, message language (D-050) and optional invoice GSTIN with format check only (API-M08-02, API-M08-03, `expected_version`); contact change of mobile or email that needs verification of both the current and the new contact and sends a sign-in alert (API-M08-04); and saved addresses (API-M08-05…API-M08-08) with ownership checked on every use (BR-M08-13), PIN format under D-059, one default per owner, locked registered business addresses, and orders keeping their own address snapshot when an address is edited or removed. The address serviceability flag is filled once PIN serviceability exists (T-1A.9-M12-01). Not part of this task: consents API (T-1A.8-M08-03), data requests (T-1A.8-M08-04), the P-S12 `#register` and P-S09 screens (T-1A.8-M09-01, T-1A.8-M09-02), guest checkout (T-1A.9-M10-06), password migration (T-1A.17-M02-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/customers/` — RegistrationService, CustomerProfileService, AddressService, API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-customer, E-user_account, E-consent_record, E-terms_acceptance, E-address, E-audit_event; reads E-verification_challenge.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M08-01, API-M08-02, API-M08-03, API-M08-04, API-M08-05, API-M08-06, API-M08-07, API-M08-08; consumes API-M02-02 and API-M02-03 verification tokens.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-S12 `#register` in T-1A.8-M09-01; P-S09 in T-1A.8-M09-02).
- **Backend impact:** RegistrationService, CustomerProfileService, AddressService, OtpService/SessionService integration; BR-M08-06, BR-M08-13, BR-M02-09, BR-M02-11.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-09 — profile, contact change with dual codes, addresses; TS-AUTH-06 — registration with verification token, consents and terms version; TS-AUTH-01 — no enumeration on registration; TS-UNIT-07 — address/PIN and GSTIN format validation; TS-PERM-02.2 address part — a customer using another customer's address id receives 404; TS-API-01 and TS-API-04 for the eight endpoints.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Registration without a valid `register` verification token is refused; with it, the account, consent records and terms/privacy-notice acceptances are created and a session is issued.
   2. Marketing consent is recorded only when explicitly granted; service and marketing consents are separate records.
   3. Registering an already-registered contact returns the same generic response as other failures (no enumeration).
   4. A contact change requires verification of both the current and the new contact and sends a sign-in alert.
   5. A customer can add, edit, set default and remove only own addresses; another customer's address id returns 404; a locked registered address cannot be edited by members.
   6. Profile updates with a stale `expected_version` return 409; invoice GSTIN is format-checked but never treated as business verification.
   7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.8-M08-03 · Consent records per channel/purpose with history, customer/dealer terms and privacy-notice versions (staff drafts published via approval) and acceptance, S-15 customer terms (API-M08-09, API-M08-10, API-M14-57, API-M14-58)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.8 / M08
- **Depends on:** T-1A.8-M08-01
- **Decisions:** D-188, D-037
- **References:** 08 §4.22, §4.23; 03 §2.7.7, §6 S-15; 06 API-M08-09, API-M08-10; 16 TS-ECOM-09, TS-SVC-05; BP §13.3, §19.2; T25
- **Description:** Implement ConsentService and terms versions (BP §13.3, §19.2; 08 §4.22, §4.23; 03 §2.7.7). Consents: own consent state per channel (WhatsApp, SMS, email) and purpose (values per D-058) with full history (API-M08-09) and grant/withdraw including "stop all marketing", which withdraws marketing purposes only (API-M08-10); every change is an append-only E-consent_record with source and privacy-notice version, the current state is the latest record, saving a phone number never grants marketing permission (BR-M08-06, BR-M08-07), and a consent-lookup function is exposed for every outbound message so that opted-out recipients are never messaged (T25 basis; dispatch in T-1A.13-M20-01). Terms versions: staff list of supplier, dealer and customer terms and privacy-notice versions (API-M14-57) and creation of a draft version with document, effective date, change summary and acceptance flag whose publication is decided through API-M17-03 (API-M14-58); published versions are immutable and acceptances are recorded as E-terms_acceptance with evidence; whether a new version requires re-acceptance before it applies, or may be deemed accepted, follows D-188. Seed S-15 part: customer terms and privacy notice with the versions and content decided under D-037 (dealer terms in T-1A.8-M08-08; supplier terms in 1B). API-M14-57 and API-M14-58 are guarded by the permission keys `terms.read` and `terms.manage` defined in 07 §5.5/§13.13. Not part of this task: P-S09 `#privacy` (T-1A.8-M09-02), notification dispatch and templates (T-1A.13-M20-01), guest newsletter subscription (MOCKUP-ONLY, T-1A.13-M20-05).
- **Files/components:** `backend/customers/` — ConsentService; terms-version service in `backend/vendors/` per 06-api (M14 TermsService) with API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002); S-15 seed definitions (customer terms, privacy notice).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-consent_record (append-only), E-terms_version, E-terms_acceptance, E-approval_request, E-attachment; seed S-15 (customer terms and privacy notice part).
- **API impact:** Implements API-M08-09, API-M08-10, API-M14-57, API-M14-58; consumes API-M17-03 for publication.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-S09 `#privacy` and `m-consent-log` in T-1A.8-M09-02; terms-version staff screen placement per D-004 — no mockup screen).
- **Backend impact:** ConsentService (consent lookup used by M20), TermsService; BR-M08-06, BR-M08-07; approval via ApprovalService.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-09 consent part — change recorded with channel, purpose, source and notice version; history shown; "stop all marketing" leaves service consents unchanged; TS-SVC-05 opt-out case (consent lookup refuses a marketing send to an opted-out recipient — T25 basis); TS-DB-04 — consent records append-only; TS-DB-05 — S-15 part loads only decided content; TS-API-01 for the four endpoints; TS-PERM-01 — endpoints mapped to `terms.read` and `terms.manage`.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Every consent change creates a new record with channel, purpose, source and notice version; the current state equals the latest record and the history lists all changes.
   2. "Stop all marketing" withdraws all marketing purposes and leaves service-update consents unchanged.
   3. The consent lookup returns "not permitted" for a recipient whose latest record for that channel and purpose is an opt-out.
   4. A terms version draft is published only after an approval decision; a published version cannot be edited; the acceptance rule follows D-188.
   5. S-15 customer terms and privacy notice load with the content and versions decided under D-037 and pass TS-DB-05.
   6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.8-M08-04 · Data-rights requests: own requests, staff queue with retention check and processing (API-M08-12, API-M08-13, API-M08-44, API-M08-45; E-data_request)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.8 / M08
- **Depends on:** T-1A.8-M08-01, T-1A.2-M17-01
- **Decisions:** D-060, D-036
- **References:** 08 §4.22; 03 §2.7.8, §9; 06 API-M08-12, API-M08-13, API-M08-44, API-M08-45; 16 TS-DB-06; BP §19.2, §19.3
- **Description:** Implement DataRequestService for data-rights requests (BP §19.2, §19.3; 08 §4.22; 03 §2.7.8, §9): the customer's own requests and status (API-M08-12) and new requests of type access/export, correction, nomination or account deletion (API-M08-13) with identity re-verification per D-202, a dry run for deletion that lists blockers (open orders, open RMAs, pending refunds) and due dates per D-037; the staff queue with retention check showing which records are statutorily retained (API-M08-44) and processing actions — process, re-send secure link, open a request on behalf of a customer (API-M08-45). Deletion separates removal of profile and access from legally retained transaction records: profile PD1 fields are anonymised through the retention hooks while invoice, warranty and other statutory records are kept (masked) (BR-M08-09, BR-M08-10); access exports are private, expiring files. Which rights apply and their deadlines follow D-037, the deletion workflow D-060 and retention periods D-036; due-date tracking runs as a job and overdue requests surface through the exception core. Not part of this task: the full retention matrix and its hooks for all entities (T-1A.16-M26-02), P-S09 `#privacy` (T-1A.8-M09-02), P-E10 `#privacy` (T-1A.8-M08-11).
- **Files/components:** `backend/customers/` — DataRequestService, anonymisation step for customer profiles, due-date job, API handlers and tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-data_request, E-customer (state, anonymised PD1), E-address, E-consent_record (withdrawals), E-attachment (export files), E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M08-12, API-M08-13, API-M08-44, API-M08-45.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-S09 `#privacy`, `m-delete` in T-1A.8-M09-02; P-E10 `#privacy` in T-1A.8-M08-11).
- **Backend impact:** DataRequestService; BR-M08-09, BR-M08-10; due-date job on the job runtime; approvals/queue via M17 where the process requires review.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-DB-06 — deletion anonymises profile data and keeps statutory records; each retention class hook applied to customer data; TS-ECOM-09 data-request part — request, blockers on dry run, status; TS-API-01 for the four endpoints; TS-PERM-02 — a customer cannot read another customer's request (404).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A deletion dry run lists open orders, RMAs and pending refunds as blockers; a deletion request with blockers cannot be completed.
   2. Processing a deletion anonymises the customer's profile and contact data, withdraws marketing consents and leaves invoices, warranty and other statutory records intact (TS-DB-06 passes).
   3. An access/export request produces a private, expiring file for the requester only.
   4. Every request records received time, due date per D-037 and the staff decision with reason; overdue requests are visible to staff.
   5. A customer sees only own requests; staff processing is limited to the privacy roles (R-ops_admin, R-owner).
   6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

- **Frontend impact:** None (P-S12 `#dealer` in T-1A.8-M09-01; P-S11 status panel in T-1A.8-M09-03).
- **Backend impact:** DealerApplicationService, GstinVerificationPort/Adapter; automation A27; BR-M08-01, BR-M08-02; integration contract per BR-M23-01.

- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A submitted application passes through the A27 completeness check and lands in review; no path approves it automatically.
   2. A GSTIN verification stores the source response, time and reference; a cancelled or malformed GSTIN blocks submission with the reason; an unavailable source returns 503 and the application can proceed to manual review.
   3. A GSTIN already used by a non-rejected business account is flagged as a duplicate.
   4. The applicant sees the current state with reasons and requested actions and can update and re-submit only when the state requires action.
   5. Uploaded documents are private files visible only to the applicant and authorised reviewers.
   6. The GSTIN adapter's integration contract checklist is complete (TS-INT-10).

#### T-1A.8-M08-06 · Business accounts, members and member invitations, account change requests with re-verification; buyer context from verified membership completes API-M02-01 buyer context; dealer's private price-list view (API-M08-24…27, API-M08-50, API-M05-04)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **Depends on:** T-1A.8-M08-05, T-1A.5-M05-02, T-1A.2-M02-07
- **Decisions:** D-066, D-205

- **Description:** Implement BusinessAccountService and MembershipService and complete the buyer context (BP §6.5, §8.3; 07 §3.3, §3.4, §4.4; 05 BR-M02-13): creation of an approved business account from an application — account, owner membership (owner invitation to the contact person) and price-list assignment in one transaction, used by the decision endpoint of T-1A.8-M08-07; the account overview (API-M08-24); members with roles and limits (API-M08-25); member invitations sent through InvitationService and accepted on P-S14 (API-M08-26, API-M02-16, API-M02-17); change of member role/limit or removal, never removing the last owner and revoking access immediately (API-M08-27); account change requests for GSTIN, legal name or registered address that require re-verification and pause dealer pricing meanwhile (API-M08-50; BR-M08-16); and the dealer's private price-list view with retail vs account price vs tiers, returned `private, no-store` (API-M05-04). Buyer context in API-M02-01 is now derived only from an active membership of an approved account (segment, business account, member role, opaque price-list reference); pending, rejected, suspended or approval-expired accounts and removed members get public prices immediately with permission caches invalidated (BR-M02-13, BR-M02-14, BR-M05-08, BR-M05-16, BR-M08-05); the approval-expiry job sets `approval_expired` and sends reminders per the D-067 rule. Not part of this task: staff business-account administration (T-1A.8-M08-07), P-S11 screens (T-1A.8-M09-03), dealer order approvals (T-1A.9-M08-01), price-list export (T-1A.15-M18-03).

- **Database impact:** Writes E-business_account, E-business_account_member, E-invitation, E-verification_document (change requests), E-approval_request, E-audit_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M08-24, API-M08-25, API-M08-26, API-M08-27, API-M08-50, API-M05-04; completes the `buyer_context` of API-M02-01; consumes API-M02-16 and API-M02-17 for member acceptance.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-S11 in T-1A.8-M09-03; P-S14 invitation landing already built in T-1A.3-M09-05).
- **Backend impact:** BusinessAccountService, MembershipService, BuyerContextResolver, InvitationService; BR-M02-13, BR-M02-14, BR-M05-08, BR-M05-16, BR-M08-03, BR-M08-05, BR-M08-16; approval-expiry job.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-10 — approved, suspended and approval-expired states, member invitations; TS-PERM-02.3 — a member of account X reading Y's price list, members or overview receives 404; TS-PERM-05.3 — removing a member or suspending the account removes dealer context on the next request; TS-PERM-03.4 — a member cannot change own role or limit; TS-PERM-03.6 — owner GSTIN change creates a change request and pauses dealer pricing, buyer attempt returns 403; TS-AUTH-06 — member invitation single-use and expiring; TS-API-07 — API-M05-04 is `private, no-store`; TS-SVC-11 — approval-expiry reminders; T02 membership part.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Account creation from an approved application creates the account, the owner membership/invitation and the price-list assignment atomically; a failure leaves none of them.
   2. Only an active member of an approved account receives dealer context in API-M02-01 and dealer prices from the engine (T02 membership part passes).
   3. Suspension, approval expiry or member removal makes the next request return public prices; no cached private price is served afterwards (TS-PERM-05.3 passes).
   4. Cross-account access to overview, members or price list returns 404 (TS-PERM-02.3 passes).
   5. Member invitations are single-use and expiring; the last owner cannot be removed; removal revokes access immediately.
   6. A GSTIN/legal-name/address change request pauses dealer pricing until re-verification.
   7. Behaviour with several memberships follows D-205, and member-role permissions follow D-066.
   8. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

Not part of this task: P-E10 screens (T-1A.8-M08-11), tags and bulk messages (T-1A.8-M08-09), view as dealer (T-1A.8-M08-10), duplicates (T-1A.12-M08-01), data-request processing (T-1A.8-M08-04).

- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-17 — application decision with reason and price list, suspension and reinstatement, members on behalf; TS-PERM-10.1 — customer list and 360 masked for staff roles; TS-PERM-08.1 — the initiator cannot approve own price-list change or reinstatement; TS-PERM-09.2 — request-only roles create approval requests instead of executing; TS-API-01 for the implemented endpoints; T02 staff-approval part.

#### T-1A.8-M02-01 · Sensitive-field masking and reveal with reason, time limit and audit (P-E10 reveal, P-E08 m-reveal of manufacturer serials); field-level protection at rest (API-M02-31)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.8 / M02
- **Depends on:** T-1A.8-M08-07, T-1A.2-M02-03
- **Decisions:** D-153, D-130
- **References:** 07 §7; 05 BR-M02-17; 03 §9.2; 06 API-M02-31; 16 TS-PERM-10
- **Description:** Implement SensitiveRevealService and sensitive-field protection (07 §7; BR-M02-17; 03 §9.2): masking of sensitive fields in staff responses — customer contact data (PD1) in the customer list and 360, manufacturer serials of sold units (PD-R) in unit, receipt and lookup responses, identity/KYC data (PD2) — according to the field × role policy decided in D-153 (masking is applied server-side, not only in the UI); the reveal endpoint (API-M02-31) that requires a reason from the D-153 reason list, returns the value with a `visible_until` time limit and writes an audit event for every reveal (`422` without reason); and field-level protection at rest for PAN, bank details, identity documents, manufacturer serials, beneficiary details and guest access secrets per the mechanism decided in D-130. UI: the "Reveal" link and reason modal on P-E10 `#d-360` (email/phone) and the P-E08 `#serials` "Reveal (audited)" link with `m-reveal` (also used by the P-E09 `#receive` masked serial), built as custom UI if D-004 so decides. Not part of this task: cost/margin visibility (D-197, handled in the pricing/purchasing tasks), audit viewer (T-1A.3-M02-02), export controls (T-1A.15-M18-03).
- **Files/components:** `backend/identity/` — SensitiveRevealService, masking policy applied by the response layers of `backend/customers/`, `backend/inventory/`, `backend/purchasing/`; at-rest protection per D-130 in the persistence layer (finer structure per D-001/D-002); reveal link and `m-reveal` in the P-E10 and P-E08 folders of `frontend/workspace/screens/` if D-004 = custom.
- **Database impact:** Applies the D-130 protection to the PD2/PD-R columns of E-customer, E-business_account, E-dealer_application, E-verification_document, E-supplier, E-serial_unit (and later entities as they are created); writes E-audit_event for reveals.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M02-31; changes the masked output of API-M08-28, API-M08-29, API-M06-06, API-M06-07 and API-M07-10.
- **Frontend impact:** P-E10 `#d-360` "Reveal" with reason; P-E08 `#serials` "Reveal (audited)" and `m-reveal`; masked-serial reveal on P-E09 `#receive`.
- **Backend impact:** SensitiveRevealService; BR-M02-17, BR-M02-08, BR-M02-11; masking policy per D-153; at-rest protection per D-130.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-PERM-10 — case 10.1 masking by role for customer 360 and serial units, case 10.2 reveal without reason → 422 and with reason → value with time limit and audit entry; TS-SEC-07 — storage protection of the D-130 fields verified; TS-SVC-03 — reveal audit written in the same transaction; TS-SEC-06 — revealed values and identity documents never appear in logs; TS-API-01 for API-M02-31.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Staff responses mask the fields listed in D-153 for each role; the masking is present in the API response, not only in the UI (TS-PERM-10.1 passes).
   2. A reveal without a reason returns 422; with a reason it returns the value with `visible_until` and writes one audit event with actor, object, field and reason (TS-PERM-10.2 passes).
   3. After `visible_until` the value is no longer returned unmasked without a new reveal.
   4. The D-130 fields are protected at rest by the decided mechanism (TS-SEC-07 check passes).
   5. No revealed value, identity document number or serial appears in logs (TS-SEC-06 scan clean).
   6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

In the documented read-only form, API-M08-37 returns what the dealer account sees — its price-list view and sample prices for selected SKUs computed by the pricing engine for that account's context — without creating a dealer session, without any write capability, and with an audit event for every preview (07 §11 "view as dealer" is an audited sensitive action). - **API impact:** Implements API-M08-37; consumes the pricing engine/PriceSimulator.
- **Frontend impact:** P-E10 `#business` "View as dealer" read-only preview, only when enabled.
- **Backend impact:** Dealer preview via PriceSimulator; BR-M02-08 (audit of the preview); BR-M05-16 (private prices shown only to authorised staff).
- **Testing requirements:** Disabled: FEATURE_DISABLED and hidden action; enabled (read-only form): preview prices equal the engine result for the account context, no session or write is possible, each preview writes an audit event, only the roles of API-M08-37 may call it (TS-PERM-01 route mapping); TS-API-01 for API-M08-37.

#### T-1A.9-M05-01 · Quote service: basket quote with snapshot, versions and validity, server-derived context only (API-M05-01, API-M05-02; E-quote)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.9 / M05
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M10-01, T-1A.5-M05-02, T-1A.9-M12-01
- **Decisions:** D-154
- **References:** 06 §4.2 API-M05-01, API-M05-02, §1.4; 08 §4.15; 16 TS-API-09, TS-API-10; BP §8.1 step 8, §17.4; T10
- **Description:** Build M05 QuoteService: `POST /v1/quotes` (API-M05-01) and `GET /v1/quotes/{id}` (API-M05-02) per 06 §4.2. The server resolves buyer context (company, currency, channel, customer, verified business-account membership) and runs PricingEngine (T-1A.5-M05-02) through BP §8.1 steps 1–7 — contract → dealer list → public list, quantity tier, eligible promotions under the stacking policy (only if D-043 enables promotions), shipping and tax, margin/discount authority and serviceability — and locks an immutable, time-limited E-quote version whose validity window and "material change" rules come from D-154. Re-quotes with `previous_quote_id` return `material_changes[]` for explicit acceptance; a quote never reserves stock (BP §10.2) and never uses client-sent price, discount, tax, segment or channel (06 §1.4; T10). In scope: the `items[]` input; not in scope: `cart:true` (T-1A.9-M10-02), `draft_order_id` (T-1A.13-M10-01), minimum-order notices (T-1A.9-M05-02), dealer quote requests (T-1A.9-M05-03), coupon codes (T-1A.5-M05-04, D-043). The shipping/serviceability step calls M12 ServiceabilityService of T-1A.9-M12-01 in-process. Rules: BR-M05-01, -02, -03, -04, -05, -08, -09, -11, -12, -15, -16.
- **Files/components:** `backend/pricing/` QuoteService, BuyerContextResolver use and quote endpoints (finer structure per D-001/D-002); unit and service tests next to the code; contract tests with the `backend/` API tests.
- **Database impact:** Writes E-quote and E-quote_line (DB-G7, created by T-1A.9-M10-01); reads E-price_list, E-price_list_item, E-quantity_tier, E-price_rule_version, E-promotion, E-margin_floor, E-discount_authority, E-offer, E-business_account_member and E-shipping_charge_rule (only if D-162 creates it). No schema change, no seeds.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M05-01 and API-M05-02 (06 §3.4, §4.2) with errors VALIDATION_FAILED, NOT_SERVICEABLE, CONTEXT_INELIGIBLE, COUPON_INVALID (only with D-043), CHECKOUT_BLOCKED_PRICE_LIST and 410 QUOTE_EXPIRED; responses `private, no-store` (06 §1.11). Consumes ServiceabilityService (API-M12-01 logic) and PricingEngine in-process.
- **Frontend impact:** None (consumers: P-S06/P-S07 in T-1A.9-M09-07; P-S11 in T-1A.9-M05-03).
- **Backend impact:** QuoteService with BR-M05-04 steps 1–7 (step 8 revalidation is used by T-1A.9-M10-03); BR-M05-05 (never "largest discount wins" by default), BR-M05-09 (expired list → configured fallback or checkout blocked, never zero), BR-M05-11/-12 (quantity and location changes re-evaluated), BR-M05-15/-16 and BR-M02-13 (private prices isolated); rule trace stored in `pricing_explanation`; quote-expiry cleanup job sets `expired` (05 §5.5 Jobs).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-API-09 (BP §17.4 "Quote basket" guards), TS-API-10 (unit_price, discount, dealer_approved, segment and channel sent by the client are ignored and recomputed on API-M05-01), TS-API-07 (no-store header), TS-UNIT-01 (engine branches exercised through the quote), TS-PERM-02.2 (another customer's quote id → not found / CONTEXT_INELIGIBLE), TS-PERM-03.1; T10 (tampered price or buyer type recomputed), T02/T03 quote part (dealer tier only for a verified member; quantity crossing a threshold changes the unit price per D-018).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. API-M05-01 returns a versioned quote with lines, tier, promotions (if enabled), shipping, tax, totals, expires_at and rule versions per 06 §4.2, and creates no E-reservation.
  2. Client-sent price, discount, tax, segment, dealer flag and channel have no effect on the result (TS-API-10, T10).
  3. A re-quote with previous_quote_id returns material_changes[] and a new immutable version; earlier versions are unchanged.
  4. Expired or superseded quotes return 410 QUOTE_EXPIRED; the validity window is read from configuration per D-154, not hard-coded.
  5. An expired price list yields the configured fallback price or CHECKOUT_BLOCKED_PRICE_LIST — never a zero price.
  6. Guest, consumer and dealer callers receive only the prices of their authorised lists; every response is `private, no-store`.
  7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M10-01, T-1A.6-M06-02, T-1A.2-M17-02
- **Decisions:** D-031, D-161, D-072
- **References:** 05 §1.2, §5.6 BR-M06-05…07; 03 §2.5.3; 06 API-M06-24, API-M06-25; 16 TS-UNIT-05, TS-ERP-01, TS-ERP-07, TS-SVC-11; BP §9.2, §9.4, §10.3; A05, A06; T04
- **Description:** Build M06 ReservationService (A05, A06): reservation happens inside the single stock-authority transaction TX-1 that creates the pending order (called in-process by T-1A.9-M10-03): lock the (sku, location, owner) positions, compute ATP (BR-M06-02) and insert E-reservation `held` rows for all lines or none (BR-M06-05; BP §16.3). A unique advertised unit reserves that serial; otherwise quantity is reserved and a valid serial allocated at picking (BR-M06-07, D-031). Includes: states held → confirmed → consumed / released with release_reason; the A06 scheduled expiry job that releases unpaid holds and skips holds with a payment in progress (BR-M06-06; durations from S-13 configuration, D-026); staff extend-once-with-reason and release (API-M06-25, BR-M06-23); read API with holds, expiry-job runs, recent releases and durations by channel (API-M06-24); A05 shortage handling — accurate `STOCK_UNAVAILABLE` details, and an E-exception_case via the exception core (T-1A.2-M17-02) where a confirmed order cannot be allocated; stock authority unavailable → stop, never guess (BR-M06-17). Exposes the "controlled re-reservation" operation used by late capture (T-1A.10-M11-03) and line reallocation (T-1A.9-M10-04). When reservation happens in the web checkout (at "Place order" or at checkout entry with checkout-start holds on `quote_line_id`) is D-161; the P-E08 #reservations tab is T-1A.9-M06-02.
- **Files/components:** `backend/inventory/` ReservationService, A06 expiry job and reservation endpoints (finer structure per D-001/D-002); concurrency tests next to the code and in `tests/acceptance/` (T04).
- **Database impact:** E-reservation (DB-G7) rows and transitions; locks/reads E-stock_position; E-job_attempt per expiry run; E-exception_case for shortages; E-audit_event for manual extend/release; hold durations and extension limit read from E-configuration_version (S-13 loaded by T-1A.6-M06-10). `quote_line_id` holds only if D-161 selects checkout-start holds. No new entities.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M06-24 and API-M06-25 (Idem; 409 STATE_TRANSITION_INVALID). Provides the in-process reservation interface used by API-M10-06, API-M10-17, API-M11-01 and API-M11-03.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E08 #reservations in T-1A.9-M06-02).
- **Backend impact:** A05 (transactional reservation at confirmation; shortage queue) and A06 (scheduled expiry with payment-race safeguard) (05 §4); BR-M06-02, -05, -06, -07, -08 (no serial on two active reservations), -17, -23; TX-1 reservation part (05 §1.2); expired-reservation counts emitted as telemetry (05 §1.7).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-UNIT-05 (ATP formula incl. zero floor, excluded dispositions, serial vs quantity reservation, expiry, extension-with-reason), TS-ERP-01 (N parallel reservations on one unit → exactly one success, others STOCK_UNAVAILABLE with the accurate available quantity; stock authority down → 503), TS-ERP-07 (expiry releases unpaid holds, skips holds with an in-flight payment, one extension with reason), TS-SVC-11 (time-travel expiry cases), TS-SVC-01 (TX-1 fault injection: no reservation without its order and vice versa), TS-DB-03 (I-02); T04 (reservation part).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Of N concurrent reservation requests for the last unit exactly one succeeds in 100 % of runs; the others receive STOCK_UNAVAILABLE with the available quantity.
  2. A multi-line reservation reserves every line or none, in the same transaction as the pending order.
  3. Unique-unit offers reserve that serial; other offers reserve quantity only (per D-031 once decided).
  4. The expiry job releases expired unpaid holds, never releases a hold with a payment in progress, and records each run (E-job_attempt) and release reason.
  5. API-M06-25 extends a hold no more than the configured limit with a mandatory reason, releases with ATP restored, and audits both.
  6. With the stock authority unavailable no reservation or order is created and 503 STOCK_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE is returned.
  7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.9-M12-01 · Serviceability and delivery options: PIN serviceability, delivery methods, estimates and charges through the shipping adapter's serviceability function (API-M12-01)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **Description:** Build M12 ServiceabilityService and the serviceability function of the shipping adapter (M23 ShippingProviderPort; provider D-013) behind `GET /v1/serviceability` (API-M12-01): PIN format and serviceability, delivery options (standard, express, store pickup) with estimate and charge reference, split-shipment notice and — only where their decisions enable them — COD eligibility with reasons (D-020) and pickup locations (D-061). Methods, charges, free-delivery threshold and cut-off messaging come from versioned E-shipping_charge_rule rows if D-162 selects stored rules (else versioned configuration), never from mockup values (00 §1.1). - **Database impact:** Reads E-location (capabilities, BR-M03-04) and E-offer; creates E-shipping_charge_rule (DB-G3 conditional, 03 §2.22.13) and loads seed S-26 only if D-162 selects stored rules — otherwise charges are E-configuration_version keys; provider calls logged in E-integration_event.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M12-01 (06 §3.11; PUB/CUS, rate-limited per D-084). Used in-process by API-M05-01 (shipping step) and API-M10-06 (serviceability guard).
- **Frontend impact:** None (consumers: shell m-pin and P-S03 delivery line in T-1A.9-M09-06; P-S06/P-S07 in T-1A.9-M09-07).
- **Backend impact:** ServiceabilityService → ShippingProviderPort with timeouts and retries of the adapter framework (T-1A.2-M23-01; BR-M23-01…05); charge computed by rule version and recorded in the quote `price_versions`; split-shipment notice only when D-029 permits partial dispatch (BR-M12-14); BR-M12-13.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-05 (serviceability checked before payment; shipping totals clear), TS-INT-02 (serviceability subset: sandbox call, timeout, provider unavailable → 503), TS-API-01 (API-M12-01 contract incl. 422 with alternatives), TS-ECOM-14 (COD and pickup blocks absent while D-020/D-061 are not enabled), TS-AUTH-03 (rate limit on the public endpoint).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A serviceable PIN returns delivery options with estimate and a charge reference from the active rule/configuration version; an unserviceable PIN returns 422 NOT_SERVICEABLE with alternatives.
  2. A provider timeout or outage returns 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE; no estimate is invented.
  3. No charge, threshold, cut-off or method value is hard-coded; values come from D-162-approved rules or configuration (S-26 only with decided values).
  4. COD and pickup information appear only when D-020 / D-061 enable them.
  5. The adapter serviceability function passes its sandbox contract cases.

#### T-1A.9-M10-02 · Cart: lines, quantity changes, save for later, revalidated price/stock notices, guest-cart merge at sign-in (API-M10-01…05, API-M10-25; E-cart/E-cart_line only if server-side)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.9 / M10
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M10-01, T-1A.9-M05-01
- **Decisions:** D-129
- **References:** 08 §4.14; 06 API-M10-01…05; 03 §2.21.15, §2.21.16; 16 TS-ECOM-04; BP §6.3; T03
- **Description:** Implement cart persistence as decided in D-129. Server-side option: create E-cart/E-cart_line (DB-G7 conditional) and M10 CartService behind API-M10-01…05 and the guest-cart merge API-M10-25 — every read re-quotes through QuoteService (`cart:true` of API-M05-01) and discloses changes (price changed since added, quantity capped to availability with reason, offer no longer purchasable) (BP §6.3); quantity change recalculates the tier (BR-M05-11, T03); a guest cart uses a hashed cart token; merging at sign-in reprices with an explicit notice (BP §6.5). Client-held option: build the basket module in `frontend/storefront/` that persists across refreshes and survives a payment interruption (BR-M10-18), priced only through API-M05-01, and record API-M10-01…05/-25 as not built (D-213). Either way a cart never reserves stock and never stores an authoritative price (03 §2.21.15). "Save for later" (not reserved) only if D-129 approves that MOCKUP-ONLY part. Not in scope: the P-S06 page and shell cart count (T-1A.9-M09-07), minimum-order rules (T-1A.9-M05-02), coupons (D-043), quick-order lines (T-1A.9-M05-03).
- **Files/components:** Server option: `backend/orders/` CartService and cart endpoints; client option: `frontend/storefront/` basket module (finer structure per D-001/D-003); tests next to the code.
- **Database impact:** Server option: E-cart and E-cart_line migration (DB-G7 conditional; 03 §2.21.15–2.21.16) with unique guest_token_hash and (cart_id, offer_id, requested_serial_unit_id); `last_quote_id` → E-quote. Client option: none.
- **API impact:** Server option: implements API-M10-01, API-M10-02, API-M10-03, API-M10-04, API-M10-05, API-M10-25 (06 §3.9; 409 STOCK_UNAVAILABLE with the capped quantity). Both options consume API-M05-01.
- **Frontend impact:** Client option only: basket persistence module used by P-S06/P-S07 (UI in T-1A.9-M09-07). Server option: none.
- **Backend impact:** CartService (BR-M10-18, BR-M05-08; buyer context re-derived on every read so private prices disappear on sign-out or membership loss, BR-M02-13); advisory availability from the projection (BR-M06-18) — the authoritative check stays at order placement.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-04 (persistence across refresh, recovery after payment interruption, changed price/stock notices), TS-API-07 (cart responses private, no-store), TS-API-10 (client price ignored), TS-PERM-05.3 (membership loss reprices the cart with notice); T03 (tier recalculated when quantity crosses a threshold), T10.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. The D-129 option is implemented and the other option recorded as not built with the D-ID.
  2. Cart contents survive a page refresh and are available again after an interrupted payment.
  3. Each cart view shows engine prices from a fresh quote and lists every change since the item was added; no client-sent price is used.
  4. Guest-to-account merge (server option) reprices with an explicit notice; sign-out removes private prices from cart data.
  5. No cart operation creates an E-reservation.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.9-M10-03 · Order placement and read: revalidate quote and reserve atomically, idempotent create, separate order/payment/fulfilment/return states, order snapshots (API-M10-06…08)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.9 / M10
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M05-01, T-1A.9-M06-01, T-1A.9-M12-01
- **Decisions:** D-150
- **References:** 06 §4.3, §4.4 API-M10-06…08; 05 §5.10 BR-M10-*; 16 TS-API-03, TS-API-09, TS-ECOM-05, TS-ERP-01, TS-DB-03; BP §10.1–10.3, §17.5, §17.6; T04, T06, T10, T33
- **Description:** Build M10 CheckoutService and OrderQueryService. `POST /v1/orders` (API-M10-06, 06 §4.3): derive buyer context; check address ownership and quote scope, version and expiry; recompute totals (material difference → 409 PRICE_CHANGED with a new quote for explicit acceptance); validate offer approval, serviceability, membership/order limit and policy acknowledgements; then in one core transaction TX-1 create E-sales_order (`awaiting_payment`) with immutable line snapshots (price, rule version, condition, warranty/return policy versions) and all reservations via ReservationService, plus E-idempotency_record, E-audit_event and the `order_created` outbox row; no customer confirmation before payment verification (BP §6.3). Idempotency: same key and payload → stored response; different payload → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (T06). `GET /v1/orders/{id}` (API-M10-07, 06 §4.4) returns separate order, payment, fulfilment and return states, allowed_actions and the staff section by role; `GET /v1/orders` (API-M10-08) serves customer history, dealer organisation history and basic staff location-scoped lists. Not in scope: further state transitions, holds and staff work-queue views (T-1A.9-M10-04), cancellations (T-1A.9-M10-05), guest orders (T-1A.9-M10-06), `order_approval_id` (T-1A.9-M08-01), payment attempts (1A.10), COD (T-1A.10-M11-08). When the checkout calls API-M10-06 is D-161; order transitions not given by the sources are D-150.
- **Files/components:** `backend/orders/` CheckoutService, OrderQueryService and order endpoints (finer structure per D-001/D-002); acceptance tests in `tests/acceptance/` (T04, T06, T10, T33).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-sales_order, E-order_line, E-reservation (through M06), E-idempotency_record, E-outbox_operation, E-audit_event; reads E-quote, E-quote_line, E-address, E-offer, E-warranty_policy, E-return_policy, E-business_account_member. No schema change.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M10-06, API-M10-07 and API-M10-08 (base filters; staff `view` presets added by T-1A.9-M10-04) with the errors of 06 §4.3 (IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, STOCK_UNAVAILABLE with lines, PRICE_CHANGED, QUOTE_EXPIRED, NOT_SERVICEABLE, CONTEXT_INELIGIBLE, POLICY_ACK_REQUIRED, STOCK_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE). Consumes QuoteService revalidation and ReservationService in-process.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-S07 placement in T-1A.9-M09-07; P-S08/P-S09 in T-1A.9-M09-08; P-E02 in T-1A.9-M10-08).
- **Backend impact:** BR-M10-01, -02 (steps 1–2), -03, -04 (competing last unit, double click, same key different basket, stock system unavailable), -05, -06, -17; BR-M05-03; BR-M08-13; BR-M06-05, -17; TX-1; order transition `— → awaiting_payment` (05 §5.10); STOCK_UNAVAILABLE and PRICE_CHANGED counted for funnel metrics (05 §5.10 Logging).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-API-03 (API-M10-06 replay → same body; changed payload → 409), TS-API-09 (Place order and Read order guards of BP §17.4), TS-API-10 (§1.4 fields ignored), TS-ECOM-05 (pending order + atomic reservation; duplicate submission), TS-ERP-01 (two sessions buy the last unit), TS-DB-03 (I-01, I-02, I-06, I-07), TS-UNIT-06, TS-PERM-02.1 and TS-PERM-02.2 (foreign order, address or quote → not found / CONTEXT_INELIGIBLE), TS-ERR-01.1, TS-ERR-01.2, TS-ERR-01.3, TS-ERR-01.9; T04, T06 (order part), T10, T33 (order snapshot part).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A valid request creates one order in awaiting_payment with snapshots and reservations for every line in one transaction; a failed reservation leaves no order.
  2. Replaying the same idempotency key returns the stored response; a changed payload returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and the first order is unchanged (T06 order part).
  3. A price difference returns 409 PRICE_CHANGED with a new quote; an expired quote 410; a foreign address, quote or context is rejected without disclosure (TS-PERM-02.2).
  4. Two concurrent orders for the last unit: exactly one succeeds, the other receives STOCK_UNAVAILABLE (T04).
  5. API-M10-07 returns order, payment, fulfilment and return states as separate fields, responds `private, no-store`, and returns 404 to out-of-scope callers.
  6. Line snapshots (price, rule version, condition, policy versions) are unchanged after a later catalog or price change (T33 order part).
  7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.9-M10-04 · Order operations: state machine, holds with reason/owner/review date, reallocation of a line, bulk actions, staff order list (API-M10-13…15, API-M10-17)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.9 / M10
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M10-03
- **Decisions:** D-150
- **References:** 05 §5.10; 11 §8; 06 API-M10-13…15, API-M10-17; 16 TS-UNIT-04, TS-ERR-01; BP §10.1
- **Description:** Build M10 OrderService operations: the order state machine as an explicit transition table with guards (05 §5.10; rows marked D-150 stay disabled until D-150 is decided); holds and hold release (API-M10-14, API-M10-15) with mandatory reason_code, owner, review date and optional customer notification (BR-M10-16), each hold opening an E-exception_case; reallocation of a line to an alternate unit or location (API-M10-17) through ReservationService, with a customer consent reference required when unit or condition differs (BP §29.6; substitution never silent); bulk actions (API-M10-13) with independent per-order results — the `hold` action here, `release_to_fulfilment` and `assign` added by T-1A.11-M12-02 (needs DB-G8 fulfilment records), `payment_reminder` by T-1A.13-M20-04 (A28, conditional); staff work-queue views on API-M10-08 (`view` = needs_action, awaiting_payment, on_hold, partially_fulfilled, cancellation_requests; location, channel, buyer_type, payment_state and fulfilment_state filters; sla_flag, age, include_counts). Every transition is audited with actor and trigger; later events cannot move an order backwards into an unsafe state. Not in scope: cancellations (T-1A.9-M10-05), notes (T-1A.9-M10-07), P-E02 UI (T-1A.9-M10-08), SLA/deadline values (A16, D-138).

- **Database impact:** Updates E-sales_order (state, hold struct), E-reservation (via M06), E-exception_case (hold, stock exception), E-audit_event, E-outbox_operation (customer-notification intent). Hold reason codes from S-14 (D-139). No schema change.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M10-13 (`hold` action), API-M10-14, API-M10-15, API-M10-17 (Idem); extends API-M10-08 with staff views and filters (06 §3.9, §1.9).
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E02 in T-1A.9-M10-08).
- **Backend impact:** BR-M10-01, -15 (release guard reused by A11), -16; BR-M17-03 (exception fields) through the exception core; BR-M02-04 (location scope); 11 §8 override rule — no override sets price, stock or payment state from client input.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-UNIT-04 (every legal order transition passes and every illegal one is rejected; D-150 rows disabled), TS-ERR-01 (TS-ERR-01.9: stock authority unavailable during reallocation → 503; hold path used by late capture, TS-ERR-01.4, completed in 1A.10), TS-API-03 (API-M10-17 replay), TS-PERM-11 (location scope on staff views and actions), TS-PERM-02.6; module tests of 10 §7.10 (hold requires reason, owner and review date; bulk action returns per-order results).

  1. The transition table matches 05 §5.10; illegal transitions return 409 STATE_TRANSITION_INVALID; D-150 rows are not executable until D-150 is decided.
  2. A hold without reason_code, owner or review date is rejected; holds and releases are audited and open/close an exception record.

#### T-1A.9-M10-05 · Line cancellations with reservation release and discount allocation (API-M10-09)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.9 / M10
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M10-04
- **Decisions:** D-082, D-022
- **References:** 08 §4.20; 06 §4.5 API-M10-09; 16 TS-ECOM-07; BP §10.3; T34 (order part)
- **Description:** Build M10 CancellationService behind `POST /v1/orders/{id}/cancellations` (API-M10-09, 06 §4.5) for customers (own/org/GAT) and staff: a preview (`dry_run`) returns per-line eligibility, allocated refund (original line discount and tax allocation, BR-M05-13), reservation/stock effect and promotion/tier effect; execution runs in one core transaction TX-3 — E-order_cancellation, release of only the affected reservations (BR-M10-07), order state recomputed (all lines cancelled → cancelled) and, when payment was captured, one refund request for the allocated amount through the M11 refund hook (RefundService arrives with T-1A.10-M11-05; before 1A.10 no order is captured). Eligibility: line not dispatched (after dispatch the customer is pointed to returns), quantity ≤ open quantity, cancellation window per D-022; effect of a partial cancellation on tier prices per D-082 (no retroactive repricing without agreed policy, BR-M05-18). Customer reason `customer_request` with sub_reason (D-139); staff-only reasons need permission. Lines already in picking/packing become `requested` cancellations completed by the warehouse (set-aside in T-1A.11-M12-03). Not in scope: refund transitions (T-1A.10-M11-05), UI (T-1A.9-M09-08, T-1A.9-M10-08).
- **Files/components:** `backend/orders/` CancellationService and endpoint (finer structure per D-001/D-002); tests next to the code and in `tests/acceptance/` (T34 order part).
- **Database impact:** Writes E-order_cancellation (states requested/completed/rejected; tier_adjustment per D-082), E-order_line.qty_cancelled, E-reservation release (release_reason line_cancelled / order_cancelled), E-idempotency_record, E-audit_event, E-outbox_operation (fulfilment update, customer notification). No schema change.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M10-09 (Idem; errors 409 STATE_TRANSITION_INVALID, 422 POLICY_INELIGIBLE, 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; `dry_run` preview).
- **Frontend impact:** None.
- **Backend impact:** BR-M10-07, BR-M05-13, BR-M05-18 (D-082), BR-M10-04 (partial-cancellation row); TX-3; refund-request interface consumed by M11 RefundService.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-07 (only the affected reservation released; discount allocation; refund once), TS-ERR-01.12, TS-API-03 (repeat cancellation with the same key → same result), TS-UNIT-02 (allocation arithmetic), TS-UNIT-04 (order → cancelled when all lines are cancelled), TS-PERM-02.1 (cannot cancel another customer's order); T34 (order part), T06 (repeated request).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Cancelling one line releases only that line's reservation; other lines keep theirs (T34 order part).
  2. dry_run returns eligibility, allocated refund amount and stock effect without changing any record.
  3. Dispatched lines are rejected with 409 and a pointer to returns; quantities above the open quantity are rejected.
  4. The allocated refund uses the original line discount and tax allocation; the tier effect follows D-082 once decided.
  5. A repeated request with the same key returns the same cancellation without a second release or refund request.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.9-M09-04 · Storefront caching and private-data isolation: public vs private rendering, invalidation on approved changes, private no-store, purge on sign-out and membership loss
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.9 / M09
- **Depends on:** T-1A.3-M09-03, T-1A.5-M04-01
- **Decisions:** D-105
- **References:** 04a §1.3, §1.5; 02 §4.2; 06 §1.11; 16 TS-API-07, TS-FE-05, TS-PERM-05; BP §8.4, §16.5; T22
- **Description:** Implement the storefront caching mechanism chosen in D-105 across `frontend/storefront/`, the API layer and `infra/`: rendering class per page (04a §1.3; 02 §4.2) — public server-rendered/cacheable content for P-S01–P-S05, P-S13 and the P-S11 landing, private islands for dealer prices/tiers, saved PIN and dealer home modules, and fully private P-S06–P-S10 and dealer P-S11; `Cache-Control: private, no-store` on every response that depends on buyer context (06 §1.11); invalidation of public projections and pages after approved catalog, price or stock changes with version/timestamp (BR-M04-20, BR-M06-18, BR-M21-03); on sign-out and on membership loss all client-held private data (dealer prices, quotes, cart prices, orders, addresses) is discarded and pages refetch as guest (04a §1.4 rule 5; BR-M02-13); dealer-context HTML is never shared-cached or indexable (BR-M27-02). Record the cache policy in `frontend/storefront/` (stage documentation, 12 §6.10). Not in scope: SEO tags (T-1A.9-M27-01), analytics (T-1A.15-M09-01).
- **Files/components:** `frontend/storefront/` rendering/cache configuration and cache-policy document; response-header handling in `backend/platform/`; CDN/cache configuration in `infra/` if D-105 uses one (finer structure per D-001/D-003).
- **Database impact:** None.
- **API impact:** Applies cache headers to every storefront-facing endpoint (API-M04-03, API-M05-01, API-M05-04, API-M09-01, API-M10-01, API-M10-07, API-M10-08 and all `/v1/me/*` endpoints); consumes API-M02-06 (sign-out) and API-M02-01 (context).
- **Frontend impact:** Rendering class per page; private-island placeholders without layout shift; purge of private client data on sign-out and membership loss in the buyer-context provider.
- **Backend impact:** BR-M09-01, BR-M05-15, BR-M02-13, BR-M04-20; invalidation hooks on approved changes.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-API-07 (every CUS/GAT/LNK response private, no-store; public catalog cacheable), TS-FE-05 (sign-out purge; context rendering), TS-PERM-05.1, TS-PERM-05.2 (incl. CDN/shared cache) and TS-PERM-05.3 (membership loss), TS-SVC-09 (stale projection detectable after an approved change); T22.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. The D-105 mechanism is implemented and the cache policy documented in `frontend/storefront/`.
  2. After a dealer signs out, a guest on the same browser and through the shared cache sees no dealer price in HTML, API responses or client storage (T22).
  3. All buyer-context responses carry `private, no-store`; public pages are cacheable.
  4. An approved price or catalog change reaches public pages through the invalidation design and carries version/timestamp.
  5. A membership suspension removes dealer prices on the next request.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

### Stage 1A.9 addition — storefront read models and caching (D-268)

#### T-1A.9-M09-13 · Storefront read models, the five cache layers and per-route query budgets
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.9 / M09
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M09-04, T-1A.9-M09-06, T-1A.3-M09-07, T-1A.4-M32-01
- **Decisions:** D-105, D-034
- **References:** 19 §25.3, §25.4; DEC D-268, D-105; BP §16.5, §20.1; 04a
- **Description:** Make the public storefront fast on real data. Build the product and category read models so a page is served from a maintained projection rather than an eight-table join, and invalidate them on catalog, price and configuration publication. Implement the five cache layers of 19 §25.4 with their exact key composition — every key contains the store, and buyer-context class separates public from dealer pricing so private prices can never be served from a shared cache. Add stampede protection on every expensive rebuild. Assert a maximum query count per storefront route with a query recorder, so an N+1 introduced later fails the test rather than the customer.
- **Files/components:** `backend/<catalog module>/projections/`, `backend/platform/cache/`, storefront route instrumentation
- **Database impact:** Read-model tables or materialised projections per store, invalidated on write and publish
- **API impact:** Cache-control and revalidation headers per route (06 §1)
- **Frontend impact:** P-S01, P-S02, P-S03 served from projections
- **Backend impact:** ProjectionBuilder, CacheKey composition, stampede protection
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-ISO-20 (no cache key without a store; dealer price never served from a public cache entry), TS-PERF-01 (route budgets), TS-SAAS-PERF-09 (query count per route), TS-CACHE (invalidation on publish and on write, stampede protection)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Home, category and product pages are served from projections and meet the 19 §25.2 storefront budgets at realistic volumes. (2) Every cache key contains the store and the buyer-context class; a test proves a dealer price is never returned from a guest cache entry. (3) Publishing catalog, price or configuration changes invalidates exactly the affected entries, verified. (4) Each storefront route has a declared maximum query count asserted in its test. (5) A simulated stampede rebuilds once, not once per request. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

## Stage 1A.10 — Payments & reconciliation

#### T-1A.10-M23-01 · Payment provider adapter: hosted collection session, status query, refund and refund status, webhook signature verification, sandbox contract tests
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.10 / M23
- **Depends on:** T-1A.2-M23-01
- **Decisions:** D-012
- **References:** 05 §5.11, §5.23; 02 §18; 16 TS-INT-01; BP §10.6, §16.4
- **Description:** Build the PaymentProviderAdapter in M23 for the single launch provider chosen in D-012 (BP §10.6; BR-M23-03) behind the M11 PaymentProviderPort: create the hosted/approved collection order or session (the application never handles card data, BR-M11-10), payment status query, refund creation with a deterministic idempotency reference (refund id + attempt number), refund status query, raw-body webhook signature verification, and settlement-report retrieval only if D-064 selects an API method. Every call runs through the adapter framework of T-1A.2-M23-01 (timeouts, retries through the outbox, E-integration_event logging, sandbox/production separation), and the integration contract checklist of BP §16.4 (authentication, mapping, source of truth, external ids, event schema/version, retries, timeouts, rate limits, idempotency, reconciliation, support owner, fallback) is completed and stored with the adapter (stage documentation, 12 §6.11). Payment modes (UPI, cards, net banking; EMI only with D-062; COD separately under D-020) are configuration. Not in scope: attempt, webhook and refund business logic (T-1A.10-M11-01…05).
- **Files/components:** `backend/integrations/` payment adapter and its contract checklist; sandbox contract tests in `backend/integrations/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002).
- **Database impact:** E-integration_setting records per environment (from S-18, T-1A.2-M24-02); E-integration_event for calls and raw payload references. No schema change.
- **API impact:** None directly; serves API-M11-01, API-M11-02, API-M11-03, API-M11-06, API-M11-10, API-M11-11, API-M11-12 and API-M11-22 through the M11 services.
- **Frontend impact:** None.
- **Backend impact:** PaymentProviderPort operations create_session, get_payment_status, create_refund, get_refund_status, verify_signature (+ settlement fetch per D-064); BR-M23-01, -02 (payment minimum behaviour and reconciliation fallback), -04, -05; secrets per D-107; payment data and secrets never logged (BR-M02-11; 02 §18.3).

#### T-1A.10-M11-01 · Hosted payment flow end to end: payment options for the order, create/reuse payment attempt, server-verified payment status, P-S07 payment step and P-S08 payment status/retry (API-M11-01, API-M11-02, API-M11-22)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.10 / M11
- **Depends on:** T-1A.10-M23-01, T-1A.9-M10-03, T-1A.9-M09-07
- **Decisions:** D-150
- **References:** 06 §4.7 API-M11-01, API-M11-02; 08 §4.18; 04a §4.7 (step 3), §4.8; 16 TS-API-03, TS-FE-08, TS-ECOM-05; BP §10.2; T06
- **Description:** Build M11 PaymentAttemptService and the customer payment surfaces. `POST /v1/orders/{id}/payment-attempts` (API-M11-01, 06 §4.7): the order must be awaiting_payment with an active reservation (expired → controlled re-reservation through ReservationService, else 409 RESERVATION_EXPIRED); a still-valid attempt is reused and a second concurrent payment is blocked; the amount is always the server's order payable; the attempt record and outbox row are written in the transaction and the provider session is created outside it (timeout → attempt `pending` + reconciliation). `GET /payment-status` (API-M11-02) is server-verified with a rate-limited provider query while pending — never a false success (BR-M10-09, BR-M11-02). `GET /payment-options` (API-M11-22) lists methods from the provider configuration (COD block added by T-1A.10-M11-08; EMI plans and saved tokens by T-1A.10-M09-01). Frontend: P-S07 step 3 payment tabs (UPI, card, net banking per D-012 — provider names in the mockup are samples), failed-payment banner (reason, no double charge, retry or change method), processing overlay and hand-off to the provider's hosted page, return and status polling (mechanism D-146); P-S08 "payment verified" confirmation, "verification pending" (don't pay again, check status now, reserved until) and failed-after-return with retry; P-S11 "Pay now" for dealer orders awaiting payment (bank-transfer instructions only if D-012/D-019 enable that route). Payment-attempt transitions not given by the sources (authorised → expired/void) are D-150.
- **Files/components:** `backend/payments/` PaymentAttemptService and payment endpoints; `frontend/storefront/` P-S07 payment step, P-S08 payment states, P-S11 pay-now (finer structure per D-001/D-003); `tests/e2e/` payment flows.
- **Database impact:** Writes E-payment_attempt, E-idempotency_record, E-outbox_operation, E-audit_event; reads E-sales_order, E-reservation, E-configuration_version. No schema change.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M11-01 (Idem; errors RESERVATION_EXPIRED, STATE_TRANSITION_INVALID, METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT), API-M11-02 and API-M11-22 (provider methods only).
- **Frontend impact:** P-S07 section 6 (payment tabs, failed banner) and section 9 (processing overlay); P-S08 sections 2a and 3 and the payment-failed state; P-S11 overview "Pay now".
- **Backend impact:** BR-M11-01, -02, -10, -11; BR-M10-02 steps 3–4, BR-M10-09; attempt transition created → pending (05 §5.11).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-API-03 (API-M11-01 replay returns the same attempt), TS-FE-08 (single submit of pay; the status page shows only the server-verified state), TS-ECOM-05 (payment attempt, verification pending, no false success, duplicate submission), TS-INT-01 (session creation against the sandbox), TS-FE-06 (RESERVATION_EXPIRED, PROVIDER_PENDING, METHOD_NOT_AVAILABLE rendering); T06 (repeated order request and double-click pay → one order, one attempt).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. An awaiting-payment order gets one attempt; a repeated request reuses it; a second concurrent payment is blocked.
  2. The attempt amount always equals the server's order payable; client amounts are ignored.
  3. P-S08 never shows "confirmed" before provider-verified capture; a pending payment shows the verification-pending state.
  4. An expired reservation is re-reserved if possible, otherwise RESERVATION_EXPIRED is shown with "Re-check & reserve again".
  5. Card data never reaches the storefront or backend; collection happens on the provider's hosted/approved method.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.10-M11-02 · Webhook processing A09: raw-body signature, persist and deduplicate on provider event id, out-of-order handling, captured never downgraded, single fulfilment release; event log (API-M11-03, API-M11-07)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.10 / M11
- **Depends on:** T-1A.10-M11-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 06 §4.7 API-M11-03, API-M11-07, §1.8; 05 §5.11; 16 TS-API-06, TS-INT-01, TS-UNIT-09; BP §10.2, §10.3; A09; T07, T08
- **Description:** Build M11 PaymentWebhookHandler (A09) behind `POST /v1/webhooks/payment-provider` (API-M11-03; 06 §4.7, §1.8): verify the raw-body signature before parsing (failure → 401 SIGNATURE_INVALID, security log only); deduplicate on the provider event id (duplicate → 200 `duplicate`, no effect); store E-payment_event with the raw payload reference; apply only legal E-payment_attempt transitions (created/pending → authorised/captured/failed/expired; authorised → captured) and never downgrade a captured payment (`ignored_out_of_order`); on capture apply TX-2 — order awaiting_payment with an active reservation → confirmed, reservation → confirmed allocation, and outbox follow-ups (fulfilment release consumed by A11 in 1A.11, customer notification by A14 in 1A.13, invoice step per D-055) keyed so that a duplicated callback gives one fulfilment release and no duplicate invoice (BR-M11-03, BR-M19-04). An amount/currency mismatch or unknown attempt is stored and raises a payment-review E-exception_case. Refund events update E-refund once RefundService exists (T-1A.10-M11-05). The handler acknowledges quickly; heavy work runs through the outbox. Also `GET /v1/payment-events` (API-M11-07) with raw payloads only for permitted roles. Capture after reservation expiry is T-1A.10-M11-03.
- **Files/components:** `backend/payments/` PaymentWebhookHandler and event-log endpoint (finer structure per D-001/D-002); fault-injection tests next to the code.
- **Database impact:** Writes E-payment_event (append-only; unique (provider, provider_event_id)), E-integration_event (raw), E-payment_attempt, E-sales_order, E-reservation (state confirmed), E-outbox_operation, E-exception_case. No schema change.
- **API impact:** Implements API-M11-03 (SIG) and API-M11-07.
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E12 #events in T-1A.10-M11-09).
- **Backend impact:** A09; BR-M11-01, -02, -03, -04, -06 (unmatched events → exception); BR-M23-05; TX-2; captured-state guard (03 §5.4).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-API-06 (raw-body signature before parsing; duplicate → no effect; out-of-order → legal transitions only; forged event rejected), TS-INT-01 (duplicate and out-of-order events from the sandbox), TS-UNIT-09 (provider event → payment transition mapping table), TS-UNIT-04 (payment-attempt transitions; captured never downgraded), TS-PERM-04.4 (forged or unsigned event → 401, no effect, logged), TS-SVC-01 (TX-2 fault injection), TS-ERR-01.5, TS-ERR-01.6; T07 (payment-effect part), T08.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A duplicated capture callback produces one payment transition, one order confirmation and one fulfilment-release outbox row (T07 payment effect).
  2. A failed event arriving after capture is stored as ignored_out_of_order and the payment stays captured (T08).
  3. An event with an invalid signature is rejected with 401 and changes nothing.
  4. Every received event is stored once with its processing result; raw payloads are visible only to permitted roles in API-M11-07.
  5. An amount mismatch or unknown attempt raises a payment-review exception instead of confirming the order.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.10-M11-03 · Payment after reservation expiry: re-reserve if possible, otherwise visible exception and refund path
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.10 / M11
- **Depends on:** T-1A.10-M11-02, T-1A.9-M06-01, T-1A.2-M17-02
- **Decisions:** D-026
- **References:** 05 §5.11; 16 TS-ERP-07, TS-E2E-06; BP §10.3, §29.6; T09
- **Description:** Implement the late-capture path of BP §10.3 / §29.6 (BR-M11-05) with the D-026 policy: when a verified capture arrives for an order whose reservation expired or was released, attempt a controlled re-reservation through ReservationService (T-1A.9-M06-01); success → the order is confirmed as normal (TX-2); failure → the payment is recorded, the order goes `on_hold` and one E-exception_case "payment captured without stock" is raised (owner and due time per D-138) with the documented resolution paths — reserve an alternate unit/location with customer consent (API-M10-17), offer an alternative, or refund (API-M11-09) — never negative stock or oversell (I-02). Also covers the pre-payment path of API-M11-01 (expired reservation → re-reserve or RESERVATION_EXPIRED) and the interplay with the A06 expiry job (holds with a payment in progress are skipped). Surfaces: P-S08 "on hold" explanation with a support route (04a §4.8), P-E02 exception callout "Payment captured after reservation expiry" with Reserve alternate / Refund, P-E12 d-pay exception callout. The owner-control-centre view (T09 "visible exception") completes in 1A.14 (T-1A.14-M17-12).
- **Files/components:** `backend/payments/` late-capture handling; `backend/inventory/` re-reservation call; `frontend/storefront/` P-S08 on-hold state; `frontend/workspace/` P-E02 exception callout (finer structure per D-001/D-003); `tests/e2e/` TS-E2E-06.
- **Database impact:** E-payment_attempt, E-sales_order (on_hold with hold reason), E-reservation, E-exception_case (late_capture_stock_conflict), E-audit_event. No schema change.
- **API impact:** Extends the processing of API-M11-03 and the guard of API-M11-01; consumes API-M10-17 and API-M11-09 for resolution; the exception queue actions API-M17-05/-07 arrive with T-1A.14-M17-05 (until then resolution is recorded through the exception core of T-1A.2-M17-02).
- **Frontend impact:** P-S08 on-hold state; P-E02 `d-order` exception callout; P-E12 `d-pay` exception callout text (policy text D-026).
- **Backend impact:** BR-M11-05, BR-M06-06, BR-M17-03; TX-2 alternate path; no automatic refund unless the D-026 policy says so.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-07 (capture after expiry → re-reserve or exception/refund path), TS-E2E-06 steps 1–4 (the P-E01 part runs in 1A.14), TS-ERR-01.4, TS-DB-03 (I-02 no negative sellable allocation), TS-SVC-11 (time travel: the hold expires before capture); T09 (payment path).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. The D-026 policy is recorded; durations and resolution rules come from configuration.
  2. A capture after expiry with stock still available re-reserves and confirms the order.
  3. A capture after expiry without stock records the payment, puts the order on hold and raises exactly one exception with owner and due time; stock is never oversold.
  4. Staff can resolve by reserving an alternate with consent or by requesting a refund; the resolution is audited.
  5. The customer sees an on-hold explanation, never a false confirmation.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A refund request above the refundable amount returns 422 AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_REFUNDABLE.
  2. The requester cannot approve their own refund; bank-transfer refunds need a second finance user for check & release.

  4. After a provider timeout the refund is pending and a retry is refused until a status check says safe_to_retry (T19).
  5. Cancelling a captured line creates exactly one refund request for the allocated amount (T34 refund part).

- **Description:** Build M12 FulfilmentQueueService (A11): a subscriber to the order-confirmation outbox events (capture from T-1A.10-M11-02, confirmed offline payments, COD if enabled) releases eligible orders — confirmed or approved and reserved, not on hold, no pending cancellation (BR-M10-15, BR-M12-02) — into location-scoped warehouse queues by creating E-fulfilment and E-fulfilment_line rows (reservation linked; serial allocated now for unit-specific reservations, at picking otherwise per D-031). #### T-1A.11-M12-03 · Pick, scan verification (bin → SKU → serial against allocation), pick exceptions and pack with checklist, parcels and evidence (API-M12-07…09)

- **Description:** Build M12 PickService and PackService. Scan verification `POST /fulfilments/{id}/scans` (API-M12-07): bin → SKU → serial against the allocation using the scanning conventions of D-110 (T-1A.6-M03-01); results ok, wrong_unit, wrong_bin, not_found, duplicate; the serial must equal the allocated unit or be a valid sellable unit of the same SKU/condition (D-031); a serial on another active fulfilment is rejected (BR-M06-08); a different configuration or condition is never substituted at the bench (BR-M12-05); every scan stored in E-fulfilment_scan, unknown scans change nothing. Pick exceptions (API-M12-08): short pick → count task (API-M06-19) + exception; park line; set aside a cancel-requested line (completing the requested cancellation of T-1A.9-M10-05); mis-slot → recount (A24). Transitions (API-M12-09, Idem): complete_pick only when every line is verified; mark_packed with the packing checklist (serial re-verified, condition matches the listing, accessories, data-erasure evidence for storage devices via API-M06-10, inspection sheet, warranty card, invoice, packaging, weight, packed-box photo) creating E-fulfilment_parcel and enqueuing courier booking (A13) through the outbox. Serial and inspection record are set on the fulfilment line (BR-M12-04). Not in scope: scale/camera/ printer integration (T-1A.11-M12-10), documents (T-1A.11-M19-01), booking (T-1A.11-M12-04), dispatch (T-1A.11-M12-05).

No schema change.

- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E03 in T-1A.11-M12-11).
- **Backend impact:** BR-M12-01, -03, -04, -05, -12; BR-M06-08, BR-M06-16; fulfilment transitions allocated → picking → packed (picking → allocated/unallocated after a short pick is D-150).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-10 (scan verifies location/SKU/serial against the allocation; substitution flagged; packed only with a complete checklist), TS-ERP-03 (no serial on two active fulfilments), TS-UNIT-04 (fulfilment transitions), TS-API-03 (API-M12-09 replay); T17 (serial-linkage part); BP §30.2 "dispatch the correct serial" (pick/pack part).

  1. A wrong unit, wrong bin or different-condition scan is rejected with the expected-vs-scanned comparison and changes nothing.

- **Frontend impact:** None (template screens have no mockup — D-004; P-S08, P-S09, P-E02 and P-E03 surfaces are in T-1A.11-M09-01 and T-1A.11-M12-11).
- **Backend impact:** A12; BR-M19-02, -04, -05, -08; BR-M12-12 (documents from approved templates with serial verification).

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. D-055, D-111 and D-008 recorded.
