## Stage 1A.15 — Reporting & finance export

#### T-1A.15-M18-01 · Report service and catalogue: versioned definitions with event-date basis, gross/net and tax labels, freshness labels, branch scope, restricted column groups (API-M18-01, API-M18-02, API-M18-17, API-M18-18)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.15 / M18
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M09-01, T-1A.2-M02-02
- **Decisions:** D-197
- **References:** 10 §13; 05 §5.18; 06 API-M18-01, API-M18-02; 16 TS-UNIT-11, TS-ERP-19, TS-PERM-11; BP §14.3, §14.4
- **Description:** Build the M18 ReportService and report catalogue (BP §14.3, §14.4; 10 §13; 05 §5.18): catalogue filtered by the caller's permission and group (API-M18-01); report run with explicit event-date basis (order, payment, invoice, dispatch, settlement), period, location, channel, buyer type, condition, category, tax basis (incl./excl.), group-by and drill, returning KPIs, series, table, the definition text and version, per-source freshness and failed feeds (API-M18-02; BR-M18-02, BR-M18-03); versioned report definitions (event-date basis, gross vs net, tax basis, refund-period treatment) with history (API-M18-17) and new versions proposed with finance approval before use (API-M18-18 → API-M17-03; BR-M18-10). Supplier cost, personal data and margin column groups only for authorised roles (BR-M18-04; D-197); branch managers see their branch, cross-branch per D-029 (BR-M18-09); test traffic, duplicate events and verification-transaction orders are excluded (BR-M18-07); gross margin is labelled as not a statutory P&L (BR-M18-08). Reports run read-only on operational data; a read replica or report store only when measured need triggers it (BP §28.5). Not in scope: the individual launch reports (T-1A.15-M18-02), exports (T-1A.15-M18-03), schedules (T-1A.15-M18-04), saved views (T-1A.15-M18-05), P-E13 UI (T-1A.15-M18-07).
- **Files/components:** `backend/reporting/` (ReportService, report-definition registry, column-group permission filter, freshness tracker); tests in `backend/reporting/` and `tests/acceptance/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002)
- **Database impact:** None new — report definitions as E-configuration_version (versioned, approved), E-approval_request (definition approvals); reads operational entities listed for API-M18-02 (E-sales_order, E-order_line, E-refund, E-stock_position, E-stock_movement, E-payment_attempt, E-settlement_record, E-return_request, E-job_attempt, E-approval_request, E-audit_event)
- **API impact:** Implements API-M18-01, API-M18-02, API-M18-17, API-M18-18 (`202 {version, approval_request_id}`); consumes API-M17-03 for the finance approval
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E13 in T-1A.15-M18-07)
- **Backend impact:** Report registry where each report declares its sources, allowed filters, column groups with required permissions and its current definition version; date-basis handling per D-124 business day; per-source `as_of` and failed-feed detection from job runs (E-job_attempt); definition changes never apply before approval; rules BR-M18-01…BR-M18-04, BR-M18-07…BR-M18-10
- **Testing requirements:** TS-UNIT-11 (distinct event dates, gross/net, tax-inclusive/exclusive labels), TS-ERP-19 (definitions, event-date basis, freshness labels, branch scope, restricted columns), TS-PERM-11.2 (branch-scoped reports), TS-PERM-10.3 (cost/margin columns absent for unauthorised roles), TS-PERM-08.1 (definition proposer cannot approve), TS-API-01, TS-REG-02 for M18
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. API-M18-01 returns only reports the caller may run; restricted reports are absent for other roles.
  2. API-M18-02 requires an explicit date basis, labels gross/net and tax basis, returns the definition version and per-source freshness, and lists failed feeds.
  3. A branch manager receives only own-branch rows; filters outside scope are ignored or refused.
  4. Cost, margin and personal-data column groups are omitted unless the caller holds the D-197 permission.
  5. A new definition version is not used until finance approves it; history shows version, approver and date.
  6. Verification-transaction orders and duplicate events never appear in report totals.
  7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.15-M18-02 · Launch report set (sales & returns by branch, stock and valuation extracts, payments, fulfilment, returns, automation health) per the approved list
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.15 / M18
- **Depends on:** T-1A.15-M18-01, T-1A.15-M09-01
- **Decisions:** D-075, D-135
- **References:** 10 §13.2; 16 TS-ERP-19; BP §14.3; R14; WP15
- **Description:** Implement the launch report set approved under D-075 on the ReportService (BP §14.3; 10 §13.2; R14; WP15). Candidates from the sources: sales and returns (date, channel, branch, buyer type, category, condition — incl. "by branch"), stock position, stock ageing, low stock, order ageing, payment reconciliation, gross margin (finance/owner; not a statutory P&L), returns and warranty, automation health, customer funnel (data from T-1A.15-M09-01, D-106), audit export (→ P-E15 `#audit`), inventory extract for the accountant (meaning of BP §14.1 "inventory extracts" is D-075) and branch comparison (BP §30.1). Stock value, valuation and margin figures use the cost valuation method of D-135. Each report gets a finance-approved definition (event-date basis, gross/net, tax basis, refund treatment), its filters, column groups and restrictions, and is reconciled with sample transactions before publication (BP §22.5 "For reports, include definitions and reconciled totals"; 16 §15.2 D6). Vendor performance and approval ageing are 1B (MK; D-192) and not built here. Not in scope: exports, schedules, UI.
- **Files/components:** `backend/reporting/` (one report definition/query module per approved report), definition texts recorded as configuration versions; reconciliation fixtures in `tests/acceptance/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002)
- **Database impact:** None new — definitions as E-configuration_version; reads per report as listed in 10 §13.2 (E-invoice_reference, E-order_line, E-return_line, E-refund, E-stock_position, E-reservation, E-stock_movement, E-serial_unit, E-reorder_rule, E-purchase_order_line, E-sales_order, E-payment_attempt, E-fulfilment, E-settlement_record, E-return_request, E-warranty_case, E-job_attempt, E-automation_rule, E-audit_event)
- **API impact:** None new — each report is served by API-M18-01/-02 (T-1A.15-M18-01); audit export uses API-M02-30
- **Frontend impact:** None (rendered by P-E13 in T-1A.15-M18-07)
- **Backend impact:** Report queries with explicit denominators and exclusions (test traffic, duplicates, verification transactions; BR-M18-07); automation-health report from E-job_attempt runs, errors, age and retry counts (BP §14.3) with hours saved labelled as estimates (D-193); gross-margin report restricted and labelled (BR-M18-08, BR-M11-18); rules BR-M18-01, BR-M18-02, BR-M18-04, BR-M18-07
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-19 (launch report set definitions, event-date basis, freshness, branch scope, restricted columns, totals reconcile with sample transactions), TS-UNIT-11 per launch report definition, TS-PERM-10.3, TS-REG-02 for M18
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Exactly the D-075 reports are published; each has an approved definition version with approver and date.
  2. For a seeded sample of transactions, each report's totals reconcile with the source records (documented reconciliation per report).
  3. Stock value and margin figures state the D-135 valuation basis; gross margin carries the "not a statutory P&L" label and is visible only to permitted roles.
  4. Reports marked 1B (vendor performance, approval ageing) are not in the catalogue.
  5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.15-M18-03 · Export jobs and secure downloads for lists/reports incl. dealer private price-list export: row limits, expiring audited links, restricted columns, formula neutralisation, job isolation (API-M18-03…05, API-M05-05)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.15 / M18
- **Depends on:** T-1A.15-M18-01, T-1A.1-M17-01, T-1A.8-M08-06
- **Decisions:** D-152
- **References:** 06 API-M18-03…05, API-M05-05, §1.12; 16 TS-SVC-10, TS-SEC-10, TS-PERF-05; BP §14.4, §20.2; T35
- **Description:** Build export jobs and secure downloads for every list and report (BP §14.4 "row limits, secure download expiry, and audit history"; §20.2; 06 §1.12): ExportService creates a background job for a dataset (report key or list: orders, catalog, stock snapshot, stock ledger, audit log, price lists, customers masked/full, payment ledger, reconciliation report, PO register, RMA list, quantity tiers, unit lifecycle, dealer accounts & price lists) with filters, permitted column groups, CSV/XLSX and an optional row-count estimate (API-M18-03); lists own/team exports (API-M18-04); serves expiring, audited downloads (API-M18-05, `410 LINK_EXPIRED`); personal-data or cost columns need permission and full personal-data exports become approval requests (`data_export`; BP §18.1); every cell neutralises spreadsheet formula injection (BR-M18-05); jobs run on isolated worker capacity so large exports never starve checkout (BR-M18-06; T35). Add the dealer's private price-list export, watermarked with the account and audited (API-M05-05). Row limits, link expiry, approval datasets and watermarking are D-152 values. Wire the shared "Export" action pattern (04b §2.20 #2) into the existing P-E screens and P-S11 `#pricelist` "XLSX". Not in scope: P-E13 `m-export` and `#exports` (T-1A.15-M18-07), invoice ZIP and GST export endpoints (T-1A.15-M19-02, which reuse this service).
- **Files/components:** `backend/reporting/` (ExportService, export worker pool, formula-neutralising writers), `backend/pricing/` (price-list export dataset), private file storage through `backend/files/`; `frontend/workspace/` Export action on P-E01, P-E02, P-E04, P-E06, P-E07, P-E08, P-E09, P-E10, P-E12, P-E15 `#audit`; `frontend/storefront/` P-S11 `#pricelist` "XLSX"; tests in `backend/reporting/`, `tests/security/`, `tests/load/` (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** None new — E-export_job (DB-G10: filters, field groups, includes_personal_data, purpose, approval_request_id, row_count/row_limit, state, file, download_expires_at, downloads), E-approval_request (`data_export`), E-attachment (private file), E-audit_event
- **API impact:** Implements API-M18-03 (`Idem`; `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED`; `422 ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`), API-M18-04, API-M18-05, API-M05-05
- **Frontend impact:** "Export" buttons on the listed P-E screens create a job for the current filters/selection and show "export queued" and where the file appears; P-S11 `#pricelist` "XLSX" shows the watermark/confidentiality notice; `APPROVAL_REQUIRED` rendered as sent for approval
- **Backend impact:** Column groups checked against permissions (D-197, BR-M08-12); row limit enforced before generation; files stored privately and served only through API-M18-05 with expiry and a download audit record; formula neutralisation for CSV and XLSX; worker isolation (separate queue/capacity) from checkout workers; export filters intersected with caller scope; rules BR-M18-04, BR-M18-05, BR-M18-06, BR-M08-12
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SVC-10 (row limits, expiring audited downloads, restricted columns, isolation), TS-SEC-10 (formula cells neutralised in every export), TS-UNIT-11 (formatting), TS-API-08 (202 + job reference, expiring download), TS-PERM-02.9 (another user's export → `404`), TS-PERM-10.3 (cost/margin columns), TS-PERF-05 staging check (export during checkout; formal T35 measurement in T-1A.17-M26-04), TS-REG-02 for M18, M05
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. An export over the D-152 row limit is refused with `422 ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (or queued as the documented background job); within the limit it produces a file with the permitted column groups only.
  2. A full personal-data export returns `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` and generates nothing until approved.
  3. Every cell beginning with a formula trigger character is neutralised in CSV and XLSX output.
  4. Download links expire at the D-152 time and return `410 LINK_EXPIRED` afterwards; each download writes an audit record; another user's export returns `404`.
  5. The dealer price-list export contains only the caller's account prices, carries the account watermark and is audited.
  6. Running a large export on staging during checkout leaves checkout functional with no timeouts attributable to the export (TS-PERF-05 staging check).
  7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.15-M18-04 · Report schedules and scheduled digests with test run and run history; seed S-19 (API-M18-06…10; E-report_schedule)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.15 / M18
- **Depends on:** T-1A.15-M18-01, T-1A.13-M20-01
- **Decisions:** D-075
- **References:** 06 API-M18-06…10; 03 §2.16.2, §6 S-19; 16 TS-ERP-19
- **Description:** Build report schedules and scheduled digests (PR1 §10 "Scheduled daily/weekly management reports"; BP §14.1, §14.4; 04c §6.5): ReportScheduleService lists, creates, edits, pauses/resumes schedules of a report or saved view with frequency, time, recipients, format, stale-data behaviour (send with warning / hold and retry / skip), skip-if-empty and "raise one exception on failure" (API-M18-06…08); sends a test run to a named recipient (API-M18-09) and keeps run history with delivery results (API-M18-10). Recipients must be authorised for the report and receive it with their own record scope; delivery is an expiring secure link through M20 email, never a raw attachment with personal data (04c §6.5); failed delivery retries and then raises exactly one exception (`report_delivery_failure`; BR-M17-11). External recipients (e.g. an external accountant) are supported only if D-075 includes scheduled files to accountants/suppliers. Load S-19 with the decided launch schedules (D-075); the owner-digest schedule row is configured through API-M17-26 (T-1A.14-M17-09, D-063). Not in scope: P-E13 `#schedules` UI (T-1A.15-M18-07).
- **Files/components:** `backend/reporting/` (ReportScheduleService, schedule runner job), S-19 seed in `backend/`; tests in `backend/reporting/` and `tests/acceptance/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002)
- **Database impact:** None new — E-report_schedule (DB-G10; saved_view_id, frequency, recipients, external_recipients, delivery_channels, format, stale_data_behaviour, skip_if_empty, raise_exception_on_failure, state, last/next run), E-job_attempt (runs), E-export_job (generated files), E-notification, E-exception_case; seed S-19 (values D-075, D-063)
- **API impact:** Implements API-M18-06, API-M18-07, API-M18-08, API-M18-09, API-M18-10; uses ExportService (T-1A.15-M18-03) and NotificationService in-process
- **Frontend impact:** None (P-E13 `#schedules`, `m-schedule` in T-1A.15-M18-07)
- **Backend impact:** Scheduler honours the business timezone (D-124) and the automation pause state (non-critical pause stops digests, T-1A.14-M17-04); per-recipient scope applied at generation; stale behaviour evaluated from report freshness; retries then one exception; rules BR-M18-03, BR-M18-05, BR-M17-11, BR-M17-12
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-19 (schedules deliver reconciled reports with freshness), TS-SVC-05 (delivery through M20), TS-SVC-11 (time-travel runs), TS-ERR-06 (delivery failure → one exception), TS-DB-05 (S-19), TS-API-01, TS-REG-02 for M18
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A schedule can only list recipients authorised for its report; each recipient's file is limited to their record scope.
  2. Deliveries are expiring secure links; no raw attachment with personal data is sent.
  3. Stale data follows the chosen behaviour (warning, hold and retry, or skip) and the run history shows it.
  4. A failed delivery is retried and then raises exactly one exception; the run history records the error.
  5. A test run reaches only the named recipient; pause and resume change `next_run`.
  6. S-19 loads only decided schedules; external recipients exist only if D-075 includes them.
  7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.15-M18-05 · Saved views / work queues wired into P-E list screens (API-M18-13, API-M18-14, API-M18-19; E-saved_view)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.15 / M18
- **Depends on:** T-1A.9-M09-01, T-1A.3-M24-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 00 §7.1 E-saved_view; 06 API-M18-13, API-M18-14; 04b §2, §5.2; 16 TS-FE-03
- **Description:** Build saved views / work queues (MK:erp-orders.html "Saved views = work queues"; 00 §7.1 E-saved_view): SavedViewService lists the caller's and team-shared views for a screen key (API-M18-13), saves the current filters as a named view optionally shared with the team (API-M18-14), and renames, updates, shares/unshares or archives own views (API-M18-19; `expected_version`). Sharing never widens data access — a shared view's rows are always filtered by the viewer's record scope (03 §2.21.25). Provide a reusable saved-view control in the workspace and wire it into P-E02 (view tabs with counts from `include_counts`, "Save view"); the P-E13 report viewer uses the same control when it is built in T-1A.15-M18-07 (no dependency is declared between the two tasks). Persisting per-user column choices is D-170 and not part of this task.
- **Files/components:** `backend/reporting/` (SavedViewService), `frontend/workspace/` (shared saved-view control; P-E02 wiring); tests in `backend/reporting/` and component tests (finer structure per D-001/D-002; workspace per D-101)
- **Database impact:** None new — E-saved_view (DB-G10: screen_code, name, filters, owner_user_id, shared_with, state)
- **API impact:** Implements API-M18-13, API-M18-14, API-M18-19; list endpoints' `include_counts` (06 §1.9) supply the tab counts
- **Frontend impact:** P-E02 saved-view tabs and "Save view" (name, share with team), rename/archive of own views; reusable control for other P-E lists (P-E13 in T-1A.15-M18-07)
- **Backend impact:** Owner-only edits; team sharing limited to the caller's team scope; filters stored as data and always re-evaluated against the viewer's scope; audit of create/share (03 §2.21.25)
- **Testing requirements:** TS-FE-03 (saved views on P-E02), TS-API-01 and TS-API-04 (version conflict on update), TS-API-05 (shared view never returns rows outside the viewer's scope), TS-REG-02 for M18
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. A user can save, list, rename, share and archive own views for a screen key; others' views cannot be edited (`404`/`403`).
  2. A view shared with the team shows each viewer only rows within their own record scope.
  3. P-E02 view tabs apply the stored filters and show counts.
  4. Stale `expected_version` returns `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`.
  5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.15-M19-01 · Accounting export A26 with accounting adapter (file or API): batches with control totals, per-document status, retry with the same keys, acknowledgement import; P-E12 #export and GST series view (API-M19-06…09)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.15 / M19
- **Depends on:** T-1A.11-M19-01, T-1A.12-M13-04, T-1A.2-M23-01, T-1A.3-M24-01
- **Decisions:** D-011, D-004
- **References:** 05 §5.19; 10 §10; 04c §5.9; 06 API-M19-06…09; 03 §2.17.2; 16 TS-INT-05, TS-ERP-14, TS-DB-02; BP §14.2; A26; T18, T27
- **Description:** Build automation A26 accounting export (BP §14.2, §16.4, §17.6; A26 P1/C; 10 §10; 05 §5.19): AccountingExportService publishes approved financial documents (invoices, credit notes, receipts and other documents in the D-011 scope) to the retained official accounting authority (BR-M19-01) in batches, once per document and version (unique mapping I-09; BR-M19-03), through the accounting adapter by file or API (D-011; signed-off file export is the documented fallback, BP §16.4); batch control totals (documents, taxable value, tax components, receipts, credit notes) ours vs acknowledgement vs difference; per-document status sent/acknowledged/failed/skipped (API-M19-06); retry of failed documents with the same idempotency keys (API-M19-07); control-total report download (API-M19-08); acknowledgement import; a control-total mismatch raises a finance exception; corrections go as credit/debit notes, never by editing an exported voucher (10 §10.2). Build P-E12 `#export` (callout, control totals, "Retry failed (n)", "Control-total report", documents table with filter, GST invoice-series table from API-M19-09). Verification-transaction orders are excluded (BR-M10-19). Activate A26 through the S-17 procedure (T-1A.14-M17-02) once complete. P-E12 screen built only if D-004 decides custom. Not in scope: invoice issue and series (T-1A.11-M19-01), daily close (T-1A.15-M11-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/finance/` (AccountingExportService, acknowledgement import), `backend/integrations/` (accounting adapter, file and/or API per D-011), `frontend/workspace/` (P-E12 `#export`); tests in `backend/finance/`, `backend/integrations/` sandbox tests, `tests/acceptance/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002; workspace per D-101)
- **Database impact:** None new — E-accounting_export (DB-G8; document polyref, document_version, target_system, method, state, external_reference, control_totals, error; unique (document type, id, version, target)), E-invoice_reference (read), E-outbox_operation, E-job_attempt, E-exception_case, E-integration_event (acknowledgements)
- **API impact:** Implements API-M19-06, API-M19-07 (`Idem`), API-M19-08; consumes API-M19-09 (implemented in T-1A.11-M19-01) for the series table
- **Frontend impact:** P-E12 `#export` (04c §5.9): control-totals table (ours · accounting ack. · diff), documents table (All / Failed / Skipped), "Retry failed (n)", "Control-total report", GST invoice-series table; accounting product names in MK are samples (D-011)
- **Backend impact:** Export intent written to the outbox with the document's business transaction; worker sends via the adapter with the idempotency key = document id + version; re-runs skip acknowledged documents; timeout → query the target/control totals before resend (16 §8.1); rules BR-M19-01, BR-M19-02, BR-M19-03, BR-M19-04, BR-M19-07, BR-M10-19
- **Testing requirements:** TS-INT-05 (one mapping per approved document/version, retries with the same keys, control totals, file fallback), TS-ERP-14 (accounting export with control totals), TS-DB-02 (unique mapping constraint I-09), T18 accounting half (duplicate refund command → one accounting effect), T27 export part, TS-API-03 (API-M19-07 replay), TS-FE-03 (P-E12 `#export`), TS-REG-02 for M19
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Each approved document version is exported once; re-running a batch skips acknowledged documents and a second mapping for the same document/version is rejected by the database constraint.
  2. Control totals of every batch show ours, acknowledged and difference; a non-zero difference raises one finance exception.
  3. Retrying failed documents uses the original idempotency keys and never creates a duplicate voucher.
  4. The control-total report downloads for a batch; the invoice-series table shows gap check and cancelled numbers without reuse.
  5. A duplicated refund command results in one refund and one accounting document export (T18 accounting half).
  6. Verification-transaction documents are excluded from batches.
  7. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.15-M11-01 · Daily close with maker-checker and P-E12 #close (API-M11-20, API-M11-21; E-finance_day_close)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **Description:** Build the daily finance close with maker-checker (MK:erp-finance.html `#close`; BP §14.2 "reconcile document counts, amounts, taxes, and status", §18.2 separation of duties; T27): DailyCloseService returns the day's checklist with status, open items and evidence per check (API-M11-20) and supports re-run checks, maker sign-off (an exceptions note is mandatory while items are open) and checker approval by a different person (API-M11-21; BR-M11-17). Checks come from the finance-approved list (D-011); MK samples include webhook events processed, pending attempts resolved, settlement imported and matched (CONDITIONAL D-064), bank statement matched, failed refunds reviewed, COD remittances (CONDITIONAL D-020), branch POS and terminal totals (D-009, D-030), invoice-series gap check and accounting-export control totals. Sign-off locks the day's payment ledger for export and later events post to the next business date with a reference to the close (MK; E-finance_day_close.ledger_locked). Build P-E12 `#close` including the checker approval view not drawn in MK (04c §5.10); business-date boundary D-124, deadline value D-179. Built only if D-004 decides P-E12 custom. Not in scope: the underlying reconciliation functions (1A.10), accounting export (T-1A.15-M19-01).

- **Database impact:** None new — E-finance_day_close (DB-G7: business_date, scope, checks, exceptions_note, maker/checker, state open/signed_off/approved, ledger_locked); reads E-payment_event, E-payment_attempt, E-refund, E-settlement_record, E-invoice_reference, E-accounting_export
- **API impact:** Implements API-M11-20, API-M11-21 (`409` on invalid transition)
- **Frontend impact:** P-E12 `#close` (header with maker, checker, deadline, progress; checklist rows with "Resolve" links; exceptions note; "Re-run checks", "Sign off with exceptions"; checker "Approve" for a user ≠ maker; error "Add an exceptions note — n items are still open")
- **Backend impact:** Check definitions configurable by finance (D-011) — no invented check list; maker ≠ checker enforced server-side (SoD-6); ledger lock after sign-off with next-business-date posting of late events; audit of sign-off and approval; rules BR-M11-17, BR-M02-06
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-14 (daily close maker-checker), TS-PERM-08.2 (same user as maker and checker → `403`), T27 close part, TS-FE-03 (P-E12 `#close` states), TS-API-01, TS-REG-02 for M11
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. The checklist shows each configured check with status and open items; re-run refreshes them.
  2. Sign-off with open items and no exceptions note is refused; with a note it moves the day to `signed_off` and locks the payment ledger for export.
  3. The maker cannot approve the same close (`403`); a different finance user or R-owner can.
  4. An event arriving after sign-off posts to the next business date with a reference to the close.
  5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1A.16-M26-01 · Alert catalogue: conditions, page vs daily review, named owners; alert routing drills (API-M24-14)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **Description:** Build the alert catalogue and its routing (BP §20.3 "Assign an owner to every alert. Page only for urgent customer/revenue/stock risk. Thresholds, routes and owners are D-195 values (MK samples are not requirements); storage in versioned configuration or the monitoring tool per D-052. - **Files/components:** `backend/platform/observability/` and `infra/` (alert definitions and routing per D-052), `backend/admin/` (API-M24-14 handler), `frontend/workspace/` (P-E15 `#system` "Monitoring & alerts" edit action); drill scripts and evidence in `tests/acceptance/` or `infra/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002)
- **Database impact:** None new — alert catalogue as E-configuration_version entries (or monitoring-tool configuration per D-052); E-audit_event for changes

- **Frontend impact:** P-E15 `#system` "Monitoring & alerts": table Alert · Condition · Route · Owner · Last fired with an edit form (condition, route, owner, reason) for R-owner/R-ops_admin
- **Backend impact:** Alert evaluation from the telemetry emitted by modules (05 §1.7); paging only for urgent customer/revenue/stock risk; daily-review digest for the rest; exception-queue route creates/updates E-exception_case via ExceptionService; removing an alert's owner is refused; rules BR-M26-01, BR-M26-02, BR-M26-10, BR-M17-17
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ADM-08 (alert routing), alert-routing drills (page path and daily-review path reach the named owner; exception route creates one case), TS-API-01, TS-API-04, TS-PERM-01 (`system.alerts.manage` only for R-ops_admin/R-owner), TS-REG-02 for M26, M24

#### T-1A.16-M26-02 · Data retention matrix: retention classes → entity hooks, anonymisation that keeps statutory records
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.16 / M26
- **Depends on:** T-1A.8-M08-04
- **Decisions:** D-036
- **References:** 03 §9.1; 11 §12.4; 16 TS-DB-06; BP §19.3
- **Description:** Implement the data-retention matrix as hooks per retention class (BP §19.3; 03 §9.1; 11 §12.4): for each class RC-account, RC-order, RC-invoice, RC-warranty, RC-chat, RC-identity, RC-log, RC-backup, RC-operational the purpose, access, retention basis, deletion/anonymisation method and exceptions decided in D-036 are stored as configuration and enforced by retention jobs on the listed entities — account deletion via a reviewed data request removes profile/access and anonymises PD1 fields while keeping references from statutory records (BR-M08-09), invoices and accounting exports are never destroyed by customer deletion (RC-invoice, D-037), chat transcripts deleted after their period with ticket summaries kept (RC-chat), identity documents securely deleted after relationship end plus period (RC-identity), logs rolling with audit longer than application logs (RC-log). Every deletion job checks the dispute and statutory exceptions (open returns, `payment_dispute` tickets, chargeback settlement lines; 03 §9.1). Deletions and anonymisations are logged so that they can be re-applied after a restore (03 §7.5; TS-BKP-03). The matrix is published read-only in P-E15 `#system` through API-M24-08. Not in scope: the data-request screens and processing flow (T-1A.8-M08-04, which calls these hooks), backup expiry mechanics (D-108 infrastructure).
- **Files/components:** retention registry and scheduler in `backend/platform/`, per-class hooks in the owning module folders (`backend/customers/`, `backend/orders/`, `backend/support/`, `backend/identity/`, `backend/files/`, …); tests in those folders and `tests/acceptance/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002)
- **Database impact:** None new — retention configuration as E-configuration_version (matrix per D-036); hooks act on the entities of 03 §9.1 per class; a re-application log of executed deletions/anonymisations kept with the retention job records (E-job_attempt)
- **API impact:** None new — API-M24-08 `retention_matrix` (T-1A.16-M24-01) exposes the matrix; data requests use API-M08-44/-45 (T-1A.8-M08-04)
- **Frontend impact:** P-E15 `#system` "Data retention matrix" shows the decided matrix (read-only)
- **Backend impact:** Retention jobs per class with dispute/statutory exception checks; anonymisation replaces PD1 fields while keeping financial fields and statutory references; secure deletion for PD2 files; re-application list for restores; rules BR-M26-07, BR-M08-09, BR-M08-10, BR-M25-07
- **Testing requirements:** TS-DB-06 (personal-data classification tagged; anonymisation keeps statutory records; deletion separates profile from transactions — each retention class), TS-BKP-03 (deletions re-applied after restore, with T-1A.17-M25-04), TS-SVC-11 (time-travel expiry per class), TS-REG-02 for M26, M08, M16
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Each retention class has the D-036 values stored as configuration and a hook covering all its entities from 03 §9.1.
  2. Deleting a customer account removes profile and access, anonymises personal fields and leaves invoices, accounting exports and order financial fields intact.
  3. A record under an open dispute, return or statutory hold is skipped by every deletion job and reported.
  4. Every executed deletion/anonymisation is listed for re-application after a restore.
  5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Every editable unlocked key renders with its plain-language label, help text and validation, with no key identifier visible. (2) Locking a key in the configuration removes it from the screen and from the screen's data entirely. (3) Invalid input is rejected with the same rule the compiler applies. (4) Changes are versioned, approved where required and audited. (5) The rendered page contains none of the banned vocabulary. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

### Stage 1A.16 additions — delegated feature management for the store administrator (D-258)

#### T-1A.16-M24-09 · Store Features screen in P-E15: the delegated modules and capabilities only, in the store's own language, with dependency and run-out handling
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.16 / M24
- **Depends on:** T-1A.16-M24-08, T-1A.1-M31-08
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** SAAS §3 S03; 19 §5.4.3 CTL-1…CTL-7, §9 INV-4, §23.3; 11 (SaaS additions); DEC D-258, D-229
- **Description:** Give the store's administrator the screen the brief asks for: the features they were allowed to manage, and nothing else. It lists only `delegated` modules and capabilities, grouped in business language with the plain-language description from the schema, and never shows a module id, capability id or configuration key. Items that are locked or that the store does not have are absent — not greyed, not labelled as managed elsewhere. Turning something on resolves its dependencies first and explains them in the store's own words; turning something off shows how many open records exist and what the run-out rule will do before it is confirmed. Every change is versioned, audited in the store's own trail and applied within the propagation budget without a deployment.
- **Files/components:** `frontend/workspace/screens/settings/features/`, store feature endpoints from T-1A.1-M31-08
- **Database impact:** E-store_feature_state writes; E-audit_event entries
- **API impact:** Store feature read/write endpoints, delegated set only
- **Frontend impact:** P-E15 Features section
- **Backend impact:** None new
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-CAP-09 (CTL-1…CTL-7 through the UI), TS-SAAS-ISO-04 (locked and absent items invisible in the page and its data), TS-SAAS-CAP-10 (run-out confirmation), TS-SAAS-ISO-01 (no platform vocabulary), TS-A11Y, TS-AUDIT
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) The screen lists exactly the delegated set, in business language, with no identifier visible. (2) A locked or absent feature appears nowhere on the page or in the data the page loads. (3) Enabling a feature with dependencies enables them with an explanation written in the store's own words. (4) Disabling a feature with open work shows the count and the run-out consequence before confirming. (5) A change takes effect within the propagation budget with no deployment, and is audited in the store's own trail. (6) The rendered page contains none of the banned vocabulary. (7) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —


### Stage 1A.16 addition — workspace and vendor performance (D-268)

#### T-1A.16-M24-10 · Workspace and vendor performance: screen-shaped endpoints, keyset pagination, virtualised lists and per-screen query budgets
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.16 / M24
- **Depends on:** T-1A.16-M24-03, T-1A.3-M09-07, T-1A.1-M30-06
- **Decisions:** D-034, D-053
- **References:** 19 §25.2, §25.3; DEC D-268, D-034; BP §20.1; 04b §2, 04c
- **Description:** Make the staff and vendor applications fast on real data, which is where an ERP is normally slow. Convert the busiest screens to screen-shaped endpoints so one screen is one round trip rather than nine entity calls; move every growing list — orders, stock movements, audit, messages, submissions — to keyset pagination; virtualise long tables; and assert a maximum query count per screen with the query recorder. Review the index of every query path added by the workspace screens and confirm each has a supporting `store_id`-leading index. Move every heavy action — bulk updates, exports, reports, imports — to the job runtime so no request does heavy work.
- **Files/components:** `backend/<workspace modules>/screens/`, `frontend/workspace/`, `frontend/vendor-portal/`, migration index review
- **Database impact:** Supporting indexes for every workspace query path; no unindexed scan on a growing table
- **API impact:** Screen-shaped endpoints for the busiest P-E and P-V screens
- **Frontend impact:** P-E02, P-E03, P-E06, P-E08, P-E09, P-E10, P-E12, P-E13, P-V02, P-V03 list behaviour
- **Backend impact:** Query-count instrumentation, keyset pagination helpers
- **Testing requirements:** TS-PERF-02 (list query p95 and action round trip), TS-SAAS-PERF-10 (query count per screen), TS-DB (every query path has a supporting index), TS-FE (virtualised list keyboard and screen-reader behaviour)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Every listed screen meets the 19 §25.2 workspace budgets at realistic volumes with two stores. (2) Each screen declares and asserts a maximum query count; an introduced N+1 fails the test. (3) Every growing list uses keyset pagination and stays fast at page 500, verified. (4) Every workspace query path has a supporting `store_id`-leading index, confirmed against the query plans. (5) No bulk action, export or report runs inside a request. (6) Virtualised lists remain keyboard and screen-reader navigable (WCAG 2.2 AA). (7) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —


### Stage 1A.16 addition — store-side channel and automation administration (D-258, D-274)

#### T-1A.16-M24-11 · Store-side channel and automation administration: the channels the store owns, its templates, its automations — delegated items only
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.16 / M24
- **Depends on:** T-1A.16-M24-09, T-1A.13-M20-06, T-1A.13-M17-01

- **Description:** Give the store's administrator the channel and automation controls the platform delegated to them, and nothing else. Where a channel is delegated, they can switch it on and off, manage their own sender identity and verification, edit and submit their templates, and see delivery health. Where an automation is delegated, they can enable, preview, pause and read its run log. Channels and automations the store does not have, or that are locked, are absent — no switch, no greyed row, no mention. Enabling a delegated channel still requires its verification to pass, so the store gets the same clear report rather than a silent failure.

- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Only delegated channels and automations appear; the rest are absent from the page and from the data it loads. (2) A store enabling a delegated channel sees the same verification requirements and the same clear report as an operator would. (3) Template edits are versioned, and where the provider requires approval the state is shown honestly. (4) Automation enable, preview, pause and run log work for delegated rules only. (5) Every change is audited in the store's own trail. (6) The page contains no platform vocabulary and no identifiers. (7) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

## Stage 1A.17 — Migration, UAT & launch readiness

#### T-1A.17-M25-01 · Migration toolkit consolidation and remaining datasets (S-20): vendors/suppliers and supplier-code mapping, open orders, payment/refund provider references, warranty records, historical order archive (audited idempotent batch jobs)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.17 / M25
- **Depends on:** T-1A.4-M25-01, T-1A.6-M25-01, T-1A.7-M25-01, T-1A.8-M25-01, T-1A.12-M13-05
- **Decisions:** D-038, D-009
- **References:** 05 §5.25; 09 §5.23; 03 §7.4; 16 TS-MIG-03; BP §21.2
- **Description:** Consolidate the migration toolkit and add the remaining datasets of S-20 (BP §21.2; 05 §5.25; 03 §7.4): one repeatable, audited, idempotent batch-job framework with validation and row-level error reports (BR-M25-06) that runs the dataset scripts written earlier (catalog T-1A.4-M25-01, stock and serials T-1A.6-M25-01, open POs T-1A.7-M25-01, customers and dealers T-1A.8-M25-01) and the new ones: vendors/suppliers with supplier-code mapping and approved categories (09 §5.23; status and code-mapping reconciliation), open orders migrated with lines and reservations or completed in legacy with an explicit boundary (D-038), payment and refund provider references with unresolved items (captured/refunded/settled totals), warranty records (serial, sale date, policy version, evidence; sample claim reconstruction; uses the warranty services of T-1A.12-M13-05) and the historical order archive (read-only archive or selected migration per D-038). All loads go through module services, never direct table writes (BP §16.3); only masked extracts outside production (BR-M25-07; D-136); legacy exports and access per D-009; accounting history stays in the accounting authority (BP §21.2; D-011). Vendor approval records and vendor-portal users (E-vendor_approval, invitations) belong to DB-G9 and are created when that group exists (1B.1), not here. Not in scope: rehearsals (T-1A.17-M25-02/-03), passwords (T-1A.17-M02-01), SEO redirects (T-1A.17-M27-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/migration/` (toolkit, dataset scripts, mappings, reconciliation reports), dataset control-total tests in `tests/migration/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002)
- **Database impact:** Loads S-20 opening data via services into E-supplier, E-supplier_code_mapping, E-sales_order/E-order_line/E-reservation (open orders per D-038), E-payment_attempt, E-refund, E-serial_unit warranty fields, E-warranty_case and the historical archive per D-038; each run tracked as E-import_job (`job_type` migration) with E-import_row results
- **API impact:** None (scripts; no external endpoint)
- **Frontend impact:** None
- **Backend impact:** Batch jobs are idempotent on legacy identifiers (`[EXT]` fields), re-runnable, audited, and produce per-dataset control totals and rejected-row reports; rules BR-M25-01, BR-M25-03, BR-M25-06, BR-M25-07; stock is never inserted as positions directly (opening-balance movements only, 03 §7.4)
- **Testing requirements:** TS-MIG-03 (dataset control totals per BP §21.2), re-run idempotency tests (second run creates no duplicates), row-level error-report tests, TS-DB-07 after the stock load, TS-REG-02 for M25
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Every BP §21.2 dataset in the D-038 scope has a script whose re-run on the same extract creates no duplicate record.
  2. Each run produces control totals and a rejected-row report per dataset.
  3. Supplier statuses and supplier-code mappings reconcile with the legacy source.
  4. Open orders, payment/refund references and warranty records reconcile on amount, status, payment, reservation, shipment and sample claim reconstruction.
  5. No production personal data is used outside production except approved masked extracts.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.17-M02-01 · Password migration via a proven compatible method or forced reset
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.17 / M02
- **Depends on:** T-1A.8-M25-01, T-1A.2-M02-05
- **Decisions:** D-039
- **References:** 05 BR-M02-16; 07 §3.9; 16 TS-MIG-04, TS-AUTH-05; BP §21.2 (Passwords)
- **Description:** Migrate customer passwords only through a compatible secure method proven on the selected platform, otherwise force a reset (BP §21.2 "Use compatible secure migration only when proven; otherwise reset"; BR-M02-16, BR-M25-05; 07 §3.9; decision D-039). Proven path: import legacy hashes into E-user_account through the platform's supported mechanism, and verify sign-in for a sample of migrated accounts. Reset path: migrated accounts are loaded without a password, so the first sign-in goes through the existing reset or code sign-in flows (API-M02-07/-08; methods D-040) with an approved message template. No plaintext password exists in extracts, logs, audit records or error messages at any point (BP §19.1). Staff accounts are created by invitation (S-04) and vendor users are invited afresh (09 §5.23), so neither receives migrated passwords. Not in scope: authentication flows themselves (1A.2/1A.3).
- **Files/components:** `backend/migration/` (password dataset script), `backend/identity/` (verification of migrated credentials or first-sign-in reset handling per D-039); tests in `tests/migration/`, `tests/security/` (finer structure per D-001/D-002)
- **Database impact:** E-user_account `password_hash` (SEC) loaded (proven path) or left empty (reset path) per D-039, legacy account id in `[EXT]`; no new column; E-audit_event for resets
- **API impact:** Consumes API-M02-07 and API-M02-08 for the reset path; no new endpoint
- **Frontend impact:** None beyond messages on the existing sign-in/reset screens (P-S12 `#signin`, P-S14) telling migrated users to reset, if D-039 chooses reset
- **Backend impact:** Supported-mechanism check (never a custom hash scheme unless the platform supports it, D-001/D-040); reset tokens single-use and expiring; rate limits of the reset flow (D-084); rules BR-M02-16, BR-M25-05, BR-M02-11
- **Testing requirements:** TS-MIG-04 (sign-in works or reset issued; no plaintext), TS-AUTH-05 (password storage, reset single-use/expiry, migration or forced reset), TS-AUTH-10 (no passwords/tokens in logs, audit or URLs), TS-REG-02 for M02, M25
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. With the proven path, sampled migrated users sign in with their existing password; with the reset path, every migrated user must reset before first use.
  2. A scan of extracts, logs, audit payloads and error messages finds no plaintext password or reset token.
  3. Reset tokens are single-use and expire.
  4. No staff or vendor account carries a migrated password.
  5. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.17-M25-06 · Cutover execution: freeze or final delta, final import with control totals, verify opening stock/serials/payment references/permissions, switch channels, supervised low-risk production transactions, legacy read-only access
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **Description:** Execute the cutover (BP §21.3 steps 5–10; WP17): freeze relevant legacy changes or capture an auditable final delta; import final master and open-transaction data with the toolkit and reconcile control totals against the stop/go thresholds (E-migration_rehearsal `final_cutover`, go/no-go approved); verify opening stock, serials, payment references and permissions (TS-MIG-06, TS-PERM-01); switch the selected channels to the new authority with one documented stock authority per transaction and no two independent live ledgers (BR-M25-03); activate the S-23 redirects; perform supervised real low-risk transactions and refunds flagged as verification transactions through API-M10-26 as D-209 prescribes; keep legacy read-only access for history (TS-MIG-08). A no-go at any stop/go threshold triggers the rollback plan of T-1A.17-M25-04. D-048 decides the launch scope; under a combined launch this task is re-staged after 1B.5 per D-213. Not in scope: hypercare (T-1A.17-M26-07).

- **Database impact:** Production load of S-20 opening data and S-23 redirects; E-migration_rehearsal `final_cutover` (control totals, stop/go thresholds, outcome go/no_go, approvals); verification orders flagged in `E-sales_order.verification_transaction`
- **API impact:** Consumes API-M10-26 (flag supervised verification transactions); no new endpoint
- **Frontend impact:** None (channel switch is configuration/routing)
- **Backend impact:** Final-delta capture and load through services; legacy system set read-only for history (D-009, D-038); rules BR-M25-02, BR-M25-03, BR-M10-19
- **Testing requirements:** TS-MIG-03 (final load control totals), TS-MIG-06 (cutover verification incl. flagged supervised transactions), TS-MIG-08 (legacy read-only), TS-PERM-01 on production permissions, TS-MIG-05 spot check of redirects after the switch
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  1. Final control totals reconcile within the stop/go thresholds and the go decision is recorded with approvers.
  2. Opening stock, serials, payment references and permissions are verified and signed.
  3. After the switch each channel uses the new stock authority; no legacy channel writes stock independently.
  4. Supervised verification transactions and refunds succeed, are flagged and are excluded from reports and accounting export.
  5. Legacy history is readable and not writable.
  6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1A.17-M25-07 · Migration into store `tradex`: store-scoped load, per-store control totals, store context on every migration script
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.17 / M25
- **Depends on:** T-1A.17-M25-01, T-1A.1-M30-02
- **Decisions:** D-038, D-001
- **References:** SAAS §3 S01; 19 §16 (M25 row); 20 §10; DEC D-251, D-233, D-038; BP §21.2, §21.3
- **Description:** Make the Phase 1 migration a per-store operation. Every migration and reconciliation script runs inside an explicit store context, writes `store_id` on every row, and produces control totals per store rather than globally, so a future second store cannot blur the figures. Verify that a script run without a store context fails rather than defaulting, and that a rehearsal load into a second test store leaves the Tradex store untouched. The datasets, mappings and reconciliation rules of the existing migration tasks are unchanged.
- **Files/components:** `backend/` migration scripts under the tenancy guard, `plan/records/1A.17/` control totals
- **Database impact:** All migrated rows carry `store_id`; control totals recorded per store
- **API impact:** None

### Stage 1A.17 additions — per-store recovery and the edge-case suite (D-260)

#### T-1A.17-M26-09 · Per-store backup, restore, export and deletion: mechanism, tooling and a timed single-store restore rehearsal
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1A.17 / M26
- **Depends on:** T-1A.17-M26-01, T-1A.1-M30-02, T-1A.1-M35-01
- **Decisions:** D-108, D-036, D-122, D-033
- **References:** 19 §18, §14 BR-M35-05; DEC D-260, D-108, D-036; BP §19.3, §20.1, §23.4, T28
- **Description:** Make "restore one store" a real, rehearsed procedure rather than an assumption. Build the store-scoped logical export and the key-preserving idempotent import, and document the restore path: scratch-restore the cluster to a point in time, export the target `store_id`, import it back under that store's tenant context, reconcile control totals. Restoring in place over a shared database is not a supported path and the tooling refuses it. Build the per-store export used for portability, end of contract and legal requests, covering business data, store-owned settings and delegated feature states, the configuration artefact and media. Implement deletion with the retention period and destruction evidence, and state plainly to the owner that backups still hold the data until they age out. Rehearse a single-store restore end to end and record the measured time as the store-level recovery figure.
- **Files/components:** `backend/platform/tenancy/export/`, `infra/runbooks/store-restore.md`, `infra/runbooks/store-export.md`, `tests/restore/per-store/`
- **Database impact:** No schema change; the export and import operate through the tenant-scoped data-access layer
- **API impact:** Operator-triggered export job (platform side, API-M34-08)
- **Frontend impact:** None (operator surfaces are P-R05 and P-R12)
- **Backend impact:** StoreExporter, StoreImporter with key preservation and idempotency
- **Testing requirements:** TS-BKP per store, TS-SAAS-ISO-19 (a single-store restore leaves every other store byte-identical), TS-SAAS-DEPLOY-15 (import is idempotent and key-preserving), TS-MIG (control-total reconciliation)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) A single store is restored to a chosen point in time and every other store is byte-identical before and after, verified by comparison. (2) Re-running the import changes nothing and creates no duplicates. (3) Control totals reconcile against the scratch instance. (4) The per-store export contains business data, store-owned settings, delegated feature states, the configuration artefact and media, and is documented. (5) The rehearsal is timed and the figure is recorded as the store-level recovery time. (6) The runbooks exist and have been followed once by someone who did not write them. (7) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Every store-side row of 19 §23 has a named test case that asserts the documented behaviour. (2) Each test fails if the behaviour is reverted, demonstrated for at least five cases in the evidence. (3) No case is skipped or marked pending; a case that cannot run yet blocks this task. ## Stage 1R.1 — Root admin foundation & store registry

Stage `1R.1` was added by the SaaS architecture change (`D-227`). It starts after the 1A stages and before 1B
(`12-phases.md` §10.3). References: `20-root-admin.md`, `19-saas-platform.md` §2–§5.

#### T-1R.1-M34-01 · Root admin application scaffolding: separate manifest, build, CI pipeline, database, environments, health endpoint and enforced import boundary
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.1 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1A.1-M01-11, T-1A.16-M24-05
- **Decisions:** D-002, D-005, D-077, D-101, D-109, D-244
- **References:** SAAS §3 S04, S23; 20 §1, §2; 19 §2 SEP-1…SEP-6; DEC D-228, D-244; BP §15.6, §16.6, §19.1
- **Description:** Stand up the Configurable Root Admin as its own application inside `root-admin/`: dependency manifest, build, test runner, CI pipeline, its own database and migration runner, its own development/staging/production environments and secrets, a health endpoint, and structured logging with correlation ids. Reuse the store platform's conventions — API envelope, pagination, money and date formats, idempotency transport — because one convention across two applications is cheaper than two; reuse no store code. The portal is reachable only through the identity-aware proxy or allow-listed networks, and it can reach object storage and its own database but never a store database.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/` (manifest, app/, api/, domain/, compiler/, deploy/, platform-ops/, migrations/, tests/), `infra/` environment and pipeline definitions for the platform
- **Database impact:** Root admin database created with its own migration runner (separate from the store database)
- **API impact:** Platform API base path, error envelope and conventions per D-080/D-079; never exposed on a store hostname
- **Frontend impact:** Portal application skeleton (screens follow in T-1R.1-M34-09)
- **Backend impact:** Platform application skeleton, configuration loader, health endpoint
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-SEP-01…06 (boundary, no shared session, no store database access), TS-API-01 (health and conventions), pipeline runs both test suites independently
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) `root-admin/` builds, tests and deploys through its own pipeline without building the store applications. (2) The platform has its own database and cannot open a store database connection, verified by test. (3) No session, cookie domain or token issuer is shared with any store. (4) Health, logging and correlation ids work and the environments are separated with their own secrets. (5) The store applications still build and deploy unchanged. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1R.1-M34-04 · Platform audit trail: every mutating action recorded with actor, target store, before and after, and reason; query and export

- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Every mutating platform command writes an audit entry in the same transaction; a command that cannot audit fails. (2) Entries carry actor, role, target store, before, after, reason, correlation id and timestamp. (3) The trail cannot be updated or deleted through any path. #### T-1R.1-M34-07 · The configuration compiler: layer resolution L0–L3, validation, capability dependency and conflict resolution, deterministic artefact build, checksums and the artefact store
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.1 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.1-M34-06, T-1A.1-M31-03
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** SAAS §3 S12–S15; 19 §3.1, §4.2, §14 BR-M31-04/05, BR-M34-02; 20 §2, §5 steps 1–2; DEC D-230, D-231
- **Description:** Build the heart of the platform. The compiler takes the platform defaults published with the store release, the pack version, the template version and the store's configuration values, resolves the layers in order, resolves capability dependencies and conflicts, validates everything against the schema and the pack and template rules, and emits the artefact set of 19 §4.2 with a checksum, a schema hash and the target platform release. It is deterministic: the same inputs always produce byte-identical output, which is what makes content addressing, diffing and rollback trustworthy. Secrets are never embedded — only references. A validation failure blocks the build and cannot be overridden.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/compiler/` (resolver, validators, emitters, determinism tests), artefact storage adapter
- **Database impact:** E-config_artifact (metadata: checksum, size, file list, build duration, compiler version, platform release, storage URI)
- **API impact:** API-M34-12 (validate), API-M34-13 (compile dry run)
- **Frontend impact:** None (consumed by P-R05 and P-R10)
- **Backend impact:** Compiler pipeline, artefact writer
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-CFG-05 (determinism: identical inputs → identical bytes, 100 runs), TS-SAAS-CFG-14 (validation blocks publish and cannot be overridden), TS-SAAS-CFG-06 (no secret value in the artefact), TS-SAAS-CAP-03 (dependency and conflict resolution)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Compiling the same inputs twice produces byte-identical artefacts including checksums. (2) A schema, pack, template, capability-dependency, capability-conflict or contrast violation blocks the build with a precise, readable report. (3) There is no override path for a failed validation. (4) The emitted artefact matches the 19 §4.2 file list and validates in the store runtime loader. (5) No secret value appears anywhere in the artefact. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1R.1-M34-08 · Configuration drafts, versions, diff, publish and rollback (P-R05 configuration tabs)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.1 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.1-M34-07, T-1A.1-M31-04
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 19 §3.4, §4.4, §14 BR-M31-05, BR-M34-02; 20 §4, §5 steps 3, 5; DEC D-230, D-232; MK-R:ra-store.html
- **Description:** Give operators the safe editing path. A draft per store per environment holds work in progress and never affects a running store; validation runs on demand and on publish; the diff shows in plain language what would change for the store — capabilities turned on or off, settings changed, terminology changed, theme changed, and any schema change that touches existing data — and requires acknowledgement for anything that looks destructive. Publishing creates an immutable version, writes the artefact, records the publication and emits `config.published`. Rollback republishes an earlier version through exactly the same path.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/domain/config/`, `root-admin/api/config/`, `root-admin/app/screens/store/config/`
- **Database impact:** E-store_config_draft, E-store_config_version, E-config_publication
- **API impact:** API-M34-10…19
- **Frontend impact:** P-R05 configuration tabs and the version history/diff view
- **Backend impact:** Draft service, publisher, event emission through the outbox
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-CFG-15 (draft never affects a live store), TS-SAAS-CFG-08 (rollback), TS-SAAS-CFG-16 (diff accuracy against a known change set), TS-SVC-02 (idempotent publish)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Editing a draft changes nothing in the running store until publish. (2) The diff correctly reports capability, setting, terminology, theme and schema changes for a known change set. (3) Destructive-looking changes require an explicit acknowledgement that is audited. (4) Publish is idempotent and produces exactly one version and one artefact per attempt. (5) Rollback to any retained version works through the same path and is audited. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

### Stage 1R.1 addition — contextual help engine (D-280)

#### T-1R.1-M34-11 · Root admin contextual help: the ⓘ engine, the page-guide panel, search, the platform glossary and the help icons control
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.1 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.1-M34-09
- **Decisions:** D-051, D-101
- **References:** 20-root-admin.md §11 (H-1…H-6); DEC D-280, D-224, D-225; MK-R:all screens; 19 §24.1 gate 14
- **Description:** Build for the platform portal the help the store workspace already has. An ⓘ next to every heading, tab, section and significant control opens a non-modal side panel on that entry, shifting the main column rather than covering it so the thing being explained stays visible. The ? in the top bar opens the whole-page guide; each tab bar gets an "About this tab" control; the panel carries a search across every entry and a glossary of the platform's own vocabulary, reachable from any dotted-underlined word on a screen; and a Help icons control hides or shows every ⓘ, remembered between visits. Each entry follows the six-part shape of 20 §11.2 — what it is, why it matters, how to read it, what to do, what happens next, worth knowing. Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour matches the store workspace: Esc closes, focus returns, the panel is announced, and every ⓘ has an accessible name.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/app/shell/help/` (engine, panel, search, glossary), help content beside each screen
- **Database impact:** None (content ships with the application)
- **API impact:** None
- **Frontend impact:** Every P-R screen and the portal shell
- **Backend impact:** None
- **Testing requirements:** TS-FE (panel opens on every ⓘ; no empty panel; every referenced key resolves; search, glossary, back history, icons toggle persistence), TS-A11Y (keyboard, Esc, focus return, accessible names, WCAG 2.2 AA), TS-SAAS-ISO-28 (no help text reveals another client's data)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Every heading, tab, section and significant control on every P-R screen has an ⓘ that opens a populated entry — no empty panels and no missing keys, verified by clicking every one. (2) Each tab bar has an "About this tab" control that explains the open tab. (3) The ? opens the page guide; search returns results across entries and glossary terms. (4) Every glossary term is reachable from the panel and from its dotted-underlined first mention on a screen. (5) Help icons can be hidden and shown, and the choice is remembered. (6) Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour matches the store workspace and passes WCAG 2.2 AA. (7) No help text names another client or exposes data outside this portal. (8) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

## Stage 1R.2 — Store configurator, packs, templates & terminology

The configurator that the SAAS brief describes: category, template, colours, logo, features, behaviour
(`20-root-admin.md` §4). The stage gate is the brief's own Fashion & Apparel example, executed with no code change.

#### T-1R.2-M34-01 · Vertical pack authoring and versioning (P-R06): create, validate, publish, deprecate, retire, usage tracking and seed sets
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.2 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.1-M34-10
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** SAAS §3 S02, S06, S22; 19 §6.1, §6.6, §14 BR-M32-01/03; 20 §6 (P-R06); DEC D-237, D-247; MK-R:ra-packs.html
- **Description:** Build the authoring surface for e-commerce categories. A pack version is composed from the sections of 19 §6.1, validated against the configuration schema, the capability registry and the identity-model rules, and published as immutable content with a usage count. Deprecation removes it from selection for new stores without touching existing ones; retirement is possible only when no store uses it. The screen explains each pack in plain language — what it turns on, what structure it creates, which templates suit it — because that is what an operator chooses from.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/domain/packs/`, `root-admin/api/packs/`, `root-admin/app/screens/packs/`
- **Database impact:** E-vertical_pack, E-vertical_pack_version
- **API impact:** API-M34-20…27
- **Frontend impact:** P-R06
- **Backend impact:** Pack validator, publisher, usage tracker
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-PACK-10 (validation rejects an inconsistent pack), TS-SAAS-PACK-11 (published version immutable), TS-SAAS-PACK-12 (deprecate/retire rules), TS-FE
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) A pack version can be authored, validated and published, and is immutable afterwards. (2) A pack that conflicts with the capability registry or the identity-model rules is rejected with a precise report. (3) Deprecating a pack removes it from new-store selection and changes no existing store. (4) Retirement is refused while any store uses the pack. (5) The screen states in plain language what the pack turns on. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1R.2-M34-02 · Pack migration planner and executor: impact preview per store, staged execution, rollback
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.2 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.2-M34-01
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 19 §6.6, §14 BR-M32-04; 20 §6; DEC D-247
- **Description:** Move a store from one pack version to another deliberately and reversibly. The planner shows, per affected store, exactly what would change: capabilities turned on or off, schema additions and removals, attribute type changes, terminology changes, profile changes, and anything that touches existing data. Execution goes through the ordinary configuration publish path so the change is a normal, rollback-able version. Stores are never migrated implicitly by a pack update.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/domain/packs/migration/`, `root-admin/app/screens/packs/migration/`
- **Database impact:** E-pack_migration
- **API impact:** API-M34-26, -27
- **Frontend impact:** P-R06 migration planner
- **Backend impact:** Migration planner and executor over the compiler and publisher
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-PACK-13 (preview accuracy), TS-SAAS-PACK-14 (no implicit migration on pack publish), TS-SAAS-CFG-08 (rollback)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Publishing a new pack version changes no store until a migration is executed. (2) The preview matches the actual change exactly for a known version pair. (3) Migrations that would remove in-use structure are reported and require acknowledgement. (4) A migrated store can be rolled back to its previous configuration version. (5) Every migration is audited with actor, stores, versions and reason. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1R.2-M34-04 · Template assignment and per-store template migration with preview
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED

- **Depends on:** T-1R.2-M34-03

- **Description:** Let an operator select and later change a store's template safely. Assignment pins template id and version in the store's configuration; changing it produces a preview of the storefront under the new template with the store's real configuration and branding, then publishes as an ordinary configuration version. Because a template may not change business behaviour, the switch requires no data migration — and the verification asserts that the store's business output is unchanged across the switch.

- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) A store's template can be selected at creation and changed later. (2) The preview matches what the store renders after publishing. (3) Order, price, stock and policy output are identical before and after the switch in the test fixture. (4) Switching back restores the previous appearance exactly. #### T-1R.2-M34-05 · Branding: logo upload and validation, variant generation, palette derivation and the WCAG 2.2 AA contrast gate
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.2 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.1-M34-08, T-1A.4-M22-01
- **Decisions:** D-051, D-033
- **References:** SAAS §3 S08, S09, S21; 19 §7.4; 20 §4 steps 4–5; DEC D-240, D-051; BP §6.7
- **Description:** Implement the brief's steps 4 and 5. Logos (light, dark, mark), favicon and social image are uploaded, validated for format, dimensions, transparency and size, converted into the required variants and stored under the store's storage prefix. Brand colours are entered once and the compiler derives the full surface and text ramps from them; every foreground/background pair the components use is checked against WCAG 2.2 AA and a failing palette blocks publication with a report naming the failing pairs and the nearest passing alternatives. Typography, shape, density and motion settings complete the visual configuration.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/domain/branding/`, `root-admin/api/branding/`, `root-admin/app/screens/store/branding/`
- **Database impact:** E-brand_asset; theme values in the configuration version
- **API impact:** API-M34-48…53

- **Backend impact:** Asset validation and variant generation, palette derivation, contrast checker
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-TPL-09 (derivation and contrast gate), TS-A11Y-01 (contrast across the derived ramp), TS-FILE (upload validation), TS-SAAS-CFG-14 (publish blocked on failure)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Logo upload validates format, dimensions, transparency and size and generates every required variant. (2) Entering brand colours produces a complete ramp without further input. (3) A palette that cannot meet WCAG 2.2 AA blocks publication and the report names the failing pairs. (4) Assets are stored under the store's prefix and referenced, never embedded, in the artefact. (5) The rendered store reflects the branding after publish. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1R.2-M34-06 · Terminology authoring (P-R09): token registry, per-pack sets per locale, per-store overrides, coverage report and preview
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

The screen lists the token registry with each token's meaning and grammatical information, lets a pack author supply a complete set per locale, lets a store override individual tokens where allowed, reports coverage gaps before publication, and previews a real screen with the chosen set applied so wording is judged in context rather than in a spreadsheet. Publication is blocked while a required token is missing for an enabled locale.

#### T-1R.2-M34-07 · Feature configuration (P-R08 / P-R05 Features): capability toggles with dependency and conflict resolution, lock switches and data-retaining acknowledgement
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.2 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.1-M34-06, T-1R.1-M34-08
- **Decisions:** —

- **Description:** Implement the brief's step 6 for features. Capabilities are presented grouped by business area in plain language, pre-set from the pack defaults, with dependencies resolved automatically (turning one on turns on what it needs, with an explanation) and conflicts blocked rather than silently reconciled. Each capability can be locked so the store cannot change it. Turning off a capability that hides existing data requires an explicit acknowledgement recorded in the audit, and the screen states clearly that data is hidden, not deleted.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/domain/capabilities/configuration/`, `root-admin/app/screens/store/features/`, `root-admin/app/screens/capabilities/`

- **Backend impact:** Dependency and conflict resolver shared with the compiler
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SAAS-CAP-03 (dependencies and conflicts), TS-SAAS-CAP-04 (disable then re-enable preserves data), TS-SAAS-CFG-14 (conflicting set cannot be published)
- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Capabilities are grouped in business language with pack defaults pre-applied. (2) Enabling a capability enables its dependencies with a visible explanation. (3) A conflicting combination cannot be published. (4) Disabling a data-retaining capability requires an acknowledgement that is audited, and no data is deleted. (5) Locking a capability prevents any store-side change to it. (6) TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1R.2-M34-11 · Surface, module and delegation editor: switch applications and modules per store and choose which of them the store's administrator may manage
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1R.2 / M34
- **Depends on:** T-1R.2-M34-07, T-1A.1-M31-08
- **Decisions:** —

- **Description:** Give the operator the controls the brief asks for, at the three levels the architecture provides. Switch each **surface** (storefront, staff workspace, vendor portal) on or off for a store. Switch each **module** on or off, seeing what it contains in plain language and what is currently in use. For each module and each capability, set the control state: the store does not have it, the store has it and cannot change it, or the store's administrator may manage it. Dependencies resolve with an explanation; conflicts and invalid delegations are blocked by the compiler rather than resolved silently; and switching something off shows the open work it affects before it is confirmed. Every change is audited and takes effect through the ordinary publish path.
- **Files/components:** `root-admin/app/screens/store/features/`, `root-admin/app/screens/capabilities/`, `root-admin/domain/capabilities/control/`

- **Acceptance criteria:** (1) Surfaces, modules and capabilities can each be switched, with the module view showing what it contains in plain language. (2) Every module and capability can be set to not-available, available-and-locked, or delegated to the store. (3) An invalid delegation — a delegated capability inside a disabled module, or one whose dependency is less available — cannot be published. (4) Switching something off shows the count of open records and the run-out consequence before confirming. (5) Disabling `MOD-administration` is rejected.
