## Stage 1B.3 — Guided WhatsApp ordering

#### T-1B.3-M23-01 · WhatsApp Business Platform adapter: inbound webhook with deduplication, outbound session and template messages, 24-hour window, template status sync, opt-out handling (API-M16-10)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.3 / M23
- **Depends on:** T-1A.2-M23-01
- **Decisions:** D-014
- **References:** 06 §4.16 API-M16-10; 05 §5.16, §5.23; 16 TS-INT-03, TS-API-06; BP §13.3, §13.5
- **Description:** Build the WhatsApp Business Platform adapter (M23 WhatsAppAdapter behind the M16 WhatsAppProviderPort) for the provider chosen under D-014 (BSP or Cloud API, business/number setup, number eligibility and coexistence confirmed before any reuse is promised — BP §13.3), plus the inbound webhook API-M16-10 per 06 §4.16 and §1.8: raw-body signature check before parsing, deduplication on the provider message/event id through E-integration_event, fast acknowledgement, and one transaction per inbound customer message that finds or creates the WhatsApp E-support_conversation by WhatsApp identity (never linking or merging an account, BR-M16-08), stores the E-support_message and refreshes the customer-service window (24 hours from the last customer message, BP §13.3). Outbound, the adapter offers session (free-text) sends only while that window is open and approved-template sends otherwise and for every business-initiated message (BR-M16-04, BR-M20-04), all through E-outbox_operation with a deterministic reference, reconciliation by provider message id before any resend and a retry cap that exposes the delivery failure (BR-M17-10; 16 §8.1 WhatsApp column). Delivery statuses (sent, delivered, read, failed; out-of-order tolerated, never downgraded) update the matching E-support_message / E-notification, opt-out keywords or provider opt-out events append an E-consent_record opt_out in the same transaction as the inbound message (05 §5.16 DB/transactions; T25), and a template status sync (webhook events plus a scheduled reconciliation job) keeps E-message_template.provider_approval_state current. Inbound messages are handed to the M16 dispatcher, which in this task only routes them to the inbox; not in scope: inbox features and routing (T-1B.3-M16-01), guided A08/A15 steps (T-1B.3-M16-02, T-1B.3-M16-03), bot handoff (T-1B.3-M16-04), template authoring/submission UI and S-16 WhatsApp content (T-1B.3-M16-05), the A14 WhatsApp channel (T-1B.3-M20-01) and the adapter framework (T-1A.2-M23-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/integrations/` (WhatsApp adapter: signature verification, payload normalisation, session/template sends, template submission and status calls, message-status query, sandbox/production configuration); `backend/support/` (WhatsAppProviderPort, WhatsAppWebhookHandler for API-M16-10, template status sync and message-status reconciliation jobs); adapter contract tests next to the code in `backend/integrations/`; webhook security cases in `tests/security/` (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** No new migration (tables from DB-G0, DB-G6, DB-G7, DB-G10). Writes E-integration_event (unique integration + provider_event_id, signature_valid, processing_state received/processed/duplicate/rejected/failed), E-support_conversation (channel whatsapp, contact_identifier, counterparty_type contact until verified link, service_window_expires_at, provider_conversation_ref), E-support_message (unique provider + provider_message_id, delivery_state, template_version_id), E-consent_record (append-only opt_out rows, channel whatsapp, source STOP keyword, evidence = inbound message id), E-message_template.provider_approval_state / provider_template_ref, E-notification state and provider_message_id for WhatsApp sends, E-outbox_operation, E-attachment (inbound media as private files); E-integration_setting row integration_code whatsapp per environment with contract, fallback_mode and support owner (S-18 record for the WhatsApp provider, loaded through the T-1A.2-M24-02 mechanism once D-014 is decided)
- **API impact:** Implements API-M16-10 (SIG · `webhook.whatsapp`; `401 SIGNATURE_INVALID`, duplicate → `200` no effect). Provides the provider calls behind API-M16-07, API-M16-18, API-M10-20 and API-M20-03 (their WhatsApp paths are wired by T-1B.3-M16-01, T-1B.3-M16-05, T-1B.3-M16-02 and T-1B.3-M20-01); integration status and test call through the existing API-M24-03 and API-M24-04 (consumed)
- **Frontend impact:** None (the WhatsApp integration appears on the existing P-E15 #integrations card through API-M24-03; no new screen)
- **Backend impact:** M23 WhatsAppAdapter (send session message, send template message, submit template, query template status, query message status); M16 WhatsAppProviderPort and WhatsAppWebhookHandler; jobs: outbox send worker for WhatsApp, template status sync with the provider, message-status reconciliation (05 §5.16 Jobs, §1.3); rules BR-M23-01 (integration contract), BR-M23-02 (fallback: website/email/support handoff), BR-M23-04, BR-M23-05, BR-M16-04, BR-M16-05, BR-M16-08, BR-M20-04, BR-M08-06, BR-M08-07, BR-M17-10, BR-M17-11; retry cap → one exception (A38); provider signature scheme and capabilities per D-014; no complete chat content, tokens or secrets in technical logs (BP §19.1; BR-M02-11)
- **Testing requirements:** TS-INT-03 adapter cases on the provider sandbox (inbound dedup, 24-hour window and approved templates, delivery status, opt-out) including every WhatsApp cell of the 16 §8.1 fault matrix (timeout before/after send, duplicate, out-of-order, worker crash, invalid signature, provider unavailable, retry cap); TS-API-06 for API-M16-10 (raw-body signature before parsing, persist + dedup, duplicate no effect, out-of-order legal only, fast acknowledgement); TS-PERM-04.4 and TS-AUTH-09 (forged/unsigned WhatsApp webhook rejected); TS-SVC-02 (outbox crash reconciliation); TS-DB-04 (E-integration_event and E-consent_record append-only); TS-SEC-06 (no complete chat content in logs); TS-INT-10 (WhatsApp contract checklist complete); T25 precondition (opt-out captured)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A call to API-M16-10 with a missing or invalid signature returns `401 SIGNATURE_INVALID`, is stored as rejected and changes no conversation, message, consent or template record (TS-PERM-04.4).
   2. The same provider message or status event delivered twice yields one processed E-integration_event (the repeat marked duplicate), one E-support_message and a `200` response for both (TS-API-06).
   3. An inbound customer message creates or reuses the WhatsApp conversation for that WhatsApp identity without linking or merging any customer account, and sets service_window_expires_at to 24 hours after the message, in the same transaction as the message record.
   4. A session (free-text) send is refused by the adapter when the window is closed; a template send is accepted only for a template version whose provider_approval_state is approved; every send goes through E-outbox_operation and stores the provider message id.
   5. Delivery statuses update the matching E-support_message or E-notification; a late "delivered" after "read" does not downgrade the state; a message still failing after the retry cap shows a visible delivery failure and leaves the related order or conversation unchanged.
   6. An opt-out keyword or provider opt-out event appends an E-consent_record opt_out (channel whatsapp, source STOP keyword, evidence = inbound message id) and later prohibited sends to that contact are blocked (T25 precondition).
   7. Template status events and the scheduled sync update provider_approval_state (approved, rejected, paused); rejected and paused versions cannot be sent.
   8. A timeout after a send is resolved by querying the provider message id before any resend (no duplicate customer message), and a worker crash between send and save is recovered by the outbox scanner (TS-SVC-02).
   9. With the provider unavailable, sends return `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` and the documented fallback (website/email/support handoff) is recorded in E-integration_setting.fallback_mode; staging and production credentials are separate records.
   10. A log scan after the suite run finds no complete message bodies, tokens or secrets (TS-SEC-06).
   11. The WhatsApp integration contract checklist (BR-M23-01) is complete and TS-INT-03 and TS-API-06 pass on the provider sandbox.
   12. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1B.3-M16-01 · Shared inbox WhatsApp channel: conversations, service-window state, templates outside the window, automation pause per conversation, routing; P-E05 #inbox WhatsApp features
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.3 / M16
- **Depends on:** T-1B.3-M23-01, T-1A.13-M16-04, T-1B.3-M16-05
- **Decisions:** D-074, D-004
- **References:** 04b §8.2; 05 §5.16; 06 API-M16-04…08; 16 TS-ERP-18, TS-INT-03; BP §13.3, §13.4
- **Description:** Add the WhatsApp channel to the shared inbox built for the web channel in 1A.13 (backend T-1A.13-M16-02, P-E05 T-1A.13-M16-04): API-M16-04 lists WhatsApp conversations with window_state and a masked contact until verified, API-M16-05 returns window{open, closes_at}, consent{marketing, service} and automation_paused, and API-M16-06 returns each message with its delivery state. API-M16-07 for WhatsApp accepts free text and approved answers only inside the 24-hour customer-service window and otherwise only approved templates (`409 WINDOW_CLOSED_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED`), blocks templates whose purpose lacks a current opt-in (`403 CONSENT_MISSING`, T25) and sends through the outbox to the WhatsApp adapter (BR-M16-04, BR-M20-04); API-M16-08 supports for WhatsApp assign, close (a customer reply reopens), pause/resume automation so the bot and automatic updates stay silent (BR-M16-11), staff-recorded opt-out, and identity linking only with verification evidence, never by name match (BR-M16-08). New and handed-off WhatsApp conversations are routed to agents whose availability (API-M16-19, 1A.13) is "available", and a service-window expiry job marks conversations "Template only"; routing and handoff rules are REQUIRES_DECISION (D-074), live updates D-146, native vs custom P-E05 per D-004. Not in scope: adapter and webhook (T-1B.3-M23-01), draft baskets (T-1B.3-M16-02), verified order status (T-1B.3-M16-03), bot handoff and SLA timers (T-1B.3-M16-04), template authoring/submission (T-1B.3-M16-05).
- **Files/components:** `backend/support/` (ConversationService WhatsApp channel, routing, service-window expiry job, send validation); `frontend/workspace/` P-E05 #inbox WhatsApp features only if D-004 decides "custom" (otherwise configuration in `backend/`); service/API tests next to the code; `tests/acceptance/` for TS-ERP-18 cases (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** No new migration. Uses DB-G10 E-support_conversation (channel whatsapp, state, owner_user_id, priority, automation_paused, service_window_expires_at, identity_verification, customer_id only after verified link) and E-support_message (template_version_id required for out-of-window sends, delivery_state, attachments); DB-G6 E-consent_record (staff-recorded opt-out rows, read for consent state); DB-G7 E-message_template (approved WhatsApp versions, read); DB-G0 E-outbox_operation and E-audit_event (assign, pause/resume, opt-out, identity link)
- **API impact:** Extends to the WhatsApp channel API-M16-04, API-M16-05, API-M16-06, API-M16-07 (`409 WINDOW_CLOSED_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED`, `403 CONSENT_MISSING`) and API-M16-08 (implemented for web chat by T-1A.13-M16-02). Consumes API-M16-17 (template list from T-1B.3-M16-05), API-M16-14 (quick answers), API-M16-19 (agent availability), API-M22-01 (attachments) and API-M20-04 (delivery status)
- **Frontend impact:** P-E05 #inbox WhatsApp features (04b §8.2): channel filter "WhatsApp"; conversation items with WhatsApp icon, masked number or "Unknown contact", verified / not-verified icon, "Template only" badge when the window is closed, status pill, assignee; thread window bar (open · closes in … / closed at …), window-closed callout (free text not allowed, marketing blocked after opt-out), composer disabled with the template placeholder when closed, templates menu (approved WhatsApp templates, marketing disabled without consent) and quick answers, "Send template" result text, attach disabled when closed, per-message delivery states with failed + retry; sub-bar "Pause automation in this conversation" with system line; side-pane Consent rows (service replies in window, order & return updates, marketing) with "Record opt-out"; click-to-chat system line "product reference — a reference, not a trusted price"; provider-unavailable `503` banner with conversations still readable
- **Backend impact:** M16 ConversationService (WhatsApp channel, assignment, routing to available agents, close/reopen), outbound sends via E-outbox_operation → M23 WhatsAppAdapter, service-window expiry marking job (05 §5.16 Jobs); rules BR-M16-04, BR-M16-06, BR-M16-07 (masking until verified), BR-M16-08, BR-M16-11, BR-M20-03, BR-M20-04, BR-M08-06, BR-M08-07; permissions `support.inbox`, `support.conversation.manage` (07 §13); message bodies never in technical logs (BR-M02-11)
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-18 (assignment, automation pause in a conversation, verification-state masking, templates outside the window); TS-INT-03 inbox cases on the sandbox (window and approved templates, delivery status, identity linking only after verification); TS-API-01 contract cases for API-M16-04…API-M16-08 on the WhatsApp channel incl. `409 WINDOW_CLOSED_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED` and `403 CONSENT_MISSING`; TS-API-05 (inbox filters intersected with scope); TS-PERM-02.10 (conversation BOLA); TS-FE-03 (P-E05 WhatsApp states, if custom); TS-SEC-06; T25 (marketing template blocked for an opted-out contact)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. API-M16-04 with channel=whatsapp lists only conversations in the caller's assigned scope, each with window_state and a masked contact until the conversation is verified.
   2. API-M16-05 returns window{open, closes_at}, consent and automation_paused for a WhatsApp conversation and no order, address, serial or payment data before verification.
   3. After the window closes a free-text send returns `409 WINDOW_CLOSED_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED`; an approved utility template is sent and its template_version_id stored; a marketing template to an opted-out contact returns `403 CONSENT_MISSING` and nothing is sent.
   4. Pausing automation stops bot replies and automatic updates in that conversation until resumed; pause and resume appear as system lines and are audited.
   5. "Record opt-out" appends a staff-recorded E-consent_record and the side pane shows the new consent state at once.
   6. link_identity without verification evidence is rejected; no account link or merge happens on a name match.
   7. A new WhatsApp conversation is routed only to agents whose availability is "available" (never to busy or away agents), following the rules decided under D-074.
   8. Each outbound message shows sent, delivered, read or failed; failed offers retry; with the provider down P-E05 shows the `503` banner and conversations stay readable.
   9. TS-ERP-18 and the TS-INT-03 inbox cases pass.
   10. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1B.3-M16-02 · Guided WhatsApp ordering A08: guided item/quantity selection → draft basket, customer confirms price and address, ambiguity → agent; P-E05 m-basket; storefront L2 entry points and basket checkout-link landing
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.3 / M16
- **Depends on:** T-1B.3-M16-01, T-1A.13-M10-01
- **Decisions:** D-151, D-014
- **References:** 08 §4.24; 04b §8.5; 06 API-M10-18…22; 16 TS-ECOM-11, TS-E2E-05; BP §13.2, §29.5; A08
- **Description:** Implement A08 guided WhatsApp ordering (BP §13.1 Level 2, §13.2, §29.5): a deterministic guided "buy" step (GuidedFlowService, no LLM) takes the product reference carried by click-to-chat — a reference, never a trusted price — and guided buttons/forms for item and quantity (provider capabilities per D-014), resolves them to exactly one approved SKU/offer and condition, and creates a draft basket in the main order system through M10 AssistedOrderService in-process (source whatsapp_basket, conversation_id; E-sales_order state draft, order_channel whatsapp) priced by the single pricing engine; several matching configurations or conditions, a missing reference or unconfirmed text go to an agent, and an order is never inferred from unconfirmed text (BR-M16-02, BR-M16-03, BR-M10-10). Agents build or complete the basket in P-E05 m-basket on a verified conversation using API-M10-18 and API-M10-19 (delivered by T-1A.13-M10-01), and the secure checkout link is sent as an approved WhatsApp template by extending API-M10-20 with channel whatsapp_template (consent, approved template, no pending approval on the draft). The customer confirms address and final price on P-S07 opened from the link (API-M10-22) and pays through API-M10-06 → API-M11-01 with the same reservation, payment and fulfilment controls as web checkout; whether stock is reserved when the link is sent or when the customer confirms is REQUIRES_DECISION (D-151) (durations D-026, draft expiry D-150). On the storefront, the Level 2 entry points (P-S01 WhatsApp ordering explainer, shell(S) WhatsApp button, P-S13 WhatsApp card) start the guided flow with the page reference behind a feature flag (BR-M01-05; launch scope D-048), and the P-S07 link landing gains the WhatsApp-basket states. Not in scope: assisted-order core, P-E02 m-assisted and the base link landing (T-1A.13-M10-01), Level 1 click-to-chat (T-1A.13-M16-03), handoff mechanics and SLA (T-1B.3-M16-04), A08 activation in S-17 (T-1B.4-M17-02).
- **Files/components:** `backend/support/` (GuidedFlowService WhatsApp buy step, A08 rule); `backend/orders/` (AssistedOrderService source whatsapp_basket, CheckoutLinkService channel whatsapp_template); `frontend/workspace/` P-E05 m-basket, draft-basket card and side-pane actions only if D-004 decides "custom"; `frontend/storefront/` (P-S01 explainer, shell WhatsApp button, P-S13 WhatsApp card, P-S07 link-landing states); `tests/acceptance/` (TS-ECOM-11), `tests/e2e/` (TS-E2E-05) (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** No new migration. Uses DB-G7 E-sales_order (state draft, order_channel whatsapp, source_reference → E-support_conversation, quote_id/quote_version), E-order_line, E-quote, E-quote_line, E-reservation (created at the point decided by D-151), E-notification and E-message_template (link template), E-idempotency_record; DB-G0 E-approval_request (discount above authority), E-automation_rule record for A08 (activated by T-1B.4-M17-02); DB-G6 E-consent_record (checked); DB-G10 E-support_message (bot messages, draft-basket and checkout events)
- **API impact:** Consumes API-M10-18, API-M10-19 and API-M10-22 (T-1A.13-M10-01) with source whatsapp_basket and conversation_id; extends API-M10-20 with channel whatsapp_template (Idem; REQUIRES_DECISION D-151, D-014). Consumes API-M05-01, API-M21-01, API-M04-03, API-M10-06, API-M11-01, API-M16-05 and API-M16-07; the bot creates drafts through AssistedOrderService in-process, not through the staff endpoint (06 §1.1 rule 5)
- **Frontend impact:** P-E05 m-basket (04b §8.5: source callout "never infers an order from unconfirmed text", lines with rule and payable total, "Send link via" WhatsApp approved template / SMS / email, link & reservation expiry select, reservation explanation per D-151, foot "Open as assisted order" → P-E02 / "Save draft" / "Send secure checkout link"); P-E05 header "Draft basket" and side-pane actions "Create draft basket" (verified only) and "Send secure checkout link"; thread draft-basket card (items, rule, total, link expiry, "Converted · {order}"). Storefront: P-S01 WhatsApp ordering explainer, shell(S) WhatsApp button and P-S13 WhatsApp card in their Level 2 form; P-S07 link landing for WhatsApp baskets (base landing with T-1A.13-M10-01): draft lines fixed by the WhatsApp flow, recomputed quote with `PRICE_CHANGED` acceptance, `LINK_EXPIRED` state with a WhatsApp/support route
- **Backend impact:** M16 GuidedFlowService (buy step, skipped while automation is paused — BR-M16-11); M10 AssistedOrderService and CheckoutLinkService; M05 PricingEngine (one price calculation); M06 reservation per D-151 (TX-1 at order placement); A08 implemented to its BP §12.3 template (BR-M17-01; kill switch BR-M17-15); rules BR-M16-02, BR-M16-03, BR-M10-05, BR-M10-10, BR-M10-11 (staff discount within authority, else approval, D-024), BR-M10-17 (shared order reference), BR-M08-13; buyer context stays public unless the WhatsApp identity is securely linked (BR-M16-08) — chat never selects a dealer price
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-11 (live price and stock, chat reference not trusted, secure link, same reservation and payment controls; reservation-timing cases once D-151 is decided); TS-E2E-05 steps 1–5 on staging with the provider sandbox; TS-API-01 (API-M10-18 whatsapp_basket source, API-M10-20 whatsapp_template channel); TS-API-03 (API-M10-20 replay/conflict); TS-API-10 and T10 (price in the chat text ignored); TS-AUTH-07 (link token bound to one draft, expiry, no enumeration); TS-UNIT-04 (draft → awaiting_payment / cancelled guards); TS-FE-02 (P-S07 link states) and TS-FE-03 (m-basket); TS-INT-03 (link template send); T24 (ambiguous item → agent)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. A click-to-chat message carrying a product reference and a price creates no order; the guided step resolves the reference to one explicit SKU/offer and condition and the draft price comes from the pricing engine, ignoring the price in the message (T10).
   2. When more than one configuration or condition matches, or item or quantity is unconfirmed, no draft is created and the conversation is handed to an agent with the reference and transcript.
   3. A draft from the guided flow or m-basket is an E-sales_order in state draft with order_channel whatsapp and source_reference to the conversation; saving a draft reserves no stock.
   4. "Create draft basket" is enabled only for verified conversations; a staff discount above the caller's authority returns `202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED` and no link can be sent while that approval is pending.
   5. API-M10-20 with channel whatsapp_template sends only an approved template to a contact with the required consent; a repeat with the same idempotency key returns the stored result; the link token is single-purpose, bound to the draft and expiring (TS-AUTH-07).
   6. Opening the link recomputes the price (a changed price needs explicit acceptance); the customer confirms the address and pays through API-M10-06 → API-M11-01, and the order keeps one shared reference shown as "Converted" in P-E05 and in P-E02.
   7. Stock is reserved exactly at the point decided under D-151 with the same atomic reservation and expiry rules as web checkout; an expired link shows `LINK_EXPIRED` with a WhatsApp/support route.
   8. No guided message is sent into a conversation whose automation is paused.
   9. With the Level 2 feature flag off, the storefront entry points keep their Level 1 click-to-chat behaviour.
   10. TS-ECOM-11 and TS-E2E-05 steps 1–5 pass on the provider sandbox.
   11. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1B.3-M16-03 · Verified order status over WhatsApp A15 (API-M16-09) — no disclosure without verification
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.3 / M16
- **Depends on:** T-1B.3-M16-01, T-1A.13-M16-02
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 06 API-M16-09; 16 TS-PERM-06; BP §13.4, §12.2 A15; T23 (WhatsApp)
- **Description:** Implement A15 "where is my order?" over WhatsApp (BP §12.2 A15, §13.2 "Verify order access → Return permitted order status", §13.4): the guided "track my order" step asks for the order number, sends a one-time code only to the phone on that order through ChatVerificationService (the logic behind API-M16-09 send_otp / verify_otp → M02 OtpService, E-verification_challenge) and, after successful verification, replies with the permitted status of that order (order, payment and fulfilment states, BP §10.1) only (BR-M16-15). Addresses, invoices, serials and payment information are never revealed without verification (BR-M16-07); the verification covers only the verified order in that conversation, so a request for another order gets no disclosure (TS-PERM-06.2), and wrong or expired codes, rate limits (D-084) and third-party requests end with no disclosure and an offer of call-back to the registered number or a human handoff with context. Staff use the same controls in P-E05 for WhatsApp conversations: API-M16-09 actions, the identity section, the linked-orders card and the "Order status" insert, which stay blocked until verified; while automation is paused the bot does not answer and the agent verifies. Verification of one order never links or merges the WhatsApp identity with an account (BR-M16-08). Not in scope: API-M16-09 and web-chat verification core (T-1A.13-M16-02), guest order access API-M10-10 and API-M10-11, handoff mechanics (T-1B.3-M16-04), A15 activation in S-17 (T-1B.4-M17-02).
- **Files/components:** `backend/support/` (ChatVerificationService A15 for WhatsApp, GuidedFlowService track step); `frontend/workspace/` P-E05 identity / linked-orders / order-status insert for WhatsApp only if D-004 decides "custom"; `tests/acceptance/` (T23 WhatsApp), `tests/security/` (TS-PERM-06) (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** No new migration. Uses E-verification_challenge (DB-G1, migrated with T-1A.2-M02-05), E-support_conversation.identity_verification {method, verified_at, scope} and linked_order_ids (DB-G10), E-exception_case (call-back task, DB-G0), E-audit_event, E-automation_rule record for A15 (activated by T-1B.4-M17-02); reads E-sales_order and fulfilment states through M10/M12 query services
- **API impact:** Extends API-M16-09 (send_otp, verify_otp, callback_registered_number; `422 CODE_INVALID`, `429`) and API-M16-05 linked_orders (verified only) to WhatsApp conversations; the bot uses ChatVerificationService in-process; consumes M02 OtpService and M10 OrderQueryService in-process (no new endpoint)
- **Frontend impact:** P-E05 side pane Identity (Verified by OTP / Not verified / Guest; "Resend OTP", "Call-back to registered no."), Linked orders ("Order details hidden until verified") and the composer "Order status" insert ("Blocked — verify identity before sharing order details") for WhatsApp conversations (04b §8.2); no storefront change
- **Backend impact:** M16 ChatVerificationService (A15) and GuidedFlowService track step; M02 OtpService with rate limits and lockout (BR-M02-09, D-084); M10 OrderQueryService; A15 implemented to its BP §12.3 template (BR-M17-01); rules BR-M16-07, BR-M16-08, BR-M16-12, BR-M16-15, BR-M02-11 (codes never logged); call-back requests create an E-exception_case task
- **Testing requirements:** TS-PERM-06 cases 06.1 (unverified WhatsApp user asks for status, address, invoice or serial → no disclosure, verification offered, handoff) and 06.2 (verified for O1, asks for O2 → no disclosure); T23 (WhatsApp); TS-PERM-02.10; TS-API-01 for API-M16-09 on WhatsApp conversations; TS-AUTH-03 (OTP rate limit and lockout); TS-AUTH-10 and TS-SEC-06 (codes and message bodies absent from logs); TS-ECOM-12 verification-before-disclosure cases
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. An unverified WhatsApp contact asking for the status, address, invoice or serial of any order receives no order data; verification and a handoff are offered (TS-PERM-06.1).
   2. The one-time code goes only to the phone number on the order, and the reply never reveals whether the order number exists or whose phone it belongs to.
   3. After a successful verify_otp the bot replies with the permitted status of that order only; a request for a different order in the same conversation gets no disclosure (TS-PERM-06.2).
   4. A wrong or expired code returns `422 CODE_INVALID` with no disclosure; repeated failures hit the rate limit or lockout with `429` (values D-084).
   5. A call-back request creates exactly one E-exception_case task and discloses nothing in the chat.
   6. Verification does not link or merge the WhatsApp identity with a customer account.
   7. In P-E05 the linked orders and the "Order status" insert are blocked for an unverified WhatsApp conversation and available after verification; while automation is paused the bot sends no status reply.
   8. Codes, tokens and message bodies are absent from technical logs.
   9. T23 (WhatsApp) and TS-PERM-06 pass.
   10. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1B.3-M16-04 · Bot-to-human handoff with context, escalation categories and SLA timers
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.3 / M16
- **Depends on:** T-1B.3-M16-02
- **Decisions:** D-074
- **References:** 05 §5.16; 16 TS-ECOM-12; BP §13.4; T24
- **Description:** Implement the WhatsApp bot-to-human handoff (BP §13.3 "clear escalation path when automation is used", §13.4; T24): when the guided bot cannot resolve a request — free text it cannot map to a guided option (never answered by guessing), ambiguity from A08, failed verification, a flow or provider failure, "talk to a person", or an escalation topic — the conversation moves to handed_off with a visible handoff marker (queue or agent and reason), keeping the full transcript, verification state, product/order references and any draft basket as context, and the bot stays silent afterwards (BR-M16-10, BR-M16-12, BR-M16-13). Escalation categories (payment disputes, warranty ambiguity, missing orders, unsafe product issues, uncertain compatibility) always go to a person and can become tickets through API-M16-11 with the transcript attached and the customer told by an approved template when the window is closed; the category catalogue and priorities are REQUIRES_DECISION (D-074), codes per D-139. SLA timers: a scheduled job computes and tracks conversation accept/first-response due times and ticket sla_due_at from priority and support hours held in configuration, shows due and breached states in the inbox and ticket list, and escalates a breach once (05 §5.16 Jobs; BR-M16-06, BR-M17-12); hours, SLA targets, handoff rules and after-hours behaviour are REQUIRES_DECISION (D-074). Outside support hours the WhatsApp customer receives the after-hours message with a reference while guided help and order tracking remain available (BP §6.3 Help). Not in scope: web-chat handoff and ticket endpoints (T-1A.13-M16-02), agent routing (T-1B.3-M16-01), activation of A08/A15 (T-1B.4-M17-02).
- **Files/components:** `backend/support/` (GuidedFlowService handoff triggers, ConversationService handoff state, TicketService escalation from WhatsApp, SLA timer and escalation job); `frontend/workspace/` P-E05 handoff marker, SLA texts and #tickets SLA states only if D-004 decides "custom"; `tests/acceptance/` (T24, TS-ECOM-12) (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** No new migration. Uses DB-G10 E-support_conversation (state handed_off, owner_user_id, priority), E-support_message (system handoff marker), E-support_ticket (category, priority, sla_due_at, state, linked records); DB-G0 E-configuration_version for support hours, SLA targets and handoff rules (values D-074; support contact channels S-28); E-notification for the ticket-created notice
- **API impact:** Extends for WhatsApp conversations API-M16-11 (escalation ticket with related.conversation_id, keep_conversation_open, notify_customer_template), API-M16-12 (breached status, sla_due), API-M16-13 and the `sla` field of API-M16-04; handoff markers delivered through API-M16-06; consumes API-M16-02 ("Talk to a person" option) and API-M16-20 (hours, open state)
- **Frontend impact:** P-E05 #inbox: handoff marker in the thread ("Handed off to human · {agent/queue} · reason"), status pills Waiting for agent / Escalated · ticket / Escalated · safety, SLA texts on conversation items ("Reply in n min", "Accept in n min", "Breached n"); m-ticket from a WhatsApp conversation with "Keep the conversation open & notify" (template); #tickets SLA meter (due / breached / paused / met) and "Breached" filter (04b §8.2, §8.3, §8.6); SLA values shown are configuration, not mockup samples
- **Backend impact:** M16 GuidedFlowService (handoff triggers), ConversationService (handed_off state, context preserved), TicketService (escalation categories), SLA timer and escalation job (05 §5.16 Jobs); rules BR-M16-04, BR-M16-06, BR-M16-10, BR-M16-12, BR-M16-13, BR-M17-12; BR-M23-02 fallback (provider unavailable → website/email/support handoff); no hard-coded hours or SLA values (12 §1.2)
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ECOM-12 (bot failure → handoff with context, outside hours, escalation categories never answered by the bot); T24; TS-INT-03 human-handoff case on the sandbox; TS-ERP-18 (tickets and escalation categories, SLA states); TS-API-01 for API-M16-11 and API-M16-12 WhatsApp cases; TS-ERR-03 (WhatsApp provider outage → documented support handoff)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Unmapped free text, an ambiguous item, a failed verification or "talk to a person" moves the conversation to handed_off with a handoff marker and reason; the agent sees the transcript and context, and the bot sends nothing further (T24).
   2. The bot never answers an escalation-category topic; it hands off, and a ticket created from the conversation keeps the full transcript linked through related.conversation_id.
   3. A ticket-created notice sent after the window has closed uses an approved template only.
   4. SLA due times are computed from the configured priority targets and support hours; a conversation or ticket past due shows as breached in API-M16-04 and API-M16-12 and is escalated once.
   5. No SLA, hours or handoff value is hard-coded; a new configuration version changes due times for items created afterwards.
   6. Outside support hours the WhatsApp customer receives the after-hours message with a reference, and guided help and order tracking still work.
   7. With the WhatsApp provider unavailable the documented fallback is used and the failure is visible to staff.
   8. T24 and the TS-ECOM-12 handoff cases pass.
   9. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1B.3-M16-05 · WhatsApp template management and provider review submission; S-16 WhatsApp templates (API-M16-17, API-M16-18)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.3 / M16
- **Depends on:** T-1B.3-M23-01, T-1A.13-M16-04
- **Decisions:** D-058, D-050, D-004
- **References:** 06 API-M16-17, API-M16-18; 03 §6 S-16; 16 TS-INT-03; BP §13.3
- **Description:** Build WhatsApp template management (BP §13.3 "template approval", §13.5 template categories; 11 §9.4): TemplateService implements API-M16-17 (templates with channel, category, version, provider status, last sent, consent rule) and API-M16-18 (submit a new or changed template → a new immutable E-message_template version in state submitted → provider review through the WhatsApp adapter; `503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`), and provider results (approved, rejected, paused) arrive through the template status sync of T-1B.3-M23-01. Only approved versions are sendable, each template carries a consent purpose that must match an opt-in purpose (D-058), its language (D-050) and a provider category (rules per D-014), and no debt-collection template is configured (restricted use, BP §13.5; BR-M16-14). P-E05 #library gets the "WhatsApp message templates" section with "Submit template" for R-ops_admin, and the composer templates menu reads API-M16-17. Load the WhatsApp part of S-16 — approved templates per event/purpose and language — only with decided values and after provider approval (TS-DB-05). Not in scope: email/SMS templates of S-16 (T-1A.13-M20-01), approved answers (T-1A.13-M16-01), sending templates (T-1B.3-M16-01, T-1B.3-M16-02, T-1B.3-M20-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/support/` (TemplateService); S-16 WhatsApp seed scripts in `backend/` (03 §6); `frontend/workspace/` P-E05 #library WhatsApp templates section and composer template data only if D-004 decides "custom"; API and adapter tests next to the code (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** No new migration (E-message_template is DB-G7). Writes E-message_template WhatsApp versions (name/version, channel whatsapp, category, language, body/variables, consent_purpose, provider_approval_state draft/submitted/approved/rejected/paused, provider_template_ref, state), E-integration_event (submission and status events), E-audit_event; seed S-16 (WhatsApp templates; values D-014, D-050, D-058)
- **API impact:** Implements API-M16-17 (`messaging.template.read`) and API-M16-18 (`messaging.template.manage`, R-ops_admin; REQUIRES_DECISION D-014; `503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`); uses the template submission and status calls of the WhatsApp adapter (T-1B.3-M23-01)
- **Frontend impact:** P-E05 #library "WhatsApp message templates" (04b §8.4): sub text, "Submit template" (fields name, channel, category, body, variables, consent rule), table Template · Category (Utility / Authentication / Marketing) · Version · Status · last sent (Approved / In review / Rejected + reason) · Rule / consent, footer note that debt-collection messages are a restricted use with no template configured; data for the P-E05 composer "Approved WhatsApp templates" menu
- **Backend impact:** M16 TemplateService → M23 WhatsAppAdapter (submission, status); versioned-content rule (a change creates a new version, approved versions are immutable — 03 §1); rules BR-M16-04, BR-M16-05, BR-M16-14, BR-M20-04; permissions `messaging.template.read` (R-sales_support, R-branch_manager read) and `messaging.template.manage` (R-ops_admin) per 07 §5
- **Testing requirements:** TS-INT-03 template cases on the sandbox (submission, approval/rejection/pause via status sync, only approved templates sendable); TS-API-01 for API-M16-17 and API-M16-18 incl. `503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`; TS-PERM-01 (key × role for `messaging.template.manage`); TS-DB-05 (S-16 WhatsApp templates load only decided values); TS-ERP-18 templates cases; TS-FE-03 (#library section, if custom)
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. API-M16-18 creates a new E-message_template version with provider_approval_state submitted and returns `202`; earlier approved versions remain unchanged.
   2. Approval, rejection (with the provider's reason where supplied) and pause from the status sync appear in API-M16-17 and in P-E05 #library.
   3. Only approved versions appear in the composer templates menu and are accepted by send operations; marketing templates are disabled for contacts without marketing consent.
   4. Every WhatsApp template has a category, a language and a consent purpose that matches an opt-in purpose; no debt-collection template exists.
   5. R-sales_support and R-branch_manager can read templates only; a submission by any role other than R-ops_admin returns `403`.
   6. With the provider unavailable API-M16-18 returns `503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` and the version stays in draft.
   7. S-16 WhatsApp templates are loaded only from decided values (D-058 events and purposes, D-050 languages) and TS-DB-05 passes.

#### T-1B.3-M20-01 · WhatsApp channel for A14 notifications with consent and opt-out
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.3 / M20
- **Depends on:** T-1B.3-M23-01, T-1A.13-M20-02, T-1B.3-M16-05
- **Decisions:** D-058
- **References:** 05 §5.20; 16 TS-SVC-05, TS-ECOM-15; BP §13.3; T25
- **Description:** Add WhatsApp as a delivery channel of the A14 status notifications built in 1A.13 (service T-1A.13-M20-01, event subscriptions T-1A.13-M20-02): for events whose channel list includes WhatsApp (event and channel list REQUIRES_DECISION (D-058)), NotificationService checks the recipient's current WhatsApp consent for the event's purpose (opted out → not sent, recorded as suppressed with the consent reference; T25), requires an approved WhatsApp template in the recipient's language for every business-initiated message (BR-M20-04; D-050), applies frequency caps and the dedupe key, and sends through the outbox to the WhatsApp adapter (02 §17). WhatsApp delivery statuses received by API-M16-10 update E-notification; failures are retried and then exposed through API-M20-04 while the order stays valid (BR-M20-02). Opt-outs captured from WhatsApp replies or recorded by staff take effect before the next send, including conditional A28 reminders if enabled, and payment reminders stay distinct from debt collection (BR-M20-03, BR-M16-14). Staff-triggered messages (API-M20-03) accept channel whatsapp under the same checks, and no automatic update is sent into a conversation whose automation is paused (04b §8.2; BR-M16-11). Not in scope: email/SMS channels and event subscriptions (1A.13), WhatsApp template content and approval (T-1B.3-M16-05), the adapter and webhook (T-1B.3-M23-01).
- **Files/components:** `backend/notifications/` (NotificationService WhatsApp channel, DeliveryStatusHandler for WhatsApp statuses); service tests next to the code; `tests/acceptance/` (T25 WhatsApp) (finer structure per D-001/D-003)
- **Database impact:** No new migration. Uses DB-G7 E-notification (channel whatsapp, template_version_id, consent_check, state queued/sent/delivered/failed/suppressed, dedupe_key, provider_message_id, attempts, failure_reason, outbox_operation_id) and E-message_template (approved WhatsApp versions); DB-G6 E-consent_record (read; opt-out rows); DB-G1 E-notification_preference (channels, read); DB-G0 E-outbox_operation; frequency caps from configuration (values D-058)
- **API impact:** Extends API-M20-03 (channel whatsapp; `403 CONSENT_MISSING`, template-only rule) and API-M20-04 (WhatsApp delivery states); consumes WhatsApp status events from API-M16-10 (T-1B.3-M23-01) and consent from API-M08-10
- **Frontend impact:** None (WhatsApp delivery status appears in the existing P-E02 #od-time, P-E04 and P-E05 views through API-M20-04)
- **Backend impact:** M20 NotificationService, TemplateRenderer and DeliveryStatusHandler with the WhatsApp channel through M23 WhatsAppAdapter; A14 (and A28 only if enabled, CONDITIONAL); rules BR-M20-01, BR-M20-02, BR-M20-03, BR-M20-04, BR-M20-06, BR-M08-06, BR-M08-07, BR-M16-11, BR-M16-14, BR-M17-10
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SVC-05 on the WhatsApp channel (approved transitions only, consent per purpose, templates, frequency caps, delivery failure visible with the order valid); TS-ECOM-15 (opted-out customer never messaged on WhatsApp; A28 stop rules when enabled); T25 (WhatsApp); TS-INT-03 delivery-status and opt-out cases on the sandbox; TS-SVC-02 (outbox); TS-ERR-01 "notification fails" case
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. For an approved transition whose channel list includes WhatsApp, a consented recipient receives exactly one WhatsApp message from an approved template in the recipient's language (one dedupe_key).
   2. A recipient who opted out (STOP reply or staff-recorded) receives no WhatsApp message for that purpose; the E-notification is recorded as suppressed with the consent reference (T25).
   3. Every A14 WhatsApp send references an approved template version; without one, nothing is sent and the reason is recorded and visible.
   4. Frequency caps from configuration are enforced per recipient (values D-058).
   5. A delivery failure after the retry cap is visible through API-M20-04 with reason and attempts, and the order state is unchanged.
   6. API-M20-03 with channel whatsapp enforces consent (`403 CONSENT_MISSING`) and the template-only rule.
   7. No automatic WhatsApp update is sent into a conversation whose automation is paused.
   8. TS-SVC-05, TS-ECOM-15 and T25 (WhatsApp) pass.
   9. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1B.3-M16-06 · Stage 1B.3 verification: T23 (WhatsApp), T24, T25 (WhatsApp); TS-E2E-05; TS-INT-03; chat-to-order and handoff demonstration

## Stage 1B.4 — Approval extensions, selected integrations & P1B automations

#### T-1B.4-M17-01 · Approval extensions: remaining approval types (vendor-related, payout changes, other 1B types), approval ageing, recurring-approval policy review
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.4 / M17
- **Depends on:** T-1A.2-M17-01, T-1B.1-M14-05, T-1B.1-M14-07, T-1A.14-M17-06, T-1A.15-M18-01, T-1B.1-M14-08
- **Decisions:** D-192
- **References:** 11 §4.2, §4.3; 10 §14.1; 04c §6 (approval ageing 1B); BP §5.1 (1B approvals)
- **Description:** Extends the 1A approval core (T-1A.2-M17-01: ApprovalService, threshold × role resolution, requester ≠ approver, expected-version decisions) and the approval queue (T-1A.14-M17-06: P-E14 #approvals, m-approve, deadlines, reminders, escalation, recurring flag) with the approval types that D-192 assigns to 1B — at least the 1B rows of 11 §4.2: payout_account_change (#10, maker-checker with call-back), vendor_content (#11, designated reviewer) and vendor account_reinstatement (#30) — plus approval ageing (BP §14.3 'Approval ageing', marked 1B in MK:erp-reports.html; 04c §6.2) and the recurring-approval policy review (BP §12.6; BR-M17-13). It does not rebuild the approval service, the queue screen or the requesting flows: payout-change submission and the vendor-side checker stay in T-1B.1-M14-05 (API-M14-43, API-M14-69), submission review in T-1B.1-M14-07 (API-M14-54, API-M17-03) and suspension/reinstatement requests in T-1B.1-M14-08 (API-M14-51). Every 1B approval records why it was required, deadline, alternate approver, escalation rule and outcome (BR-M17-06; BP §18.2), keeps per-item history in bulk review (BR-M17-07), blocks self-approval (BR-M02-06) and never runs on invented limits (BR-M17-14). Which further types are 1B, and whether the generic queue itself moves to 1B (option b: T-1A.14-M17-06 re-staged per D-213), is REQUIRES_DECISION (D-192); deadline, escalation and recurrence values are D-179 / D-185 and threshold values D-024.
- **Files/components:** `backend/automation/` (ApprovalService and ThresholdService routing for the 1B types, deadline job, recurrence review), `backend/reporting/` (approval-ageing report definition), `frontend/workspace/` P-E14 #approvals and the P-E13 report card only if D-004 decides custom UI (else native configuration in `backend/`), unit tests next to the code, cross-module cases in `tests/acceptance/` (finer structure per D-001/D-003).
- **Database impact:** No new entity or migration: the approval_type values payout_account_change, vendor_content and account_reinstatement already exist in E-approval_request (03 §2.15.6, DB-G0). Adds E-approval_threshold routing rows for the 1B types (approver_role_id, above_limit_role_id, second_approver_required, decision_deadline) as an S-05 extension loaded only with decided values (D-024; deadlines D-179, D-185; TS-DB-05); recurrence threshold and deadline settings as E-configuration_version keys; approval ageing reads the (state, approver_role_id, deadline_at) index of E-approval_request.
- **API impact:** No new IDs. Extends API-M17-01 (type filter and rows for vendor_content, payout-account and the other D-192 1B types; overdue/escalated ageing), API-M17-02 (1B subject snapshots and diff links), API-M17-03 and API-M17-04 (authority, SoD and maker-checker checks for the 1B types) and API-M17-07 `log_callback` (payout-account call-back); adds the approval-ageing report key to API-M18-01 and API-M18-02 (definition versions via API-M18-17, API-M18-18). Consumes API-M17-18, API-M24-02 (deadline/recurrence settings), API-M17-19 (threshold change proposed by a policy review) and API-M18-12 (approvals_waiting).
- **Frontend impact:** P-E14 #approvals and m-approve extended: 1B types in the type filter and rows (vendor content, payout account), 'Log call-back' on payout-account changes, 'Cannot self-approve' lock, overdue/escalated view with ageing (04c §7.7); P-E13 catalogue card and viewer 'Approval ageing' (dimensions type, assignee, due time, value; link to P-E14 #approvals; 04c §6.2); P-E01 'Approvals waiting on you' shows the 1B types through API-M18-12 without new UI. All subject to D-004.
- **Backend impact:** M17 ApprovalService / ThresholdService (05 §5.17; 11 §4.2, §4.3): payout_account_change — vendor maker ≠ vendor checker, then finance maker-checker after a logged call-back, owner controlled approval (07 §8 SoD-3, §9; BR-M14-09; D-068); vendor_content — designated reviewer only (D-081; BR-M14-05, BR-M14-12), finance tax review if required; vendor account_reinstatement — owner approval (API-M14-51 202 APPROVAL_REQUIRED). Vendor application decisions stay on their own records (API-M14-50), not approval requests (11 §4.2 note). Approval-deadline job extended to the 1B types: escalate once to the alternate, raise expired_approval, list in the owner digest (A19), never auto-approve (BR-M17-12; 11 §4.3). Recurring-approval review per BR-M17-13; M18 ReportService approval-ageing definition (BR-M18-01, BR-M18-04, BR-M18-10).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-UNIT-10 (threshold × role × delegation routing, deadlines and single escalation for each 1B type); TS-PERM-08 (08.1 self-approval, payout maker ≠ checker SoD-3), TS-PERM-09 (09.3 stale expected_version), TS-PERM-14 (14.1 reviewer without D-081 designation), TS-PERM-07 (07.2 payout change never delegable); TS-SVC-11 (approval deadlines, time travel); TS-VEN-02 and TS-VEN-09 re-run for the vendor-content and payout flows; TS-ERP-19 for the approval-ageing definition; TS-API-01 for the extended endpoints; T12 and T13 (review required, no silent live overwrite) and T31 (only true exceptions reach the owner).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. Every approval type that D-192 assigns to 1B is routed with approver role, alternate approver, deadline and escalation rule stored on E-approval_request; no 1B type is routable before D-192 is DECIDED and its threshold row is active (placeholder values never active — BR-M17-14, TS-ADM-03).
   2. A payout_account_change can be approved through API-M17-03 only after the vendor-side checker (API-M14-69) and a logged finance call-back (API-M17-07 log_callback); a user acting as both maker and checker receives 403 SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED (TS-PERM-08.1); a delegate cannot decide it (TS-PERM-07.2).
   3. A vendor_content decision by a reviewer without the D-081 designation returns 403 AUTHORITY_EXCEEDED (TS-PERM-14.1); a decision with a stale expected_version returns 409 VERSION_CONFLICT (TS-PERM-09.3); the live listing stays unchanged until approval (T12, T13).
   4. An expired 1B approval escalates exactly once to the named alternate, raises one expired_approval exception, appears in the owner digest and is never auto-approved (TS-SVC-11, TS-UNIT-10).
   5. Bulk decisions on 1B approvals (API-M17-04) keep one decision, reason and history per item (BR-M17-07).
   6. The approval-ageing report (API-M18-02) shows waiting approvals by type, approver, due time and value from a versioned, finance-approved definition, and its counts reconcile with API-M17-01 for the same filters (11 §4.5 completion criterion).
   7. Approvals flagged recurring, and similar approvals reaching the recurrence threshold configured under D-179, are listed for policy/threshold review; each review ends in a threshold change via API-M17-19 (second approver) or a recorded reason to keep the rule — never in standing owner approval (BR-M17-13).
   8. If D-004 = custom, P-E14 #approvals lists the 1B types with type filter, lock badge on own requests and 'Log call-back' for payout changes; P-E13 shows the 'Approval ageing' card for permitted roles only (BR-M18-04).
   9. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

#### T-1B.4-M05-01 · Margin-leakage flag A36 (scheduled rule; finance validates)
- **Status:** NOT_STARTED
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.4 / M05
- **Depends on:** T-1A.14-M17-01, T-1A.5-M05-05
- **Decisions:** —
- **References:** 05 §4 A36; 10 §15.2; BP §12.2 A36
- **Description:** Builds the A36 'Identify margin leakage' rule (BP §12.2, P1B): a scheduled M05 job that evaluates confirmed order lines against the approved pricing policy and flags discounts and fees that take a line or order below the active margin floor or outside discount authority, raising one low_margin_override exception per flagged entity for finance to validate cost and allocation (10 §15.2; 05 §5.5 Jobs 'A36 margin-leakage flag (1B, scheduled)'). The rule only flags: it never changes a price, order, refund or price list and never decides an override (human boundary, BP §12.3; BR-M05-10, BR-M05-20); the gross-margin view it relies on is not a statutory P&L (BR-M18-08). Policy limits are read from the active E-margin_floor / E-discount_authority versions built in T-1A.5-M05-05 (values D-024) and cost from the valuation method (D-135) as configuration, never hard-coded (BR-M24-03); lines without a decided cost basis or active floor are reported as not evaluated, not guessed. This task delivers the rule logic and the technical BP §12.3 fields of A36 (trigger, inputs, preconditions, action, idempotency, failure behaviour, human boundary, disable/rollback); owner, KPI/value, the S-17 record and activation belong to T-1B.4-M17-02, and registry, kill switch and dry run are reused from T-1A.14-M17-01.
- **Files/components:** `backend/pricing/` (A36 scheduled rule, finer structure per D-001/D-002), rule registration with the job runtime in `backend/automation/`, unit and service tests next to the code, cross-module cases in `tests/acceptance/`.
- **Database impact:** No new entity or migration. Reads E-order_line (price versions and allocated discounts), E-price_rule_version, E-margin_floor, E-discount_authority and, where recorded, provider fees on E-settlement_record (only if A10 is enabled, D-064); writes E-exception_case (type low_margin_override, one open case per job + entity) and E-job_attempt; the A36 E-automation_rule record stays proposed/off until the S-17 1B set is loaded by T-1B.4-M17-02.
- **API impact:** None new. Consumes API-M17-09, API-M17-11 (dry run on staging with masked inputs, D-077) and API-M17-10 (stop/resume) for A36; flagged cases are worked through API-M17-05, API-M17-06 and API-M17-07 (resolve with reason).
- **Frontend impact:** None new — A36 appears in P-E14 #rules and d-rule (phase 1B) and its flags in P-E14 #exceptions and, when owner-visible, P-E01 'Needs attention' (screens of T-1A.14-M17-10, T-1A.14-M17-11); the P-E13 gross-margin report is the finance validation view (launch set D-075).
- **Backend impact:** M05 margin-leakage job executed by the M17 JobRunner (retry cap → one exception, A38, BR-M17-11); inputs: order-line price and discount allocations (BR-M05-03, BR-M05-13), margin floor and discount authority (BR-M05-10, BR-M05-20), cost per D-135; output: E-exception_case low_margin_override with entity reference, severity, due time, evidence (price version, discount allocation, floor version, cost basis) and a finance assignee (BR-M17-03; severity and due rules D-138); cost and margin evidence restricted to authorised roles (BR-M18-04; D-197); the rule cannot be enabled without a completed template (BR-M17-01).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-SVC-07 (A36 cannot run without a completed template; stopping it leaves pending work recoverable; the automation actor cannot decide an override); TS-SVC-02 (durable job, retry cap → one exception); TS-SVC-06 (exception fields, one open case per job + entity); TS-ERP-16 (margin-floor override with reason is unaffected by the flag); TS-UNIT-01 margin-floor fixtures reused (thresholds are fixture values, never decision values); TS-PERM-10 (10.3 cost/margin columns hidden from unauthorised roles); dry run on staging per TS-ADM-11.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. On fixture data a scheduled A36 run flags every order line whose discounts or fees take it below the active margin floor or outside discount authority, and flags no line within policy.
   2. Re-running the same period creates no second open exception for the same entity; each flag is one E-exception_case low_margin_override with entity reference, severity, due time, evidence and a finance assignee, closed only with a resolution reason (API-M17-07).
   3. The rule changes no price, order line, refund, price list or approval, and the automation actor cannot decide an approval (TS-SVC-07).
   4. Lines without a decided cost basis (D-135) or without an active margin floor (D-024) are reported as not evaluated in the run evidence; no default cost or limit exists in code.
   5. A failure beyond the retry cap creates exactly one actionable incident (TS-SVC-02); the kill switch stops new runs and leaves pending work recoverable.
   6. A dry run on staging with masked inputs (API-M17-11) produces the expected flags; the rule remains off until T-1B.4-M17-02 activates it.
   7. Cost and margin values in the evidence are visible only to roles permitted under D-197 (TS-PERM-10.3).
   8. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —

- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION

- **References:** 05 §4; 10 §15.2, §15.3; 03 §6 S-17; 16 TS-SVC-07; BP §12.2, §12.3

#### T-1B.4-M14-01 · Supplier-fulfilment pilot: tasks with minimal customer data, confirmation deadline, cannot-fulfil return, label/documents, shipment evidence; P-V03 #tasks (CONDITIONAL; E-supplier_fulfilment_task; API-M14-27…30, API-M14-62…65)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.4 / M14
- **Depends on:** T-1B.1-M14-04, T-1A.11-M12-05, T-1B.1-M14-02
- **Decisions:** D-007, D-008, D-181
- **References:** 09 §5.15; 04c §12.3; 03 §2.12.6; 06 API-M14-27…30; 16 TS-VEN-07; BP §3.2
- **Description:** CONDITIONAL — built only if D-007 approves the supplier-fulfilment pilot and D-008 (seller of record, invoice and warranty responsibility) and D-181 (outcome of an unconfirmed task) are DECIDED; while disabled the pilot endpoints answer FEATURE_DISABLED and P-V03 #tasks is hidden (12 §1.3; TS-ECOM-14 pattern; 04c §12.3 'tab hidden for vendors not in the pilot'). Implements company sale with supplier fulfilment for approved pilot vendors and offers (BP §3.2; 09 §5.15; BR-M14-08, BR-M14-18): staff create a task from a released order line (BR-M10-15) with a confirmation deadline, the vendor sees only minimum customer data (BR-M14-07; BP §11.2), confirms or returns the task by the deadline, downloads the label and the company's invoice/packing slip, and uploads shipment evidence whose serial must match the allocated unit; expiry is processed exactly once and followed by the D-181 outcome. This task migrates E-supplier_fulfilment_task (DB-G9 conditional entity) and builds P-V03 #tasks with m-decline and m-evidence. Not included: vendor accounts, portal shell and suspension effects (T-1B.1-M14-02, T-1B.1-M14-04, T-1B.1-M14-08), dispatch and carrier tracking (T-1A.11-M12-05; API-M12-16, API-M12-17 reused), supplier confirmation of partner-stock lines and the checkout disclosure of supplier-dependent lines (08 §4.16; T-1B.2-M04-03).
- **Files/components:** `backend/vendors/` (SupplierFulfilmentTaskService, deadline job), DB-G9 conditional migration in `backend/`, `frontend/vendor-portal/` (P-V03 #tasks, m-decline, m-evidence, P-V01 pilot action item), staff UI in `frontend/workspace/` only if D-004 decides a custom view (no mockup screen), tests in `backend/vendors/` and `tests/acceptance/` (finer structure per D-001/D-101).
- **Database impact:** Migrates E-supplier_fulfilment_task (03 §2.12.6; DB-G9, CONDITIONAL): supplier_id, order_line_id/quantity, state {assigned, confirmed, declined, expired, shipped, delivered, cancelled}, confirmation_deadline, confirmed_at/decline_reason, shared_customer_data (minimum PD1), shipment_evidence, fulfilment_id; index (supplier_id, state, confirmation_deadline); adds the deferred nullable reference supplier_confirmation.supplier_fulfilment_task_id only if E-supplier_confirmation exists (DB-G7 deferred reference; T-1B.2-M04-03). Uses E-offer (fulfilment_model supplier_fulfilment), E-supplier (supply_models), E-fulfilment, E-shipment_event, E-invoice_reference, E-attachment, E-exception_case; retention class RC-order (D-036).
- **API impact:** Implements API-M14-27, API-M14-28, API-M14-29, API-M14-30 and API-M14-62 (vendor, key vendor.fulfilment_task, own organisation only) and API-M14-63, API-M14-64, API-M14-65 (staff, key fulfilment_task.manage); errors 409 TASK_EXPIRED after the deadline and 409 NOT_READY for documents before confirmation. Consumes API-M22-01 (evidence photos), API-M12-16 and API-M12-17 (carrier tracking).
- **Frontend impact:** P-V03 #tasks (open / shipped / expired segments; task cards with countdown, item, order reference, masked phone and PIN; 'Confirm — can ship today', 'Can't fulfil' → m-decline, 'Label & invoice', 'Upload shipment evidence' → m-evidence, 'View evidence', 'Add explanation' on expired tasks; 04c §12.3); P-V01 pilot action item (09 §5.15). Staff list and actions have no mockup screen — placement in P-E02 or P-E11 is REQUIRES_DECISION (D-004).
- **Backend impact:** M14 SupplierFulfilmentTaskService (BR-M14-06, BR-M14-07, BR-M14-08, BR-M14-18); release eligibility BR-M10-15; deadline job expires each task exactly once and raises an E-exception_case for the D-181 outcome (reallocate from company stock, cancel and refund the line, or hold — recorded through API-M14-65) with M10/M06/M11; label per D-013 and invoice/packing slip in the company's name per D-008 through M19 templates (A12; D-055); shipment evidence → E-shipment_event and customer tracking (M12; BR-M12-08); customer data hidden from the vendor after reassignment or closure; confirmation time and dispatch feed vendor performance (09 §5.19); pilot enablement per vendor/offer behind a feature flag (BR-M01-05; rollout D-215).
- **Testing requirements:** TS-VEN-07 (confirmation deadline, expiry returns the task, shipment evidence required, minimal customer data); TS-PERM-02 (02.4: another vendor's task id → 404; T11) and TS-PERM-04 (04.5 applicants and non-pilot vendors refused); TS-API-01 for API-M14-27…API-M14-30 and API-M14-62…API-M14-65; TS-ECOM-14 pattern (disabled → FEATURE_DISABLED, tab hidden); deadline expiry exactly once with time travel (TS-SVC-11 style); TS-FE-04 for the portal tab; decline/expiry path proven end to end with the D-181 customer outcome including refund (BP §3.2 'after confirmation and refund rules are proven').
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. With the pilot disabled, API-M14-27…API-M14-30 and API-M14-62…API-M14-65 answer FEATURE_DISABLED and P-V03 #tasks is not shown; with it enabled, only vendors approved for model supplier_fulfilment and offers with fulfilment_model supplier_fulfilment receive tasks.
   2. Vendor payloads (API-M14-27, API-M14-62) never contain more than name, city, masked phone and masked PIN; another vendor's task id returns 404 (T11).
   3. Confirm or decline after the confirmation deadline returns 409 TASK_EXPIRED; the deadline job moves each unanswered task to expired exactly once and the D-181 outcome is recorded through API-M14-65 with an audit event.
   4. Evidence (API-M14-30) requires AWB, packed weight, handover time and the declaration; a serial that does not match the allocated unit is rejected; accepted evidence sets the task to shipped and updates customer tracking.
   5. Documents (API-M14-29) are issued in the company's name per D-008 and are unavailable before confirmation (409 NOT_READY).
   6. After reassignment or closure the vendor can no longer read that task's customer data.
   7. Pilot UAT with one vendor on the D-007 scope proves the decline/expiry path end to end, including the customer outcome decided under D-181 (09 §5.15 completion criteria).
   8. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.

#### T-1B.4-M17-03 · Process-improvement measurement vs the Phase 0 baseline: owner touches, touch time, exceptions resolved at staff level, automation value (BP §12.4)
- **Status:** REQUIRES_DECISION
- **Stage / Module:** 1B.4 / M17
- **Depends on:** T-1A.14-M17-03, T-1A.15-M18-02, T-0-M17-02
- **Decisions:** D-193, D-190
- **References:** BP §4, §12.4, §5.1 (1B gate); 10 §15.4; 11 §1.3; 16 §12
- **Description:** Measures process improvement for the 1B exit gate against the Phase 0 baseline recorded by T-0-M17-02 (kept in `plan/phase0/` per D-210), with the same definitions, denominators, segmentation and exclusions (BP §4: consistent denominators, exclude test traffic and duplicate events, segment consumer/dealer, new/refurbished, branch/online; BR-M18-07). Required measures (16 §12 1B row; 11 §1.3): routine cases requiring owner action / total routine cases (K1), staff touch time per accepted order (K2, time study), exceptions resolved at staff/manager level (K8) and reliable automation — successful runs, retries, failures and hours saved by the BP §12.4 formula without counting overlapping automations twice (K11; 10 §15.4); other BP §4 measures only where D-190 selects them. System values come from existing data (API-M18-12 success_measures and owner_touches, API-M18-16 automation KPIs, API-M17-08 and API-M17-15 run data, launch reports of T-1A.15-M18-02); where D-190 has not yet defined K1, K8 or K11, their versioned definitions are added here (BR-M18-10). Time-study inputs (minutes saved per case, exception-handling hours, loaded hourly cost, whether ₹ values are shown) are REQUIRES_DECISION (D-193), and production verification transactions are excluded per D-209. The output is a measurement report vs baseline used as evidence by T-1B.5-M17-01; no improvement target is invented (BP §4 'illustrative target to negotiate').
- **Files/components:** `backend/reporting/` (measure definitions, only if added), `backend/automation/` (value-estimate inputs on the rule records), tests next to the code; measurement report and time-study records: storage location not specified in the plan (the baseline is in `plan/phase0/` per D-210, UAT evidence index in `tests/uat/`) — to be agreed with the owner and noted in `plan/STATE.md`.
- **Database impact:** No schema change. Reads E-approval_request (decisions by R-owner), E-exception_case (resolved_by role), E-job_attempt, E-sales_order and E-order_line (denominators); updates E-automation_rule.value_estimate with the decided time-study inputs (D-193); new report-definition versions only if K1, K8 or K11 are not yet defined (BR-M18-10).
- **API impact:** None new. Consumes API-M18-12 (success_measures, owner_touches), API-M18-16 (automation KPIs), API-M18-02 (automation health and other launch reports), API-M17-08 and API-M17-15 (runs); API-M18-17 and API-M18-18 (definition versions with finance approval) only if definitions are added.
- **Frontend impact:** None new — P-E01 KPI tiles and automation panel, P-E14 header 'Staff time saved (est.)' and value chart show the measured values; values stay labelled as estimates until D-193 is DECIDED.
- **Backend impact:** M18 DashboardService / ReportService measure definitions (BR-M18-02, BR-M18-07, BR-M18-10); hours_saved = monthly_cases × minutes_saved_per_case ÷ 60 − monthly_exception_handling_hours and net_monthly_value per BP §12.4 (10 §15.4), overlapping automations counted once; K2 and minutes saved per case from a time study using the BP §26.9 observation form.
- **Testing requirements:** TS-ERP-19 (definitions, denominators and exclusions reconcile with sample transactions); TS-UNIT-11 (definition labels and formatting); TS-ADM-10 (P-E01 measures carry definition and freshness); KPI definition tests per D-190 (denominators, exclusion of test and duplicate events; 11 §1.5); one measured week reproduced from raw records.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
   1. K1, K2, K8 and K11 are reported for a stated measurement period with the same definitions, denominators and segmentation as the T-0-M17-02 baseline, each value shown next to its baseline.
   2. Test traffic, duplicate events and production verification transactions (D-209) are excluded, and every system-derived figure reconciles with the underlying records (TS-ERP-19).
   3. Hours saved follow the BP §12.4 formula with exception-handling hours subtracted and no double counting across overlapping automations; inputs come from the time study under D-193, and values without decided inputs are labelled estimates.
   4. No improvement target and no ₹ value is shown unless D-190 / D-193 decide it.
   5. The report, its period, definitions and data sources are recorded (storage location noted in STATE.md) for use by T-1B.5-M17-01.
   6. TASKS.md and STATE.md updated per the continuation protocol.
- **Evidence:** —
